articles.title: CSIR-CCMB team identifies potential new targets to fight Tuberculosis
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge, as treatment requires a combination of antibiotics taken over several months and is becoming increasingly difficult due to the emergence of resistant strains

A team of scientists at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB) has identified critical weaknesses in the bacterium that causes Tuberculosis (TB), a finding that could pave the way for the development of new treatments against one of the world’s deadliest infectious diseases.

The discovery is particularly significant for India, which accounts for nearly a quarter of global TB cases and about a third of drug-resistant infections, according to the World Health Organisation’s Global TB Report 2025 . Drug-resistant TB remains a major public health challenge, as treatment requires a combination of antibiotics taken over several months and is becoming increasingly difficult due to the emergence of resistant strains.

Led by CCMB Director Vinay Kumar Nandicoori, the research team mapped the protein export machinery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), the bacterium responsible for TB. The study sheds light on how the pathogen transports proteins within and outside its cells, a process essential for its growth, survival and ability to cause disease.

The research was carried out by joint first authors Priyadarshini Sanyal and Jagadeeshwari Uppada in collaboration with scientists from the Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Chennai, led by Areejit Samal, and the Translational Health Science and Technology Institute, Faridabad.

Using a combination of computational modelling and laboratory experiments, the researchers identified 92 key components and nearly 200 molecular reactions involved in the bacterium’s protein transport network. These included the general Sec pathway, the Twin-Arginine Translocation (Tat) system and the specialised ESX secretion systems unique to this group of bacteria.

“Protein secretion acts like a delivery system inside the bacterium and is vital for its survival,” said Dr Uppada. The team focused on two major secretion pathways, SecA1 and Tat, employing CRISPR-based gene-silencing technology to reduce their activity. The results were striking: bacterial growth declined sharply both in laboratory cultures and inside immune cells, demonstrating that both pathways are essential for the pathogen’s survival.

Dr Priyadarshini Sanyal said further analysis revealed that disrupting these systems affected the export of more than 100 proteins in the SecA1 pathway and around 140 proteins linked to the Tat system. Researchers also observed structural damage to the bacterial cell membrane, making it unstable and more permeable. Proteins that normally remain inside the bacterium began leaking into the surrounding environment.

Dr Nandicoori said that these changes highlight the close connection between protein secretion and the maintenance of the bacterial cell envelope, a key factor behind TB’s persistence and resistance to treatment. The findings, published in the peer-reviewed journal Molecular & Cellular Proteomics , could help researchers identify new drug targets, although translating the discovery into effective medicines will require several more years of research.

articles.title: How AI is reshaping China’s universities
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: AI disruption and a tightening job market are driving a sweeping change across China’s universities; under the government’s ‘guideline on the reform of higher education institutions’, universities will now be tasked with specific goals, pursuing either research, application-oriented objectives, or skills development

In September 2026, China’s government unveiled an ambitious 10-year plan to reform its universities. Driving the change is an increasingly challenging job market for the country’s close to 13 million college graduates, who are facing the twin disruptions of AI and a slowing economy. Under the plan, dozens of graduate programmes are being disbanded, while universities themselves will be categorised and tasked with either pursuing research, applications or skills development.

A combination of factors, some not too dissimilar to the current challenges in India’s own job market, has left policymakers grappling with a tepid job market and a vast number of graduates facing dim job prospects. Top of the list is a mismatch in skills between graduates and what companies are seeking. Depressed economic sentiment has also led companies to cut back on hiring, with the prolonged structural slowdown in the real estate market dragging down growth. AI is the third disruptive force, changing rapidly how the marketplace views and values skills.

Top of the list is a mismatch in skills between graduates and what companies are seeking. Depressed economic sentiment has also led companies to cut back on hiring, with the prolonged structural slowdown in the real estate market dragging down growth. AI is the third disruptive force, changing rapidly how the marketplace views and values skills.

articles.title: France blames Iran for cyberattack on supermarket fridges

fullParagraphs: The October 12 attack sent refrigerator temperatures soaring, affecting about 700 of France’s supermarkets

France on Monday blamed Iran for last month's massive cyberattack on supermarket fridges , summoned the Iranian ambassador and said it would seek European sanctions against those responsible for the attack.

The October 12 attack sent refrigerator temperatures soaring, affecting about 700 of the country's 10,000 supermarkets. In a statement Monday, prosecutors in Paris said they found that Iran's paramilitary Revolutionary Guard was behind the large-scale cyberattack.

The French Foreign Ministry condemned the attack “in the strongest possible terms,” and French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot, speaking on the sidelines of G7 talks in Paris, said the Iranian ambassador was being summoned to “strongly protest against this extremely serious act.”

“This is an attack of unprecedented scale and aggressiveness,” Mr. Barrot said. “It is the first large-scale cyberattack aimed at sabotage on French soil, and it represents a major threat to our national interests and the security of the French people. That is why it will not go unanswered.”
“We will impose sanctions at the European level against all those responsible for this attack,” he added, vowing to take “any other measures needed” to respond to it and deter future attacks.

Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said in a statement that a formal judicial investigation was opened Monday into suspected organised cybercrime with the aggravating circumstance of “having been committed to serve the interests of a foreign power — in this case, Iran."

The investigation targets Shahid Kaveh, the leader of an Iranian group described as a “cyber unit” affiliated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, as well as his two deputies and any other individuals who might be identified in connection with the case.

Investigators found that the attackers had used Farsi and IP addresses linked to devices located in Iran, Mr. Beccuau said. The Paris prosecutor's office is seeking international arrest warrants, she said.

In the early hours of October 12, attackers remotely took control of refrigeration systems in hundreds of supermarkets and independent stores across France. Temperatures reached 50 degrees Celsius for about six hours, forcing stores to discard fresh and frozen goods. The Intermarche supermarket chain reported losses of “tens of millions of euros” in a single day.

articles.title: Judge sets summer 2028 trial for the man accused of killing Charlie Kirk
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Utah District Judge Graf allocated 105 days for the trial, beginning with jury selection on June 21, 2028
The man accused of assassinating conservative activist Charlie Kirk will stand trial in the summer of 2028, a Utah judge ruled on Monday (November 9, 2026).

Attorneys for defendant Tyler Robinson, 23, proposed a trial starting in 2029. But District Judge Tony Graf faced pressure from Kirk's family and supporters , including President Donald Trump, to speed up court proceedings that already have lasted more than a year.

Robinson has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder in the killing of Kirk, 31, as the activist spoke to several thousand people at Utah Valley University on September 10, 2025 . Robinson could face the death penalty if convicted.

District Judge Graf allocated 105 days for the trial, beginning with jury selection on June 21, 2028. He said the dates balance Robinson's right to prepare his defense with the rights of Kirk's widow, Erika Kirk, to a speedy resolution.
Erika Kirk's attorney disagreed with the schedule but said there is no choice but to accept it.

“A trial in the summer of 2028, three years after Charlie's assassination, does not feel very speedy to the Kirk family,” attorney Jeffrey Neiman told the judge. He had argued the trial should start next October.

In a statement after Monday's (November 9, 2026) hearing, the Kirk family characterised District Judge Graf's decision as a “delay” and said, “every additional day without justice prolongs our family's pain.”
Robinson's defense team declined to comment after the hearing.
The defendant turned himself in a day after the shooting. His lawyers have not offered alternative theories for Kirk's death.
Prosecutors had said they could be ready for trial by October 2027. Rather than hold the proceedings during the Thanksgiving and Christmas holidays, they proposed a January 2028 start date.

📰 Judge sets summer 2028 trial for the man accused of killing Charlie Kirk

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

Utah District Judge Graf allocated 105 days for the trial, beginning with jury selection on June 21, 2028

The man accused of assassinating conservative activist Charlie Kirk will stand trial in the summer of 2028, a Utah judge ruled on Monday (November 9, 2026).

Attorneys for defendant Tyler Robinson, 23, proposed a trial starting in 2029. But District Judge Tony Graf faced pressure from Kirk's family and supporters , including President Donald Trump, to speed up court proceedings that already have lasted more than a year.

Robinson has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder in the killing of Kirk, 31, as the activist spoke to several thousand people at Utah Valley University on September 10, 2025 . Robinson could face the death penalty if convicted.

District Judge Graf allocated 105 days for the trial, beginning with jury selection on June 21, 2028. He said the dates balance Robinson's right to prepare his defense with the rights of Kirk's widow, Erika Kirk, to a speedy resolution.

Erika Kirk's attorney disagreed with the schedule but said there is no choice but to accept it.

“A trial in the summer of 2028, three years after Charlie's assassination, does not feel very speedy to the Kirk family,” attorney Jeffrey Neiman told the judge. He had argued the trial should start next October.

In a statement after Monday's (November 9, 2026) hearing, the Kirk family characterised District Judge Graf's decision as a “delay” and said, “every additional day without justice prolongs our family's pain.”

Robinson's defense team declined to comment after the hearing.

The defendant turned himself in a day after the shooting. His lawyers have not offered alternative theories for Kirk's death.

Prosecutors had said they could be ready for trial by October 2027. Rather than hold the proceedings during the Thanksgiving and Christmas holidays, they proposed a January 2028 start date.

1. Core Context & Background: Utah District Judge Graf allocated 105 days for the trial, beginning with jury selection on June 21, 2028

articles.title: Anthropic launches Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 ahead of IPO
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The new models, Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, can perform up to 30 percent faster than previous versions, per Anthropic
Anthropic announced on Monday that it would release updated versions of two of its most powerful artificial intelligence (AI) models as the company prepares for a highly anticipated IPO this month.
The new models, Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, can perform up to 30 percent faster than previous versions, particularly on complex tasks such as coding, while costing 20 percent less, the company said.
Both are built on the same underlying model. Fable 5.2 has safeguards that block most cybersecurity and biology tasks, which lets Anthropic offer it to all users.
Mythos 5.2 has fewer of those restrictions and is available only to vetted organisations working in cybersecurity or biomedical research.
The first versions of Fable and Mythos were released under a cloud of controversy.

Both models were pulled days after their June launch, when the US Commerce Department, citing national security concerns, ordered Anthropic to bar access by foreign nationals. The controls were lifted weeks later.

The latest versions come as Anthropic is aiming to hold its initial public offering the week of November 16, when it is expected to raise up to $100 billion, which would make it the largest IPO on record.
The San Francisco-based lab's Wall Street debut is expected to fetch a valuation exceeding $1 trillion, though estimates have fallen in recent weeks from a high of $2 trillion.
The stock market debut is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last.
Growth has been staggering at the company. Anthropic's revenue reached $17 billion in the third quarter, up from just $1.4 billion a year earlier, a securities filing showed earlier this month.

articles.title: Google’s controversial Search and AI policy for schools | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A child’s thwarted suicide attempt in the U.S. has put the spotlight on the risks of Google’s Gemini AI and the company’s controversial decision to package Search and AI features together for students

The story so far: Google on November 3, 2026, outlined its approach to deploying AI across classrooms in the U.S. The company noted that access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search would be “entirely off for K-12 student accounts” until school administrators turned them on.

While this sounds benign, a New York Times report on the search giant turning off Search for schools that reject AI has ignited anger across the U.S., after Google’s vice president of education, Chris Phillips, confirmed that schools banning AI would not have access to Search. Google’s new ‘pick both or nothing’ policy on Search and AI features for school students has sparked a debate over its AI safety policies for children.

articles.title: El Nino Watch: the impacts around the world this week
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Experts say it could help make 2027 the hottest year on record

An exceptionally strong El Nino is driving weather disruptions around the globe, stoking food security fears and increasing the chances that 2026 will be the second-hottest year on record, experts say.
Here is how the climate phenomenon has been playing out around the world in the last week.

The world is on track for 2026 to be the second-hottest year on record, with the El Nino weather pattern turbocharging human-driven global warming, the European Union’s climate monitor said on Friday (November 6, 2026).

“October has continued the pattern of remarkable global warmth, with record global and surface ocean temperatures,” said Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for climate at the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, which operates the Copernicus monitor.
“An exceptionally strong El Nino is adding further heat to a climate already warmed by human activities,” she said.

The warming phase of a natural climate cycle, El Nino temporarily raises sea temperatures in the tropical Pacific, triggering changes in weather that can increase the risk of drought and flooding, and exacerbate man-made global warming.
Experts say it could help make 2027 the hottest year on record.
Peru declared a state of emergency across much of the country on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), given the “imminent danger” posed by El Nino-linked flooding, authorities said.
It followed Bolivia’s decision to announce a national state of emergency over the weather pattern’s effects.
El Nino cycles can bring heavy rain to Latin America, and downpours have already inundated parts of Peru’s northern Tumbes and Piura regions.

articles.title: DMK MP Jagathrakshakan, son Sundeep Anand of TVK move Madras High Court over ₹161.12-crore FEMA case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: They have challenged seizure of properties worth ₹45.34 crore in India in connection with a company incorporated in Singapore

DMK Lok Sabha member S. Jagathrakshakan, his son J. Sundeep Anand of the TVK, and his daughter J. Sri Nisha have approached the Madras High Court against the seizure of properties worth ₹45.34 crore by the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) for an alleged contravention to the tune of ₹161.12 crore under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) of 1999.

The First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan admitted the individual civil appeals filed by the three family members and ordered notice to the ED. The appellants had challenged an order passed by a FEMA appellate tribunal, located in New Delhi, on May 21, 2026, partly confirming a seizure order issued by the central agency.

The issue dates back to the incorporation of Silver Park International Pte. Limited in Singapore on June 15, 2017. The Memorandum of Articles disclosed that Mr. Jagathrakshakan held 70 lakh equity shares, his son Mr. Anand held 20 lakh shares, and another individual named V.T. Thiagarajan had 10 lakh shares with a nominal value of 1 Singapore dollar (SGD) each.

The ED had initiated the inquiry under FEMA after the Member of Parliament disclosed, in his election affidavit, of having been a director of Silver Park International Pte. Limited between June 15, 2017, and September 15, 2018. The initial inquiries revealed that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had no information whatsoever with respect to Silver Park of Singapore.

Hence, the ED summoned the MP, representing the Arakkonam constituency, for inquiry and learnt that he had gifted 45 lakh shares to his wife Anusuya (since dead), 22.50 lakh shares to his daughter, and 2.5 lakh shares to his son on September 15, 2018. Ms. Anusuya, in turn, had transferred all her shares equally to their son and daughter for a consideration of one SGD each on May 2, 2019.

However, all the family members told the ED that they did not obtain RBI permission either for subscribing to the shares, gifting them, or transferring them, since they believed that such permission was required only when the money gets paid, and not before that. The ED rejected their contention and arrived at a conclusion that the family members had contravened Section 4 of FEMA.

The central agency on September 11, 2020, passed an order seizing the family’s immovable properties worth ₹89.17 crore in India for the alleged contravention of ₹161.12 crore under FEMA. Nevertheless, the Commissioner of Customs, in his capacity as the competent authority under FEMA, set aside the seizure order in toto on February 3, 2021.

When the competent authority’s order was taken on appeal to the appellate tribunal, the latter highlighted that the financial statement of Silver Park disclosed that the share capital of the company stood at 1 crore SGD through the issuance of shares.

“Even if the value of 1 SGD per share is regarded as nominal value, it cannot be stated that the shares were of zero value,” the tribunal said and disagreed with the conclusion arrived at by the competent authority that the appellants held no share of any value in Singapore and therefore, the property seizure order was liable to be set aside.

The tribunal had also said: “Without acquisition and holding on to the subscription of shares, the allotees could not have been appointed as Directors of the Company. It is also on record that the subscription of shares was transferred as gift, which in itself demonstrates value inherent in the subscription of shares.”

📰 DMK MP Jagathrakshakan, son Sundeep Anand of TVK move Madras High Court over ₹161.12-crore FEMA case

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

They have challenged seizure of properties worth ₹45.34 crore in India in connection with a company incorporated in Singapore

DMK Lok Sabha member S. Jagathrakshakan, his son J. Sundeep Anand of the TVK, and his daughter J. Sri Nisha have approached the Madras High Court against the seizure of properties worth ₹45.34 crore by the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) for an alleged contravention to the tune of ₹161.12 crore under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) of 1999.

The First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan admitted the individual civil appeals filed by the three family members and ordered notice to the ED. The appellants had challenged an order passed by a FEMA appellate tribunal, located in New Delhi, on May 21, 2026, partly confirming a seizure order issued by the central agency.

The issue dates back to the incorporation of Silver Park International Pte. Limited in Singapore on June 15, 2017. The Memorandum of Articles disclosed that Mr. Jagathrakshakan held 70 lakh equity shares, his son Mr. Anand held 20 lakh shares, and another individual named V.T. Thiagarajan had 10 lakh shares with a nominal value of 1 Singapore dollar (SGD) each.

The ED had initiated the inquiry under FEMA after the Member of Parliament disclosed, in his election affidavit, of having been a director of Silver Park International Pte. Limited between June 15, 2017, and September 15, 2018. The initial inquiries revealed that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had no information whatsoever with respect to Silver Park of Singapore.

Hence, the ED summoned the MP, representing the Arakkonam constituency, for inquiry and learnt that he had gifted 45 lakh shares to his wife Anusuya (since dead), 22.50 lakh shares to his daughter, and 2.5 lakh shares to his son on September 15, 2018. Ms. Anusuya, in turn, had transferred all her shares equally to their son and daughter for a consideration of one SGD each on May 2, 2019.

However, all the family members told the ED that they did not obtain RBI permission either for subscribing to the shares, gifting them, or transferring them, since they believed that such permission was required only when the money gets paid, and not before that. The ED rejected their contention and arrived at a conclusion that the family members had contravened Section 4 of FEMA.

The central agency on September 11, 2020, passed an order seizing the family’s immovable properties worth ₹89.17 crore in India for the alleged contravention of ₹161.12 crore under FEMA. Nevertheless, the Commissioner of Customs, in his capacity as the competent authority under FEMA, set aside the seizure order in toto on February 3, 2021.

When the competent authority’s order was taken on appeal to the appellate tribunal, the latter highlighted that the financial statement of Silver Park disclosed that the share capital of the company stood at 1 crore SGD through the issuance of shares.

“Even if the value of 1 SGD per share is regarded as nominal value, it cannot be stated that the shares were of zero value,” the tribunal said and disagreed with the conclusion arrived at by the competent authority that the appellants held no share of any value in Singapore and therefore, the property seizure order was liable to be set aside.

The tribunal had also said: “Without acquisition and holding on to the subscription of shares, the allotees could not have been appointed as Directors of the Company. It is also on record that the subscription of shares was transferred as gift, which in itself demonstrates value inherent in the subscription of shares.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The tribunal had also said: “Without acquisition and holding on to the subscription of shares, the allotees could not have been appointed as Directors of the Company. It is also on record that the subscription of shares was transferred as gift, which in itself demonstrates value inherent in the subscription of shares.”

articles.title: Popular cinematographer Shaji Kumar passes away
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Shaji Kumar dies in Kochi at 57 after cardiac failure
Noted cinematographer Shaji Kumar, 57, who cranked the camera for popular movies including Thudarum and P ulimurugan, died in Kochi on early Tuesday (November 10, 2026) morning.
The death occurred around 12.36 a.m. following cardiac failure, according to private hospital authorities in Kochi.

Representatives of the Film Employees Federation of Kerala (FEFKA) Directors’ Union said that he experienced uneasiness at his place of stay in Alappuzha after returning from the location of a new movie featuring actor Dileep on Saturday night (November 7, 2026). He was rushed to a nearby hospital and later shifted to Kochi. His condition worsened around Monday midnight (November 8, 2026).
A native of Thiruvananthapuram, he has been staying in Perumbavoor, Ernakulam for a long time. He is survived by his wife, Smitha, and children, Aryan and Sooryan, they said.
Popular among filmmakers for his excellence in capturing mass action scenes, he had worked in nearly 50 movies in a career spanning over two decades. He had worked with leading movie directors.

The slick action scenes in movies like Pulimurugan , Naran , Odiyan, to name a few, had won the appreciation of the movie buffs. He was a much sought-after technician among the senior and new crop of filmmakers for his discipline and swift execution of even tough scenes.

The year 2025 was special for him after his collaboration with director Tharun Moorthy in Thudarum wove magic on screen and at the box office. The blockbuster movie raised his graph again, and the young filmmaker had no second choice but to fill the seat of cinematographer for his latest venture, Athimanoharam, featuring actor Mohanlal in the lead role. He was behind the camera for the forthcoming movie Ottakomban, featuring actor Suresh Gopi in lead role.

Some of his popular movies included Uthaman (2001), Valkannadi, Pakalpooram (2002), Ammakilikoodu, Pattanathil Sundaran (2003), Sathyam, Vesham (2004), Athbhuthadweep (2005), Mahasamudhram (2006), Nasrani (2007), Robinhood, Red Chillies (2009), Pokkiriraja (2010), Seniors, Ponnar Shankar (2011), The King and the Commissioner, Mallu Singh (2012), Ramaleela (2017), Madhura Raja (2019), Pathonpatham Nootandu (2022), Once Upon a Time in Kochi (2024).

articles.title: Five injured as bus rams into two cars at Wadala traffic signal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police moved the damaged vehicles to the roadside to restore normal flow of traffic at the junction

Five persons were injured, including one critically, after a bus operated by a private contractor of the Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) undertaking allegedly lost control and rammed into two cars waiting at a traffic signal near Lodha Junction in Wadala on Monday (November 9, 2026) night.

The accident occurred around 8:30 p.m. near the Bhakti Park signal in New Cuffe Parade when a BEST bus, an Ertiga and a Creta were stationary at the signal. According to preliminary information, another bus approaching from behind collided with the Creta, triggering a chain collision involving both cars and the stationary BEST bus.

According to a BEST incident report, the stationary bus, bearing registration number MH01 CR 3014, was operating on route 6/2 LTD from Colaba Depot towards Gavangaon. The bus that allegedly caused the accident, bearing registration number MH43 CE 1612, was operated by private contractor Chalo.
The impact severely damaged both cars, pushing one of them underneath the rear portion of the stationary BEST bus. Several occupants were trapped inside the damaged vehicles.

Police personnel rushed to the spot after receiving information about the accident and carried out rescue operations. A crane was deployed to remove the damaged vehicles and clear the road for traffic.
According to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), five injured persons were admitted to the civic-run Lokmanya Tilak Municipal General Hospital in Sion.
The injured were identified as Shivani Pal (65), Pranish Pal (74), Madhupurn Pal (28), Hasharat Shaikh (34) and Balaji Pandurang Jadhav (35).

According to an update received from the hospital’s Chief Medical Officer at 10:41 p.m., Shivani, Pranish and Madhupurn were in stable condition, while Shaikh was critical. Details regarding Jadhav’s condition were awaited.
A BEST incident report also stated that a pet dog was injured in the accident. Its condition could not be immediately ascertained.

The vehicles involved in the accident were subsequently moved to the roadside to restore traffic flow. Police were ascertaining the circumstances leading to the collision, and necessary legal action was being initiated.

articles.title: Tool developed to test teachers’ knowledge of inclusive education
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nagaland University researchers say the 50-item achievement test is designed to improve teaching practices for children with learning needs
Researchers at Nagaland University have developed and tested a 50-item achievement test to assess trainee and future teachers' understanding of inclusive education.
They said, “The tool is designed to help identify gaps in teachers’ preparation and improve teaching practices for children with learning needs.”

The study by Gyanendra Nath Tiwari, a professor at the university’s Department of Teacher Education, and research scholar Aseto Iralu Meyase was published in the peer-reviewed International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science.
The study said most available tools focus on teachers’ attitudes or confidence. However, few measure what future teachers know about education—its concepts, practices and policies.

“The new test aims to fill that gap. It can help teacher education institutions spot areas where trainee teachers struggle. For example, if many students find it hard to understand policies for children with special needs, educators can adjust their teaching to include more information and real-life examples,” the study said.

The test was built around the B.Ed. Course 10, titled ‘Creating an Inclusive School’, at Nagaland University. It covers five areas: special needs, education policies and provisions, inclusive classroom practices, building support networks and related concepts.
The questions test thinking levels: from simple recall to applying knowledge, analysing situations and evaluating possible solutions.

“We started with 60 questions. We reviewed them before using them on 42 M.Ed. students at our university’s Kohima Campus. We looked at how difficult each question was, how well it could distinguish strong and weak performers and how consistent the test was overall,” Prof. Tiwari said.

“Based on our analysis, we removed 10 questions that did not work well. This left us with a 50-item test. The internal consistency of the test, measured by Cronbach’s alpha, went up from 0.641 to 0.727, which means the test is more reliable now,” Mr. Meyase said.
The results showed that questions asking students to apply or analyse knowledge performed better.

articles.title: Social activist Sanjit Bunker Roy dies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Roy founded the Social Work and Research Centre, popularly known as Barefoot College, in Tilonia in 1972

Renowned social activist and Barefoot College founder Sanjit Bunker Roy, who spent more than five decades working for rural development and women's empowerment, died at his home in Tilonia in Rajasthan's Ajmer district on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) morning. He was 81.
Mr. Roy breathed his last in the presence of his wife, noted social activist Aruna Roy, and others close to him, people associated with him said in a statement in Jaipur.

"Bunker Roy passed away peacefully at 6.15 a.m. this morning with Aruna and others around him. He went as he wanted to, in his own home in Tilonia, surrounded by some of the countless people who loved and cared for him deeply and passionately," the statement said.
Activist Nikhil Dey said the funeral will take place in Tilonia at 4 p.m.

Mr. Roy founded the Social Work and Research Centre, popularly known as Barefoot College, in Tilonia in 1972. What began in a Rajasthan village went on to become an internationally recognised institution for rural development.
His work was based on the simple belief that villagers, even those without formal education, could acquire technical skills and solve problems in their own communities.

Barefoot College trained rural people in solar energy, water conservation, education, healthcare and livelihood-related activities. Its programmes placed particular importance on involving women in village development.
One of its best-known initiatives trained rural women, including those who had never attended school, to install and maintain solar lighting systems.

The women underwent practical training and returned to their villages to provide electricity to households in remote areas. The programme later expanded beyond India, bringing women from several countries to Tilonia for training.
The institution also worked on rainwater harvesting, rural education, healthcare and traditional crafts.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz LNG traffic hits highest in October since Iran war began
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: October exports ‌were ⁠the highest since February when the war ⁠started and were up from September’s corresponding tally of 23 vessels exiting the strait

The monthly tally of laden liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers exiting the ​Strait of Hormuz reached its highest in October since ‌the U.S.-Iran conflict disrupted shipping this year, vessel ​tracking data showed.

* Last month, ⁠31 LNG tankers went through the key waterway, according to data from S&P Global Energy, of which ‌23 were loaded at Ras Laffan in Qatar and eight at Das Island ‌in the United Arab Emirates.
* October exports ‌were ⁠the highest since February when the war ⁠started and were up from September’s corresponding tally of 23 vessels exiting the strait, the data showed.
* “We are ​looking at UAE ‌back to pre-war transit levels and Qatar at over 30% of pre-war Hormuz transits,” said Eric Yep, a senior principal analyst at ‌S&P Global Energy.
* Kpler’s shiptracking data showed ​42 LNG cargoes were loaded in October, up from 27 in September.

* ⁠The changes come as Ras Laffan’s October loadings reached 35 cargoes, surpassing 2.7 million tons, the ‌highest since the war started, according to Kpler data. Qatar exported nearly 6.2 million tons in February.

* Two of the vessels carrying LNG from Ras Laffan that exited the strait subsequently conducted ship-to-ship (STS) transfers off the coast of ‌Oman’s Sohar anchorage, Kpler data showed. The SC Prestige ​transferred LNG to the BW ENN Crystal Sky, which is now bound for ⁠South Korea.
* The Al Mafyar moved its LNG ⁠to Shandong Redwood and Ejnan, both of which delivered the cargoes to Pakistan.
* ‌Das Island exports held steady at seven loadings in October, flat with September, Kpler ​data showed.

* The Al Mafyar moved its LNG ⁠to Shandong Redwood and Ejnan, both of which delivered the cargoes to Pakistan.

articles.title: Republican Thomas Massie of Kentucky launches bid to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Thomas Massie, who was defeated by a Trump-backed challenger in a primary earlier this year, said Pete Hegseth's actions amounted to high crimes and misdemeanors

Rep Thomas Massie on Monday (November 9, 2026) moved to force a vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, pressing his fellow Republicans to remove one of the Trump administration's most prominent figures following sweeping election losses blamed in part on fallout from the war in Iran.

Mr. Massie, a Kentucky Republican, read the impeachment resolution from the House floor just hours after it opened for the first day of sessions after the midterms. It largely focuses on the war in Iran but also includes references to Hegseth's role in carrying out military actions in Yemen and Venezuela.
The Congressman, who was defeated by a Trump-backed challenger in a primary earlier this year, said Mr. Hegseth's actions amounted to “high crimes and misdemeanors.”
Mr. Hegseth, he said, “knowingly executed and implemented unlawful orders” and “remains a threat to the Constitution.”
President Donald Trump lashed out at Massie personally just hours after the Congressman read the resolution, calling him a “loser” who “has a lot of hatred in his heart.”

A vote in the House could come by mid-week, but next steps are highly uncertain. House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries supports the measure. If most Democrats follow him, Mr. Massie would only need support from a few Republicans to impeach Hegseth.

If the House votes to impeach, it would fall to to the Senate to either dismiss the charges or hold a trial. Republicans remain in the majority in both chambers, until the new Congress convenes in January with Democrats in control.
Sen Chuck Schumer, the Democratic leader, endorsed the impeachment push. "Hegseth must stand trial before the Senate," he said.

Republican leaders, who are eager to use their final weeks in power executing their own agenda, expressed frustration at the move. House Speaker Mike Johnson, who has tried to prevent the vote, said impeachment “in the middle of hostilities abroad would be a terrible, terrible look, a terrible thing for our allies and our enemies to see that.”
Senate Majority Leader John Thune said he wasn't sure why the vote was being held now.

articles.title: Accused Ecuadorian thief agrees to plead guilty in largest U.S. jewelry heist
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The stolen collection of fine gold, ​diamonds, rubies, emeralds and luxury watches was valued at approximately $100 million, marking the largest U.S. jewelry heist on record, according ⁠to the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Los Angeles

An Ecuadorian man has agreed to plead guilty to a federal robbery charge for his ​role in the theft of roughly $100 million worth of jewelry from an armoured truck ‌five years ago in California, considered the largest such heist ​in U.S. history.

Carlos Victor Mestanza Cercado, 32, an ⁠Ecuadorean national arrested two years ago in Panama during a layover on a flight from Guatemala to his home country, was one of seven men indicted on ‌charges of robbing a Brink’s truck at a highway rest stop north of Los Angeles on July 11, ‌2022.

The armoured vehicle was robbed while transporting 73 sacks of precious gems and fine jewellery from a major exhibition in the San Francisco Bay Area to a storage facility hundreds of miles south, ahead of another show scheduled in Pasadena.

Mestanza and his co-defendants, who had followed ​the jewellery shipment in multiple vehicles ‌for 300 miles (480 km) while coordinating by cellphone, broke through the locks of the armoured truck while it was parked at a rural Kern County rest stop and got away with 24 bags ‌of treasure, authorities said.

The stolen collection of fine gold, ​diamonds, rubies, emeralds and luxury watches was valued at approximately $100 million, marking the largest U.S. jewelry heist on record, according ⁠to the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Los Angeles.

Mestanza signed an agreement last week to plead guilty to a single count of interference with ‌commerce by robbery, a felony punishable by up to 20 years in prison, in return for prosecutors dropping several other charges he faced, according to court documents filed on Monday (November 9, 2026).
He is expected to formally enter his guilty plea at a hearing set for November 19. The 22-page plea deal states he is likely to face immediate deportation ‌once his sentence is served.
In addition to the jewelry heist, Mestanza admitted to taking part ​with his co-defendants in the highway robberies of electronics being shipped by several trucks in March 2022.

Three of ⁠Mestanza’s co-defendants are scheduled for trial in March 2027 in federal court in ⁠Los Angeles, while two others remain at large and a seventh accused member of their gang has been deported, according ‌to the Los Angeles City News Service.
It was not clear from court documents in the case whether any of the stolen ​jewelry from the Brink’s heist was ever recovered.

The country is well on track to surpass the record $1.2 trillion hit last year, when the $1 trillion mark was reached in November.
However, the export boom has fuelled tensions with several key trading partners, who worry that floods of lower-cost Chinese goods are crowding out local competition.

articles.title: UFC chief Dana White declines Donald Trump's White House job offer
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Dana White visited the White House on November 9, and Donald Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room

Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White turned down President Donald Trump's -- apparently jovial -- offer of a job as press secretary in a surprise appearance at the White House on Monday (November 9, 2026).

Mr. Trump stunned the world by saying on social media on Saturday (November 7) that he had asked Mr. White to take on the high-profile post -- but a day later the 80-year-old president said he was "only kidding."
The 57-year-old cage fighting boss visited the White House on Monday (November 9), and Mr. Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room.
"So let me ask you the big question. Would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America? Or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC? Huh?" Mr. Trump said.
"Thank you for the offer, sir -- for the offer, I have no, no -- I do not want to be in politics," Mr. White replied.
Trump smiled and headed out of the room, saying: "I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everybody."

The press secretary's post has been been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week in the post. Her combative predecessor Karoline Leavitt left in August after a year and a half in the job.

Mr. Trump's announcement that he had offered the high-profile job to "violent Fighter and Warrior" Mr. White had sparked speculation that he was ready for a aggressive stance after the Republican Party's stunning midterm elections defeat.
Mr. White is a long-time friend of the president and helped host a massive UFC match on the White House lawn earlier this year.
But there was also some scepticism about the president's announcement, and Mr. Trump said Sunday (November 8) night that he had been joking.

Dana White visited the White House on November 9, and Donald Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room

Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White turned down President Donald Trump's -- apparently jovial -- offer of a job as press secretary in a surprise appearance at the White House on Monday (November 9, 2026).

Mr. Trump stunned the world by saying on social media on Saturday (November 7) that he had asked Mr. White to take on the high-profile post -- but a day later the 80-year-old president said he was "only kidding."

The 57-year-old cage fighting boss visited the White House on Monday (November 9), and Mr. Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room.

"So let me ask you the big question. Would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America? Or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC? Huh?" Mr. Trump said.

"Thank you for the offer, sir -- for the offer, I have no, no -- I do not want to be in politics," Mr. White replied.

Trump smiled and headed out of the room, saying: "I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everybody."

The press secretary's post has been been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week in the post. Her combative predecessor Karoline Leavitt left in August after a year and a half in the job.

Mr. Trump's announcement that he had offered the high-profile job to "violent Fighter and Warrior" Mr. White had sparked speculation that he was ready for a aggressive stance after the Republican Party's stunning midterm elections defeat.

Mr. White is a long-time friend of the president and helped host a massive UFC match on the White House lawn earlier this year.

But there was also some scepticism about the president's announcement, and Mr. Trump said Sunday (November 8) night that he had been joking.

articles.title: Who is Stephen Miller, Trump’s new Chief of Staff?
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Stephen Miller, one of U.S. President Donald Trump’s closest aides for decades, will replace Susie Wiles, who becomes the first major White House casualty from the Democratic landslide earlier this week

U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday (November 6, 2026) named Stephen Miller, architect of his hardline immigration policy, as his new Chief of Staff, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback after Republicans were hammered in the midterms.

Ultra-loyalist Miller, 41, will replace Susie Wiles, who becomes the first major White House casualty from the Democratic landslide earlier this week . In a post on Truth Social announcing Mr. Miller’s appointment, Mr. Trump described him as “one of my most trusted advisors”.

Stephen Miller, a key member of Mr. Trump’s inner circle, is a prominent architect of the administration’s hardline immigration policies. Known for his sharp suits and sunglasses, Miller has been one of Mr. Trump’s closest aides for decades and longest-serving advisers, pushing nativist policies that gelled with the President’s “America First” agenda.

Mr. Miller currently serves as White House Deputy Chief of Staff and though he has a wide-ranging portfolio, he is most closely aligned with the President’s immigration policy and rhetoric on immigration. He is also a former aide to hardliner former Sen. Jeff Sessions, R-Ala., who would go on to serve as Mr. Trump’s first Attorney General.

Mr. Miller was raised in politically liberal Santa Monica, California, but developed a reputation as a combative conservative as a columnist at Duke University’s student newspaper. ⁠As a congressional aide in the 2010s, he was an early advocate for restricting immigration at a time when that was not a mainstream position in the Republican Party.

He joined Mr. Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign, then served ‌as an advisor and speechwriter in his first 2017-2021 term. After Mr. Trump lost the 2020 election, Mr. Miller founded the conservative advocacy group America First Legal, filing complaints that accused companies ‌such as Nike of discriminating against white people.
His wife, Katie Miller, is a conservative podcaster and former ⁠communications aide in Mr. Trump’s first administration.
As Mr. Trump’s Deputy Chief of Staff for policy and homeland security advisor, he was the brains behind the mass deportation programme that defined the first year of the President’s second term.

Mr. Miller is best known for driving the immigration crackdown, setting a target of 3,000 arrests per day — far above levels under previous administrations. He has pushed U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to target anybody in the country illegally, ‌not just those with criminal records.
But he faced widespread criticism after the deadly shootings of two protesters by immigration agents in Minneapolis in January — incidents that sparked mass demonstrations.

articles.title: FDA adds rare vision-loss warning to popular obesity, diabetes drugs
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The eye condition, known as non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, can cause significant vision loss and has been reported with all GLP-1 drugs,

Popular weight loss drugs including Ozempic and Wegovy will carry a new warning about a possible rare side effect that can sometimes lead to permanent vision loss, U.S. health regulators announced Monday, November 9, 2026.

The Food and Drug Administration said the risk will be added to the labelling of all GLP-1 drugs, the blockbuster medications used to treat obesity, diabetes and several other medical conditions. The class includes a dozen injectable or pill-based drugs, including widely used brands like Zepbound and Mounjaro.

The eye condition, known as non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, can cause significant vision loss. The problem, which has been reported with all GLP-1 drugs, is caused by decreased blood flow to the optic nerve, although the underlying cause isn't understood, the FDA said.
FDA scientists began looking into the problem after the publication of a 2024 medical paper tying the condition to certain patients taking semaglutide, the active drug in Eli Lilly's Ozempic.

An FDA analysis of more than 125 clinical trials found that the problem occurred in roughly 6 of every 100,000 patients who took a GLP-1 for at least one year. The comparable rate for people taking a placebo or other types of glucose-lowering medications was less than 4 per 100,000, the FDA said.
The agency also found reports of the problem in its electronic reporting system for drug injuries and side effects.

Symptoms of the problem include blurred vision, blind spots, distorted colors and other visual disturbances, according to the FDA. Patients experiencing such problems should contact a health care professional immediately, the agency said.

articles.title: Nine Shigella cases confirmed in Malappuram; Health dept. steps up preventive measures
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Health department has stepped up preventive measures in Malappuram district following an outbreak of Shigella infection, with nine cases confirmed so far.

Cleaning operations, including super-chlorination of wells and houses in the affected areas, are under way. The family health centre at Elamkulam, near Perinthalmanna, formed a special squad to conduct house-to-house surveillance and create awareness about the infection.

The outbreak came to light after more than 100 people who attended a wedding at Elamkulam on October 31 reported symptoms. Extensive testing was conducted following the reports, and more people were placed under surveillance.

In a separate development, a four-year-old girl from Fifth Mile in Amarambalam panchayat, Nilambur, tested positive for Shigella. Following this, the Health department imposed restrictions on evening tea shops and street food stalls in the area. Inspections will also be extended to all food establishments in the panchayat.

Apart from those who attended the wedding, the confirmed cases include the four-year-old girl who ate snacks from a shop at Amarambalam and two people who had mandi from a restaurant at Palunda, Nilambur.

The food outlets suspected of being linked to the outbreak have been temporarily closed by the authorities. Two infected people are undergoing treatment at Perinthalmanna and Nilambur taluk hospitals.

The Health department has advised people to seek medical attention immediately if they develop diarrhoea or other symptoms and avoid self-medication. People have also been asked to drink plenty of ORS solution and boiled and cooled rice gruel to prevent dehydration.
Health officials advised people to drink only boiled and cooled water and consume clean food served hot.

articles.title: Keralam cardiologists seek review of order banning re-use of single-use medical devices
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: With an increasing proportion of the population requiring advanced cardiac interventions, making complex procedures affordable has become a challenge. Permitting the regulated re-use of select interventional devices, wherever scientifically proven safe, could help reduce costs, say doctors

Cardiologists have called for a review of a recent order issued by the Director General of Health Services (DGHS), strictly prohibiting the sterilisation and re-use of single-use devices and disposable surgical items used in critical specialties like cardiology and cardiothoracic and vascular surgery, citing issues of patient safety

At the annual conference of the Cardiological Society of India (CSI), Kerala chapter, here on Sunday, the CSI Kerala Chapter president Asokan P.K. said the association would seek a review of the order by DGHS as the exorbitant cost of medical devices and accessories would make crucial procedures such as angioplasty unaffordable and inaccessible to many.

Prathap Kumar N., organising chairman of the conference, said the rising cost of complex angioplasty, particularly procedures requiring multiple specialised devices, had become a major concern. Reimbursement package rates under government-funded health insurance schemes were often inadequate to cover the actual cost of advanced cardiac interventions.

With an increasing proportion of the population requiring advanced cardiac interventions, making complex procedures affordable to ordinary patients was a major challenge. Permitting the regulated re-use of select interventional devices, wherever scientifically proven safe, could help reduce treatment costs and extend the benefits of modern cardiac care to a wider section of the population, Dr. Prathap Kumar pointed out

He said cardiologists had sought a review to determine whether selected catheters, guidewires and other equipment could be safely re-processed under scientifically validated protocols and re-used for patients.

“Patient safety must remain paramount. Any proposal for re-use must be supported by scientific evidence, validated sterilisation, functional testing and strict regulatory oversight,” Dr. Prathap Kumar said.

He called for wider consultation among medical specialists, infection-control experts and regulatory authorities to develop an evidence-based policy regarding the sterilisation and re-use of medical devices, balancing affordability with patient safety.

The order by the DGHS said the practice of re-using single-use devices and disposable surgical items was a serious concern from the perspective of patient safety, infection prevention and control, regulatory compliance and healthcare expenditure. It said such re-use may also expose patients to significant risks, including cross-infection, device malfunction, loss of performance and other procedure-related complications

However, it is a fact that sterilisation and re-use of medical devices, ensuring the integrity of the devices and patient safety, is a common practice in both private and public sector hospitals across the country.

The Cardiological Society of India had in 2017 brought out a consensus document, “Guidance on reuse of cardio-vascular catheters and devices in India”, which clearly endorsed re-use, but set out certain requirements which had to be met for re-use to be safe and effective.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment 📅 10 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 Keralam cardiologists seek review of order banning re-use of single-use medical devices

🎯 Exam Relevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action

With an increasing proportion of the population requiring advanced cardiac interventions, making complex procedures affordable has become a challenge. Permitting the regulated re-use of select interventional devices, wherever scientifically proven safe, could help reduce costs, say doctors

Cardiologists have called for a review of a recent order issued by the Director General of Health Services (DGHS), strictly prohibiting the sterilisation and re-use of single-use devices and disposable surgical items used in critical specialties like cardiology and cardiothoracic and vascular surgery, citing issues of patient safety

At the annual conference of the Cardiological Society of India (CSI), Kerala chapter, here on Sunday, the CSI Kerala Chapter president Asokan P.K. said the association would seek a review of the order by DGHS as the exorbitant cost of medical devices and accessories would make crucial procedures such as angioplasty unaffordable and inaccessible to many.

Prathap Kumar N., organising chairman of the conference, said the rising cost of complex angioplasty, particularly procedures requiring multiple specialised devices, had become a major concern. Reimbursement package rates under government-funded health insurance schemes were often inadequate to cover the actual cost of advanced cardiac interventions.

With an increasing proportion of the population requiring advanced cardiac interventions, making complex procedures affordable to ordinary patients was a major challenge. Permitting the regulated re-use of select interventional devices, wherever scientifically proven safe, could help reduce treatment costs and extend the benefits of modern cardiac care to a wider section of the population, Dr. Prathap Kumar pointed out

He said cardiologists had sought a review to determine whether selected catheters, guidewires and other equipment could be safely re-processed under scientifically validated protocols and re-used for patients.

“Patient safety must remain paramount. Any proposal for re-use must be supported by scientific evidence, validated sterilisation, functional testing and strict regulatory oversight,” Dr. Prathap Kumar said.

He called for wider consultation among medical specialists, infection-control experts and regulatory authorities to develop an evidence-based policy regarding the sterilisation and re-use of medical devices, balancing affordability with patient safety.

The order by the DGHS said the practice of re-using single-use devices and disposable surgical items was a serious concern from the perspective of patient safety, infection prevention and control, regulatory compliance and healthcare expenditure. It said such re-use may also expose patients to significant risks, including cross-infection, device malfunction, loss of performance and other procedure-related complications

However, it is a fact that sterilisation and re-use of medical devices, ensuring the integrity of the devices and patient safety, is a common practice in both private and public sector hospitals across the country.

The Cardiological Society of India had in 2017 brought out a consensus document, “Guidance on reuse of cardio-vascular catheters and devices in India”, which clearly endorsed re-use, but set out certain requirements which had to be met for re-use to be safe and effective.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Cardiological Society of India had in 2017 brought out a consensus document, “Guidance on reuse of cardio-vascular catheters and devices in India”, which clearly endorsed re-use, but set out certain requirements which had to be met for re-use to be safe and effective.

articles.title: NMC cautions students against fake medical colleges, asks them to verify approvals
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The advisory follows the Supreme Court taking cognisance of the issue in an ongoing case in which the court directed regulatory bodies, including the National Medical Commission, to caution students and parents against dealing with unauthorised educational institutions

The National Medical Commission (NMC) has cautioned students and parents against enrolling in medical colleges without verifying their statutory recognition and regulatory approvals, warning that fraudulent institutions could be misleading aspirants through advertisements, websites, social media promotions and unauthorised admission offers.

In a recent advisory issued in compliance with directions from the Supreme Court, the NMC has urged students to independently verify a medical college’s approval status, permitted student intake, and admission permissions for the relevant academic year before seeking admission or making any payment.

The advisory follows the Supreme Court taking cognisance of the issue in Ayesha Jain v. Amity University, Noida & Ors. , an ongoing case in which the Court directed regulatory bodies, including the NMC, to caution students and parents against dealing with unauthorised educational institutions. The directions came in the context of a reported instance of a purported fake medical college operating from a farmhouse and claiming to offer various courses.

The Commission has clarified that a medical college’s presence in an official list, or its previous operation, does not automatically establish that it has permission to admit students in subsequent academic years. Candidates must check the approval granted for the particular year and the number of seats sanctioned through official NMC and Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) records.

It has also cautioned students against relying exclusively on prospectuses, websites, advertisements, social media posts or documents such as purported Letters of Permission and approval certificates circulated by institutions or their representatives. Any doubts regarding the authenticity of such documents should be verified directly with the concerned regulatory authority.

For admissions governed by counselling procedures, candidates have been asked to use official channels, including the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC), wherever applicable, or the competent State and Union Territory counselling authorities. The Commission has also advised students against making admission-related payments to unauthorised agents, personal bank accounts or unverified intermediaries.

Highlighting the importance of distinguishing between regulatory approvals, the NMC said affiliation, registration or recognition granted by one authority for a particular purpose should not be construed as permission from the Commission to conduct an MBBS course. Each statutory requirement must be independently satisfied.

The advisory also asks students and parents to exercise caution when institutions make extraordinary claims about clinical training, hospital facilities and admission opportunities. The existence of a building, office or website, it said, does not establish that an institution is legally authorised to impart medical education.

Suspected fake medical colleges, unauthorised MBBS courses, forged permission letters and fraudulent admission offers can be reported to the NMC through its official communication channels. Complaints may also be made to the State or U.T. medical education departments, relevant regulatory authorities, and local police. Students have been advised to preserve advertisements, payment receipts, correspondence and website details as supporting evidence.

The Commission has separately clarified that courses in pharmacy, nursing, Ayurveda, and allied healthcare programmes fall under different statutory or competent regulatory authorities. Their recognition and approval must be checked with the respective regulators.

articles.title: PM Modi and Railway Minister likely to flag off Bengaluru–Mangaluru–Goa Vande Bharat Express on November 13
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: While Narendra Modi flags off the much awaited service from Bengaluru, Ashwini Vaishnaw will do it from Mangaluru Junction

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw are likely to flag off the Yeshwantpur-Mangaluru-Madgaon-Yeshwantpur Vande Bharat Express on November 13 from Bengaluru and Mangaluru Junction simultaneously.

Mr. Modi will be in Bengaluru to dedicate the 7.5 km Namma Metro Pink Line between Kalena Agrahara and Tavarekere along the Bannerghatta Road, as announced earlier by Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda. During this occasion, the Prime Minister will also remotely flag off the Bengaluru-Goa Vande Bharat Express starting from Sir M. Visvesvaraya Terminal, Bengaluru, sources in the South Western Railway (SWR) told The Hindu .

Mr. Vaishnaw, as promised to Members of Parliament from the coast, would launch the new service from Mangaluru Junction at around 2.30 p.m., sources said. Both the down and up inaugural specials would run simultaneously towards Bengaluru and Mangaluru. Regular services of the VB Express could start within a day or two, sources said adding regular services would operate out of Yeshwantpur; and not SMVTB.

The Railway Minister had, on September 29, announced that the Ministry would introduce Yeshwantpur-Mangaluru-Madgaon-Yeshwantpur Vande Bharat Express as Train No. 26655/656 by extending the existing Mangaluru Central-Madgaon-Mangaluru Central VB Express (Train No. 20646/645). Releasing the timetable of the extended service on October 30, the Ministry had said the services would start at an early convenient date or ‘no booking’ date for Mangaluru-Madgaon-Mangaluru VB.

The Bengaluru-Madgaon VB Express would have 12 halts, excluding the originating and terminating stations. They are, Shravanabelagola, Hassan, Sakleshpur, Subrahmanya Road, Kabaka Puttur, Mangaluru Junction, Udupi, Kundapura, Byndoor, Murdeshwar, Gokarna Road and Karwar.

While the Yeshwantpur-Madgaon service leaves Yeshwantpur at 7.35 a.m. to reach Madgaon at 8.55 p.m. taking 12.20 hours except on Wednesdays, the Madgaon-Yeshwantpur service departs Madgaon at 8.20 a.m. to reach Yeshwantpur at 9.15 p.m. taking 13 hours except on Thursdays.
Two rakes required for the service are kept ready, sources added.

articles.title: HMWS&SB fines Akshayakalpa Farms ₹20,000 for wasting drinking water in Hyderabad’s Jubilee Hills
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB) has imposed a fine of ₹20,000 on Akshayakalpa Farms and Foods Private Limited in Jubilee Hills for using drinking water to clean floors. The Board has also temporarily disconnected the sewage connection at the premises as part of its drive to curb the wastage and misuse of drinking water.

The action was taken after officials found drinking water being used for floor cleaning at the company’s premises in Journalist Colony, Road No. 70, Jubilee Hills. HMWS&SB said it had intensified inspections across Hyderabad in anticipation of potential water availability challenges during the upcoming summer and was taking measures to conserve drinking water.

Officials have urged residents and commercial establishments to restrict the use of drinking water to essential purposes such as drinking and cooking. They have cautioned against using potable water for floor cleaning, vehicle washing, gardening and construction activities, and advised the public to use treated water supplied from sewage treatment plants (STPs) for such purposes.

The Board warned that inspections would continue across the city and strict action would be taken against establishments found wasting or misusing drinking water. It has also appealed to citizens to report instances of drinking water wastage by sending details, photographs or videos to its WhatsApp number 99499 30003.

articles.title: NCW receives 1.5 lakh complaints annually, domestic violence tops list: Vijaya Rahatkar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: No woman should feel that she could not approach the NCW simply because she did not know how to file a complaint, Vijaya Rahatkar
The National Commission for Women receives around 1.5 lakh complaints annually, with domestic violence accounting for the highest number of cases, NCW Chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar has said.

In an interview with PTI , Ms. Rahatkar said there are multiple ways, including the commission's online portal, Management Information System (MIS), email, in person and its 24x7 helpline, for women to approach the NCW to register their complaints.
"We receive around 1.5 lakh complaints annually. If we look at the cases falling under our mandate, domestic violence accounts for the highest number of complaints," she said.

articles.title: Six months into its rule, TVK-led govt. in Tamil Nadu enjoys public goodwill despite concerns on being directionless
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Though Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, on his very first day in office, had declared that he had inherited an ‘empty coffer,’ the government has been continuing with all the major welfare measures

The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) -led government in Tamil Nadu, which completed six months in office on Monday (November 9, 2026), appears to be largely enjoying the goodwill of people, even though concerns are being raised about the regime’s tendency to be directionless.

Though Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, on his very first day in office, had declared that he had inherited an “empty coffer,” the government has been continuing with all the major welfare measures. The “precarious” financial condition did not come in the way of his government carrying out some other steps such as the extension of the breakfast scheme for school students , the provision of gold rings to babies born at government hospitals, the distribution of eight-gram gold coins and silk saris to eligible women, and the expansion of free travel for women on buses of the State Transport Corporations.

Reports of a “marked reduction“ in corruption regarding government appointments, transfers, and public services have impressed many observers including former Union Minister P. Chidambaram and UN diplomat-turned-political writer R. Kannan.

In an interview with this newspaper a couple of months ago, Mr. Chidambaram stated: “I also understand that sanctions for the appointment of teachers in [government-aided] schools and colleges have been sent by post.”

According to Mr. Kannan, “transparency remains the Vijay administration’s strongest asset.” The ruling party’s national spokesperson, Americai V. Narayanan, says: “He [Mr. Vijay] does not do things to please others or earn applause. He does them because he genuinely believes in them. In politics, where symbolism often outweighs conviction, that distinction matters.”

Notwithstanding the general perception about the government‘s integrity, the two Dravidian majors — the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) — have been unsparing. One of the areas of their attack is on the power front, where the current regime had, ironically, begun with the increase in the quantum of free power to 200 units bimonthly to domestic consumers subject to the overall consumption not exceeding 500 units. The regime’s plans for power purchase on a short-term basis at a higher cost has raised questions about the government’s competence.

DMK president M.K. Stalin and AIADMK’s Amma Peravai secretary R.B. Udhayakumar wondered when Keralam could buy electricity at lower price, why Tamil Nadu has not been able to procure at comparable rates. Besides, even the lower price has triggered a controversy in the neighbouring State.

It is not only on the power front where the government is found on a weak wicket but also on many other policy matters. On the issue of wooing industrial investment , the Opposition’s attack has not been firmly rebutted by the government. As for the TVK regime’s project of building a new Secretariat complex, there has not been any categorical statement from the Chief Minister on the controversy triggered by it, though his Ministerial colleagues, at times, make different observations.

articles.title: Newly-inducted J&K Minister Mir Saifullah pledges that NC will ‘restore pre-1953 position, get back J&K flag’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Saifullah said Kashmir was reduced to a Union Territory (UT) brazenly on August 5, 2019

Ruling National Conference (NC) minister Mir Saifullah on Monday (November 9, 2026) said the party has pledged to fight for the “return of the snatched special status and the separate flag” for Jammu and Kashmir .

“Whatever has been snatched will be taken back. It was the NC who got pre-1953 status, Article 370 and separate flag for J&K. The struggle for their return has begun. We all start from zero but will reach 100 one day. The struggle has started,” said Mr. Saifullah, a legislator from north Kashmir’s Kupwara district.

Mr. Saifullah made the statement at a rally held at Kralpora of the Trehgam constituency, Kupwara, for the first time since he was inducted in the Cabinet of Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on October 27.

Mr. Saifullah said Kashmir was reduced to a Union Territory (UT) brazenly on August 5, 2019. “The downgrading and division of J&K on August 5, 2019 was ‘ zulum ’ (injustice) that no part of the world has seen. It was a stab on out chest. Our flag and constitution were taken away. All the parties should join hands to restore the flag of J&K,” he added.
He said the NC was for everyone and “ will get Statehood and Article 35A restored” . “Only the NC can do it,” he added.

Terming the NC “a movement and not mere a party”, Mr. Saifullah the party founder Sheikh Muhammad Abdullah is the man behind the multi-dimensional development in the society. “We had no schools, no hospitals, no roads, no universities, no water supply. All this was worked on by NC’s Sheikh Abdullah.
