articles.title: 19 Indian seafarers stranded in Yemen evacuated, Embassy says
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The evacuation comes days after India said 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht involved in an incident off the Yemeni coast were safe

Nineteen Indian seafarers stranded in Yemen's Hodeidah and Sana'a for the past two weeks have been evacuated, with all of them safe and on their way back to their country, the Indian Embassy in Yemen said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

“All seafarers are safe, in good health, and on their way back to India. The Embassy sincerely thanks all concerned for their valuable cooperation and continued support in facilitating the safe evacuation of our Indian nationals,” the mission said in a post on X.

The Embassy of India to Yemen has successfully evacuated 19 Indian seafarers who were stranded in Hodeidah and Sana'a (Yemen) for the past two weeks. All seafarers are safe, in good health, and on their way back to India. The Embassy sincerely thanks all concerned for their valuable cooperation and continued support in facilitating the safe evacuation of our Indian nationals. @MEAIndia
The evacuation comes days after India said 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht involved in an incident off the Yemeni coast were safe.
It is not immediately clear whether the 14 are among the 19 seafarers evacuated.

On October 23, the Indian mission had said all 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht near Hodeidah were safe and that it was in contact with relevant parties to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

Some Arab media outlets had earlier quoted spokesperson Yahya Saree of the Yemen-based Houthi group as claiming that Saudi forces targeted the Indian yacht near Yuqar Island in the Red Sea, close to the Yemeni coast.
Mr. Saree had said the yacht was carrying 14 Indian nationals and that Houthi forces were rescuing them.
The incident came amid renewed escalation between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis, with attacks and counterattacks reported in recent days.

Saudi Arabia has intercepted Houthi missiles and drones, while Saudi-led coalition forces have carried out airstrikes in Yemen, raising fears of a return to wider conflict after relative calm under a 2022 truce.

articles.title: Fire engulfs Jammu’s Nehru Market, guts around 12 shops
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Another blaze was reported in the border district of Kathua, where, a store room at the district police lines went up in flames

Fire gutted at least a dozen shops in the historic Nehru Market in the heart of Jammu city on Sunday (November 8, 2026) night, while a separate blaze broke out at the district police lines in Kathua district, officials said.
No casualties were reported in either incident, which occurred amid widespread bursting of firecrackers on Deepavali.
All the same, the exact cause of the blazes is yet to be ascertained.
A massive fire swept the Warehouse Nehru Market, one of Jammu's oldest wholesale hubs of food grains, essential commodities and other daily-use items.
The Fire and Emergency Services Department said the fire began in one of the shops at around 9.15 p.m. and spread quickly to adjoining establishments due to storage of edible oil.
The market has been serving traders, retailers and consumers since the 1950s.

Fire tenders from several stations across Jammu city were rushed to the spot, officials said. At the site, Divisional Commissioner, Jammu, Vikas Kundal, said the fire had been largely brought under control.

"Fire and Emergency Services personnel, police teams and the civil administration are present at the spot. The fire has been brought under control, and efforts are underway to extinguish the remaining flames in the last one or two shops," he told reporters.
Warehouse Association president Deepak Gupta blamed the delayed response of the fire and emergency services for the spread of the flames.

"What started as a small fire has engulfed around 15 shops and threatens to spread further. This is a complete failure and gross negligence on the part of the fire brigade. Despite the fire station being barely five minutes away, only two fire engines arrived after an hour and a half," he alleged.

articles.title: Infiltrators lurking across the border, will send them back from the same way they enter: Adhikari
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Blaming the previous Trinamool Congress government for non-cooperation with the border guarding forces, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that a wonderful coordination has been achieved between the West Bengal police and the BSF
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday (November 9, 2026) said that infiltrators are lurking across the border and promised to send them back the same way they try to enter into India.
Mr. Adhikari spent Diwali afternoon with Border Security Force (BSF) personnel at Hingalganj in North 24 Parganas in West Bengal.

After touring the area on a BSF speedboat in the Ichhamati river that serves as a border between India and Bangladesh, the CM said that he could see no fencing on the Bangladesh side and infiltrators lurking along the border. “Bangladeshis are there. If they find a gap, they will enter India in a hurry,” he said.

Mr. Adhikari said lakhs of infiltrators have been pushed back into Bangladesh after the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power. “We will search infiltrators and send them back from the very same way they are coming. Search will go on for 15 kilometres from the border,” he said.
The BJP government came to power in West Bengal on the promise of pushing back infiltrators and the BJP government has been making claims of sending back thousands of infiltrators.

Blaming the previous Trinamool Congress government for non-cooperation with the BSF, Mr. Adhikari said that a wonderful coordination has been achieved between the West Bengal police and the BSF under his government.
“I, as the chief minister of the state, apologise to you for the derogatory remarks and behaviour of the previous regime towards BSF and CRPF,” he said.
The BJP government in West Bengal has handed over about 1,777 acres of land across nine border districts to the BSF for fencing and setting up outposts along the India-Bangladesh border.
India shares a 4,096-kilometre border with Bangladesh, of which about 2,216 km lies along West Bengal.

The Chief Minister said that most of issues have been sorted and land for erecting fencing along Ichhamati has been given. Mr. Adhikari said West Bengal’s Department of Irrigation and Waterways will construct the fencing along the 71-kilometre stretch of river.

articles.title: Nvidia investigating reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The announcement came after Jensen Huang acknowledged to the board that he had been intimate with a business executive whom U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing
Nvidia is opening an investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort,” the company's board of directors said Sunday (November 8, 2026).

The announcement came after Mr. Huang acknowledged to the board that he had been intimate with a business executive whom U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing, The New York Times reported.

Mr. Huang apologised in a message to the company, according to the Times . “I was unfaithful to my wife,” he said. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Nvidia's board said in a statement it has “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised,” but that its inquiry would examine all available information. Mr. Huang “fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it,” the board said.
Mr. Huang, 63, will remain CEO during the investigation.

The Times reported last month that U.S. intelligence agencies had discovered that Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, and determined that she was feeding information directly to Beijing. The two are not related, according to the Times .

Ms. Alice Huang was previously a television reporter in China before becoming a top executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, which has become one of Nvidia's biggest customers in Southeast Asia. Megaspeed bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years, according to the Times .

articles.title: Saudi Arabia turns to Syria for help as fighting with Houthis escalates
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A Syrian official said that an initial force of about 600 Syrian special forces fighters is expected to be deployed to Saudi Arabia in the coming week

Syria is preparing to send fighters to Saudi Arabia to deploy along its border and potentially help it fight Iranian-backed rebels in neighbouring Yemen, three officials with knowledge of the plans told The Associated Press .

Syrian military advisers have already deployed to Saudi Arabia, but no fighters have been sent to Yemen, according to a regional official and two Syrian officials, all of whom spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to comment publicly.
Officials in Saudi Arabia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Fighting escalated this summer in Yemen between the Houthi rebels and the government's Saudi-backed forces. The Houthis have also launched direct and deadly attacks on Saudi Arabia in what is the latest front in the regional conflict that began in February when the US and Israel attacked Iran.
Syria, which has a supply of battle-hardened fighters after a long civil war, has so far stayed on the sidelines.
Saudi Arabia has an array of U.S.-supplied fighter jets and missile defences but has been unable to defeat the Houthis in past rounds of conflict.

While Saudi Arabia’s other allies have been reluctant to commit ground forces to its fight with the Houthis, the Syrian government is beholden to it. The Saudis provided funds to Syrian rebels during that country's civil war and have promised much-needed financial assistance for Syria's postwar reconstruction.
A Syrian official said that an initial force of about 600 Syrian special forces fighters is expected to be deployed to Saudi Arabia in the coming week.

The official said that a Syrian delegation led by Khaled Khattab, commander of the 82nd Division, had recently made a two-week visit to Saudi Arabia. A second Syrian official said 36 Syrian military officials visited a command and operations room in Jeddah staffed by Saudi and Yemeni officials and received briefings on the different front lines and areas of operation.
A regional official with knowledge of the discussions said Syria had already deployed a “small number of advisers” to Saudi Arabia, where they helped train Yemeni forces inside the kingdom.

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

A Syrian official said that an initial force of about 600 Syrian special forces fighters is expected to be deployed to Saudi Arabia in the coming week

Syria is preparing to send fighters to Saudi Arabia to deploy along its border and potentially help it fight Iranian-backed rebels in neighbouring Yemen, three officials with knowledge of the plans told The Associated Press .

Syrian military advisers have already deployed to Saudi Arabia, but no fighters have been sent to Yemen, according to a regional official and two Syrian officials, all of whom spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to comment publicly.

Officials in Saudi Arabia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Fighting escalated this summer in Yemen between the Houthi rebels and the government's Saudi-backed forces. The Houthis have also launched direct and deadly attacks on Saudi Arabia in what is the latest front in the regional conflict that began in February when the US and Israel attacked Iran.

Syria, which has a supply of battle-hardened fighters after a long civil war, has so far stayed on the sidelines.

Saudi Arabia has an array of U.S.-supplied fighter jets and missile defences but has been unable to defeat the Houthis in past rounds of conflict.

While Saudi Arabia’s other allies have been reluctant to commit ground forces to its fight with the Houthis, the Syrian government is beholden to it. The Saudis provided funds to Syrian rebels during that country's civil war and have promised much-needed financial assistance for Syria's postwar reconstruction.

A Syrian official said that an initial force of about 600 Syrian special forces fighters is expected to be deployed to Saudi Arabia in the coming week.

The official said that a Syrian delegation led by Khaled Khattab, commander of the 82nd Division, had recently made a two-week visit to Saudi Arabia. A second Syrian official said 36 Syrian military officials visited a command and operations room in Jeddah staffed by Saudi and Yemeni officials and received briefings on the different front lines and areas of operation.

A regional official with knowledge of the discussions said Syria had already deployed a “small number of advisers” to Saudi Arabia, where they helped train Yemeni forces inside the kingdom.

articles.title: Trump and his Justice Department stand defiant as Democrats ready an investigative blitz
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Mr. Trump set the tone, declaring on social media that investigative requests already made by Democrats are “extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable”

U.S. President Donald Trump and his Department of Justice are taking a combative stance toward Democrats after their election victories in the midterms, signalling intense conflict to come as lawmakers prepare aggressive investigations into the executive branch next year.
Mr. Trump set the tone, declaring on social media that investigative requests already made by Democrats are “extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable.”
Attorney General Todd Blanche echoed the Republican president and said criminal investigations of Democrats are possible.

“They are not allowed to just go around threatening existing members of the administration, to go around threatening companies, and that's what President Trump is extremely worried about and he should be,” Mr. Blanche said as he and congressional Democrats appeared on the Sunday news shows to discuss the repercussions from last week's elections.

Rep. Robert Garcia, who is poised to chair the powerful House Oversight Committee in the next Congress, is preparing investigations into what he calls the “Trump crime family.” He said Democrats are not going to be intimidated.
“The days of us not fighting back are over,” said Mr. Garcia, D-Calif.

The early rhetoric sets up a showdown ahead that will likely define Mr. Trump's remaining two years in office and test the power of Congress to put a check on the White House. About seven in 10 voters nationally say Congress is not doing enough to provide checks and balances on the presidency, according to The AP Voter Poll, a survey of more than 1,00,000 midterm voters.
Democrats have made clear that impeachment is an option.

If there are people who have been "shortchanging the American people, screwing over the American people, or stealing from the American people, then they need to be held accountable in a manner consistent with Congress' role, constitutionally,” said Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York.

But the investigative onslaught is also a source of tension for Democrats, with many warning that delivering on their central promise to voters — actions to lower the cost of living — must take precedence.

articles.title: Pope Leo takes Milei to task as he visits divided Argentina
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Pope Leo spoke out in defence of the poor and pensioners, insisting that “particular concern be shown for those affected by illness, dependency and disability” — a veiled reference to the government’s controversial cuts to disability assistance

Pope Leo XIV delivered a stinging critique of Argentina President Javier Milei's harsh austerity measures on Sunday (November 8, 2026), insisting growth must benefit all in a speech met with rapturous applause.
"The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy," he said, shortly after landing in Argentina on the second leg of a Latin America tour.
Pope Leo stressed the plight of those who, "despite hard work, nonetheless struggle to meet their household's needs."

He spoke out in defence of the poor and pensioners, insisting that "particular concern be shown for those affected by illness, dependency and disability" — a veiled reference to the government's controversial cuts to disability assistance.
And he told Mr. Milei, known for his foul-mouthed diatribes, that strengthening democracy required a "willingness to listen" and the "careful use of words."
The visit is the first by a pontiff to Argentina in nearly four decades and Pope Leo was met with calls to help mend deep divisions in the country after three years of austerity under Mr. Milei.
Pope Leo arrived in Buenos Aires from Uruguay, where he began his first trip to Latin America as Pope, the world's most Catholic continent that is becoming increasingly secular.
The visit is the first by a pontiff to the home country of the late Pope Francis in nearly four decades.
Mr. Milei famously insulted Pope Francis for his pro-poor teachings. Pope Leo said he was "retracing" Pope Francis's steps.
Argentines are hoping the leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics will help unite the country, which is bitterly divided between supporters and opponents of Mr. Milei.

articles.title: Major fire breaks out in Mumbai's Dongri, dousing ops on; one dead in November 7 highrise blaze

fullParagraphs: The Mumbai Fire Brigade (MFB) declared it a Level-I fire call at 10.11 p.m., deploying a large number of its personnel along with those from the police, BEST, ward and 108 ambulance service for dousing operations
A major fire broke out in Mumbai's Dongri area late Sunday (November 8, 2026) night, engulfing several shops and hutments, civic officials and residents said.
The fire broke out at Haji Kasam Chawl, near Datta Mandir, on Dr Maheshwari Road, and spread across a large area.
While residents also reported hearing loud "explosion-like" sounds, it could not be independently confirmed.

The Mumbai Fire Brigade (MFB) declared it a Level-I fire call at 10.11 p.m., deploying a large number of its personnel along with those from the police, BEST, ward and 108 ambulance service for dousing operations.
"Efforts to bring the blaze under control are underway. Further details about the extent of damage and possible casualties are awaited," an official said.

Early morning visuals from Mumbai’s Dongri area, where a major fire broke out late Sunday (November 8, 2026) night at Haji Kasam Chawl, gutting several shops and hutments. Fire tenders remain on-site carrying out cooling operations while affected locals sift through the remnants of their shops. | Photo Credit: Emmanual Yogini
In another incident, a fire broke out at Kamgar Stadium in Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Nagar in Dadar West at around 10.15 a.m. on Sunday (November 8).
The blaze, involving wooden and bamboo materials, was extinguished by the fire brigade at 10.32 a.m. No injuries were reported, an official said.
Meanwhile, a person was killed in a fire that broke out at a highrise residential building in Lokhandwala in Andheri West on Saturday (November 7) night, officials said.

articles.title: Karnataka tests petrol samples at 67 locations over ethanol blending complaints: CM Shivakumar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the CM, inspections had been carried out not only at petrol pumps but also at the stages of ethanol blending and distribution

Karnataka Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar on Sunday (November 8, 2026) said petrol samples had been collected and tested at 67 locations across the state following complaints that increased ethanol blending was affecting vehicle engine performance.

Speaking to reporters in Bengaluru, Mr. Shivakumar said, “The government has taken serious note of complaints regarding 31.5 per cent ethanol being blended into petrol. Necessary instructions have been issued to the concerned minister in this regard, and information has also been sent to the Central Government.”
Thousands of motorists have complained about various issues, including reduced vehicle mileage, failure to cover expected distances, and engines stalling while in motion, he said.
According to the CM, inspections had been carried out not only at petrol pumps but also at the stages of ethanol blending and distribution.
Documents relating to where and how the blending was being undertaken had also been collected.
“The concerned minister will officially hold a press conference on Monday to provide details regarding the inspection report and the next course of action,” Mr. Shivakumar said.
Holding the Centre responsible for addressing the issue, he said, “The Centre cannot shirk responsibility on this matter. Vehicle performance, fuel quality, and public safety are paramount.”
“It is not right to increase the blending ratio simply to profit from ethanol being available at a lower cost. Causing inconvenience to the public is not acceptable,” he said.
Mr. Shivakumar said his government was taking the complaints seriously and questioned the silence of BJP and JD(S) leaders on the issue.
“Why are BJP and JD(S) leaders, as well as Leader of the Opposition R Ashoka, silent on this issue? Everyone must raise their voice on matters concerning the public interest,” he said.

Thousands of motorists have complained about various issues, including reduced vehicle mileage, failure to cover expected distances, and engines stalling while in motion, he said.

According to the CM, inspections had been carried out not only at petrol pumps but also at the stages of ethanol blending and distribution.

Documents relating to where and how the blending was being undertaken had also been collected.

“The concerned minister will officially hold a press conference on Monday to provide details regarding the inspection report and the next course of action,” Mr. Shivakumar said.

Holding the Centre responsible for addressing the issue, he said, “The Centre cannot shirk responsibility on this matter. Vehicle performance, fuel quality, and public safety are paramount.”

“It is not right to increase the blending ratio simply to profit from ethanol being available at a lower cost. Causing inconvenience to the public is not acceptable,” he said.

Mr. Shivakumar said his government was taking the complaints seriously and questioned the silence of BJP and JD(S) leaders on the issue.

“Why are BJP and JD(S) leaders, as well as Leader of the Opposition R Ashoka, silent on this issue? Everyone must raise their voice on matters concerning the public interest,” he said.

articles.title: Rubio says Trump's war against Iran not 'necessarily popular' but needed to stop a nuclear threat
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: America's top diplomat offered a robust defence of the more than eight-month-old war even as voters blamed Mr. Trump's policies for the hit to their pocketbooks, including higher energy prices that stemmed from disruptions to shipments in the Strait of Hormuz

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Sunday (November 7, 2026) that President Donald Trump launched the war against Iran, even if it was not “necessarily popular”, to safeguard the world from the country's nuclear ambitions.

He would not comment directly about the Republican wipeout in Tuesday's (November 3) elections, which delivered a resounding rebuke to Mr. Trump. The unpopularity of the Iran war and its impact on gasoline prices and other parts of the economy helped Democrats seize control of Congress.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Marco Rubio: Iran can never be allowed to become a nuclear weapons power

Asked about Vice-President J.D. Vance's social media post last week that largely blamed the war for the Republican losses, Mr. Rubio told reporters that Mr. Trump “identified a very real threat” in Iran and worked to stop the Islamic Republic from pursuing a nuclear weapon.
Trump to meet Iran war mediator Qatar, no imminent deal seen to end war

“He addressed it even though oftentimes the right thing to do for the country — confronting difficult challenges for the security of our country — doing it isn't necessarily popular, but necessary,” Mr. Rubio said in Florida before heading to a Group of 7 Foreign Ministers meeting in Paris.

America's top diplomat offered a robust defence of the more than eight-month-old war even as voters blamed Mr. Trump's policies for the hit to their pocketbooks, including higher energy prices that stemmed from disruptions to shipments in the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway where one-fifth of the world's oil transited before the war.
“I can tell you, this historically — for history — will go down as one of the best things we ever did," Mr. Trump said. "Because if they ever had a nuclear weapon, they would blow up the world."

Iran has long maintained that its nuclear programme is peaceful. According to the International Atomic Energy Agency, Iran has 440.9 kg of uranium that is enriched up to 60% purity, a short, technical step from weapons-grade levels of 90%.
With no clear administration strategy to wind down the conflict and West Asia on edge over the possibility of a return to major hostilities, mediators are trying to revive talks between the sides.

articles.title: Series of fire incidents at firecracker shops, godowns mar Deepavali in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A fire broke out at a plastic manufacturing unit in Katedan Industrial Area and subsequently spread to a neighbouring plywood unit, prompting the deployment of three fire engines

A series of fire incidents were reported in different parts of Hyderabad and Secunderabad on Sunday (November 8, 2026), with fire personnel responding to blazes at firecracker shops, commercial establishments and industrial premises. While some incidents involved firecrackers, suspected electrical faults were cited as a possible cause in others.

At Sitaphalmandi in Secunderabad, a rocket burst into a firecracker shop during the celebrations, setting off the stock of crackers stored inside. The firecrackers began exploding as the blaze spread through the premises, prompting an emergency response from the Fire Services Department. Firefighters reached the spot and brought the situation under control. The extent of the damage was yet to be assessed.

Earlier in the day, at around 11.40 a.m., a fire broke out at another firecracker shop in Chilkalguda. The shop owners told fire personnel that they had lit a lamp as part of the prayers when a suspected short circuit triggered the blaze, according to an officer at the fire control room. A fire engine was dispatched to the spot. No injuries were reported.

Industrial establishments were also affected. A fire broke out at a plastic manufacturing unit in Katedan Industrial Area and subsequently spread to a neighbouring plywood unit, prompting the deployment of three fire engines. Firefighters, assisted by disaster response teams, worked to prevent the blaze from spreading to other units. No casualties were reported immediately.

In another incident, two adjoining storage facilities in Mailardevpally Industrial Estate were affected after a fire broke out in a plastic godown and spread to a neighbouring plywood godown. Three fire engines were deployed, while police helped evacuate people from the affected premises. Both facilities suffered damage to the goods stored inside. The cause of the fire was yet to be determined.

In Secunderabad, a fire was reported at Balaji Medical Shop in Bandimet, with fire personnel rushing to the premises to tackle the blaze. A separate incident was reported at a medical warehouse in Old Bowenpally, where a fire broke out on the third floor of the building.
The causes of the incidents and the overall extent of the losses were yet to be established.

articles.title: Parliament’s Monsoon session remains unprorogued for record 88 days
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: As of November 9, 2026 morning, neither the Lok Sabha nor the Rajya Sabha had been formally prorogued, keeping open the possibility of convening an extended sitting of the existing session
Parliament's Monsoon session has remained unprorogued for 88 days since both Houses were adjourned indefinitely on August 13, breaking the previous record of 87 days in 2008.
As of Monday (November 9, 2026) morning, neither the Lok Sabha nor the Rajya Sabha had been formally prorogued, keeping open the possibility of convening an extended sitting of the existing session.

The government's decision not to prorogue (formally end) the Monsoon session has kept alive speculation about the possibility of convening Parliament at short notice to consider the proposed constitutional amendment linked to the implementation of the Women's Reservation Bill, which seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation.
An extended or special sitting of Parliament within the same session requires a minimum notice of two days, whereas convening a fresh session requires at least 14 days' notice.
This has added significance as a similar Constitution Amendment Bill had failed to secure the required numbers in the Lok Sabha during a special sitting of the Budget session on April 17.
The Constitution does not prescribe any specific time frame within which a House must be prorogued after being adjourned sine die (for an indefinite period).
The mere fact that a House remains unprorogued for an extended period does not, by itself, amount to any constitutional or procedural impropriety.
According to records, Parliament had remained unprorogued for 87 days in 2008, 76 days in 1987, 54 days in 1989, 49 days each in 2006 and 2013, and 41 days in 1963.

In 2008, the Lok Sabha met for two days, July 21 and 22, to discuss the no-confidence motion against the then UPA government. The House was subsequently kept unprorogued, reconvened on October 17 and was adjourned on October 24 to meet again on December 10.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 09 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Parliament’s Monsoon session remains unprorogued for record 88 days

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

As of November 9, 2026 morning, neither the Lok Sabha nor the Rajya Sabha had been formally prorogued, keeping open the possibility of convening an extended sitting of the existing session

Parliament's Monsoon session has remained unprorogued for 88 days since both Houses were adjourned indefinitely on August 13, breaking the previous record of 87 days in 2008.

As of Monday (November 9, 2026) morning, neither the Lok Sabha nor the Rajya Sabha had been formally prorogued, keeping open the possibility of convening an extended sitting of the existing session.

The government's decision not to prorogue (formally end) the Monsoon session has kept alive speculation about the possibility of convening Parliament at short notice to consider the proposed constitutional amendment linked to the implementation of the Women's Reservation Bill, which seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation.

An extended or special sitting of Parliament within the same session requires a minimum notice of two days, whereas convening a fresh session requires at least 14 days' notice.

This has added significance as a similar Constitution Amendment Bill had failed to secure the required numbers in the Lok Sabha during a special sitting of the Budget session on April 17.

The Constitution does not prescribe any specific time frame within which a House must be prorogued after being adjourned sine die (for an indefinite period).

The mere fact that a House remains unprorogued for an extended period does not, by itself, amount to any constitutional or procedural impropriety.

According to records, Parliament had remained unprorogued for 87 days in 2008, 76 days in 1987, 54 days in 1989, 49 days each in 2006 and 2013, and 41 days in 1963.

In 2008, the Lok Sabha met for two days, July 21 and 22, to discuss the no-confidence motion against the then UPA government. The House was subsequently kept unprorogued, reconvened on October 17 and was adjourned on October 24 to meet again on December 10.

articles.title: Air of Deepavali celebrations lingers in Hyderabad with AQI remaining at hazardous levels
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The air quality in Hyderabad deteriorated in the night itself with particulate matter 2.5 reaching 392 micrograms per cubic meter (μg/m³) at 9.30 p.m. and the Air Quality Index averaged 509

Hyderabad woke up to a grey smoggy morning on Monday (November 9, 2026) a day after a Big Bang Deepavali celebration that went on till 3 a.m. in the morning in many central localities like Banjara Hills, Srinagar Colony, Panjagutta, S.R. Nagar, Ameerpet and Somajiguda.

The air quality in Hyderabad deteriorated in the night itself with particulate matter 2.5 reaching 392 micrograms per cubic meter (μg/m³) at 9.30 p.m. and the Air Quality Index averaged 509. At the same time, Ravi Colony near Masjid Banda logged 995 AQI as crackers went off one after the other.

The data was sourced from publicly available pollution monitors as the Telangana Pollution Control Board monitors were out of order as the air pollution was rising. By 10 p.m. the TSPCB’s University of Hyderabad monitoring station was offline.

The air had a metallic sulphurous smell in many areas as the crackers went off one after the other. “For the first time in Hyderabad, I’m experiencing air pollution this bad. My eyes are burning, the air is thick with the stench of burnt chemicals and gunpowder, and breathing itself feels uncomfortable. It’s only 10 PM. The entire colony is still out, relentlessly bursting crackers. The roads are covered in the remains of firecrackers, and this photograph captures barely a fraction of the mess,” wrote one social media user.
The high AQI recordings were almost evenly spread through the city as a 20 degree celsius wind blew from the north-eastern direction.
The air pollution hit a peak at 9.30 p.m. before slowly dropping down through the night. At 11.30 p.m. when the average AQI in Hyderabad was 442, Serilingampally recorded a high of 666.
By morning it still remained hazardous at 178 AQI with PM 10 reaching 113 μg/m³.

articles.title: NDA seals YSRCP’s fate in rural local body polls by winning 499 ZPTC and 5,861 MPTC seats
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: State Election Commission set the stage for elections to Gram Panchayats in three phases i.e on November 26 and 29 and December 2, for which the Commission will issue notifications on November 13, 16 and 19

The NDA partners TDP, Jana Sena Party (JSP) and BJP sealed the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP)’s fate in the elections to 582 Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituencies (ZPTCs) by winning 499 (TDP 406, JSP 73 and BJP 20) seats confining the YSRCP to 76 seats.

In the elections to 7,768 Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies (MPTCs), TDP won 4,806, JSP 938 and BJP 117 (total 5,861). YSRCP won 1,711 MPTCs, CPI (M) 15, Congress 9 and Bhajuan Samaj Party 3.

Meanwhile, the State Election Commission set the stage for elections to Gram Panchayats in three phases i.e on November 26 and 29 and December 2, for which the Commission will issue notifications on November 13, 16 and 19.

The SEC announced the lifting of the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) in 100 Urban Local Bodies (Municipal Corporations and Municipalities) following the completion of elections to them. However, the MCC is in force in the rural areas where elections are due on the given dates.

articles.title: Deepavali 2026: All you need to know about Supreme Court-permitted time slots, green crackers and other directives
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court permitted the bursting of certified green firecrackers between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and between 8 p.m. and 10 p.m. on November 7 and November 8, 2026 in Delhi-NCR

The Supreme Court on November 2, 2026 described bursting of firecrackers during Deepavali as a “religious practice” while permitting the use of green firecrackers for two days, on November 7 and November 8, in Delhi-NCR.

The unregulated use of firecrackers during Deepavali has historically led to a sharp rise in the Air Quality Index (AQI) and pollution levels, including the emission of particulate matter, the court observed. “The right of an individual to engage in a particular practice, which may have a religious colour, is only a qualified one and cannot go beyond the Constitutional restrictions,” the Supreme Court held.

The state had “utterly failed” to comply with the Supreme Court’s orders issued since 2015 to impose restrictions on fireworks, the Bench said. In fact, the situation had not improved even after the reimposition of a complete ban on firecrackers. A significant spike in AQI levels was noticed on Dasara and the following day. The “complete ban” had not only facilitated the illegal sale of firecrackers but had also prevented people from purchasing authorised green crackers, the court said.
The court had earlier suggested that the government enlist celebrities such as cricketer Virat Kohli to spread awareness about the harmful effects of firecrackers.

In October 2025, the apex court had permitted the sale and bursting of green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR during Deepavali, subject to conditions aimed at balancing tradition with environmental and health concerns. The court had then made it clear that the use of green crackers would be restricted to specified hours on the festival day and its eve.

The court permitted the bursting of certified green firecrackers between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and between 8 p.m. and 10 p.m. on November 7, 2026 and the day after in the Delhi National Capital Region (Delhi-NCR).

“There shall not be any bursting of fireworks within a 300-metre radius of hospitals, nursing homes, primary and district health centres, old age homes and any notified silence zones. These areas will be declared as ‘no-cracker zones’, and shall be marked on the ground and published,” the court said in its 23-page order. The same restriction would apply to educational institutions.

“We are conscious that the celebration of Deepavali has a religious, social, psychological and emotional connotation amongst people, creating a positive atmosphere of hope, welfare and prosperity. That being said, allowing the environment to degrade, which results in a health hazard to all living beings, defeats the very purpose of the festivities, and the celebrations would be rendered nugatory,” the Bench reasoned.

In a series of directions, the court ordered that only manufacturers certified by CSIR-NEERI (Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute) and PESO (Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation) would be permitted to manufacture green crackers between November 2, 2026 and November 6, 2026. The cracker boxes would be sealed and kept separate from unauthorised or conventional firecrackers.

There would be no manufacture or sale of firecrackers joined in series ( ladi s) and garlands. Only firecrackers carrying product-specific QR codes would be allowed to be sold. Cancelled licences of traders would be restored temporarily from November 4, 2026 to November 6, 2026. Manufacturers and traders of firecrackers in Delhi-NCR must furnish a monetary security deposit, the amount of which would be determined by the authorities.

articles.title: Oil falls as Donald Trump says new Iran attacks ‘unlikely’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: On November 8, 2026, ​Iraq reached an understanding with the U.S. to allow Iraqi oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz via ⁠a shipping lane near Oman

Oil prices fell at Monday’s (November 9, 2026) open after U.S. President ​Donald Trump said he was highly unlikely to order new Iran ‌attackswhile talks to end the conflict make progress, despite both ​nations’ reports of attacks on ships in or near ⁠the Strait of Hormuz.
Brent was down 84 cents, or 0.85%, to $97.48 a barrel by 0138 GMT, while West Texas Intermediate fell 32 cents, or ‌0.35%, to $90.51 a barrel.

The fall reversed minor gains made on Friday’s (November 6, 2026) settlement as the market assessed the ‌possibility of further U.S. strikes on Iran, although Brent fell ‌17% ⁠last week, the steepest weekly drop since the start ⁠of the COVID pandemic and the biggest in absolute terms, according to LSEG data dating back to 1988.
“It depends on whether or not they sign ​a very strong agreement,” Trump ‌told CNN in a phone interview. “The answer is, highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary.”

Mr. Trump had hinted at renewing attacks on Iran after last week’s U.S. midterm elections , but there has ‌been no sign of a large-scale U.S. military operation. ​Iran has said it would respond by striking U.S. and Israeli targets.

Oil is headed for a glut again as recovering West Asian oil flows, rising production from other countries and weak demand have pushed global supply above consumption, JPMorgan said in a report on Friday (November 6, 2026), estimating a surplus of 1.1 million barrels ‌per day in September, widening to 1.4 million bpd in October.

On Sunday (November 8, 2026), ​Iraq reached an understanding with the U.S. to allow Iraqi oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz via ⁠a shipping lane near Oman, Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said in an ⁠interview with Al Jazeera.
He said Iraq’s losses from the Iran war and disruptions to oil exports had reached $60 ‌billion.
Separately the Houthis claimed responsibility for an attack on Saudi Aramco’s offices in the capital Riyadh on Sunday that left windows ​blown out but no reported casualties.

articles.title: G7 Ministers meet on efforts to end Ukraine conflict, halt new Iran war
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Ministers from the leading industrialised nations of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States will be gathering with preoccupations strikingly similar to those of the last such meeting in March

Foreign Ministers of the G7 group meet in Paris from Monday (November 9, 2026) for two days of talks expected to see European powers press the United States to seek a fair settlement for Ukraine in the war against Russia and deter Washington from further military action against Iran .

Ministers from the leading industrialised nations of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States will be gathering with preoccupations strikingly similar to those of the last such meeting in March.

Russia’s war against Ukraine following the February 2022 full-scale invasion of its neighbour is grinding towards its fifth anniversary. And Washington is still not ruling out new attacks against Iran even after the defeat of President Donald Trump’s Republicans in the midterms .
All eyes will be on U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio who is due to attend both days, unlike the March meeting where he only came for one.

This G7 ministerial meeting, one of the final acts of the French G7 presidency that saw President Emmanuel Macron host Donald Trump for the leaders’ summit this summer in the lakeside resort of Evian, had long been scheduled to be held in the southern port city of Marseille.
But at the last minute the event was moved to Paris, with only scheduling reasons given for the change.

The visit by Mr. Rubio — seen by U.S. media as a potential candidate to succeed Mr. Trump — will be his first abroad since the midterms. Washington will also in 2027 take over the G7 presidency from France.

The meeting coincides with U.S.-mediated talks with Moscow and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi scheduled for Tuesday (November 10, 2026) and Wednesday (November 11, 2026) on ending the Ukraine war, with Europe concerned Kyiv must not be forced to accept disadvantageous conditions.
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot told RTL radio that on this occasion “Europeans will be represented and France will be in Abu Dhabi to participate in these talks”.
Mr. Trump stoked fears of a U.S. pivot toward the Kremlin by predicting a “very big” deal with Russia involving not only the Ukraine war but “all of Europe”.

articles.title: Air pollution over 60 times WHO limit in parts of Delhi as people defy ban on firecrackers on Deepavali
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Data on air pollution missing from several monitoring stations of the Delhi Government at the peak of air pollution during the intervening night of November 8 and 9

As Delhiites burst firecrackers well past the 10 p.m. deadline set by the Supreme Court for Deepavali night, PM2.5 levels in parts of the city soared to 66 times the World Health Organization’s (WHO) recommended 24-hour guideline, before gradually declining in the early hours of Monday (November 9, 2026), according to official data.

However, at the peak of pollution following the bursting of firecrackers on Sunday (November 8) night, data from several monitoring stations operated by the Delhi Government’s Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) were unavailable for hours. This raises the possibility that the actual spike in pollution could have been higher.

Data was unavailable for several hours at multiple stations, including Anand Vihar, R.K. Puram, and Bawana, according to the DPCC website. Data from some other stations had also not been updated since Sunday (November 8) night.
Deepavali 2026: All you need to know about Supreme Court-permitted time slots, green crackers and other directives

According to DPCC data, the PM2.5 concentration in Punjabi Bagh stood at 993 micrograms per cubic metre at 4 a.m. on Monday (November 9) — about 66.2 times the WHO’s recommended 24-hour guideline of 15 micrograms per cubic metre.

In Vivek Vihar, the PM2.5 concentration was 873 micrograms per cubic metre at 2 a.m. on Monday (November 9), about 58.2 times the WHO guideline. In R.K. Puram, it stood at 924 micrograms per cubic metre at 10 p.m. on Sunday (November 8), about 61.6 times the guideline.

PM2.5 refers to fine inhalable particulate matter measuring 2.5 micrometres or less in diameter. These particles can penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream, potentially causing respiratory and other health problems.

Although the Supreme Court had permitted only green firecrackers during specified time windows on November 7 and 8, traditional firecrackers, which are more polluting, were also available in Delhi markets.

Delhi’s overall air quality remained in the ‘very poor’ category on Monday (November 9) morning, while several parts of the city continued to record ‘severe’ pollution levels, according to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data.
‘Severe’ air pollution affects healthy people and can seriously impact those with existing diseases, the CPCB says.

articles.title: Maharashtra relaxes borewell restrictions till December 15 to help farmers save trees amid drought
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The announcement came during an interaction with village sarpanches and local representatives at Lohari Sawanga in Nagpur district’s Narkhed taluka, where the Chief Minister had stayed overnight on November 7 to celebrate Deepavali with a farmer’s family

Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Sunday (November 8, 2026) announced a temporary relaxation of restrictions on drilling new borewells and deepening existing ones until December 15 to help farmers save trees amid drought conditions. The relaxation, however, will not be applicable across the board, and farmers will be required to obtain prior permission from the authorities.

The announcement came during an interaction with village sarpanches and local representatives at Lohari Sawanga in Nagpur district’s Narkhed taluka, where the Chief Minister had stayed overnight on Saturday (November 7) to celebrate Deepavali with a farmer’s family.
During the interaction, local representatives raised concerns over the prevailing drought conditions and the possibility of standing crops being destroyed due to water scarcity.

Responding to their concerns, Mr. Fadnavis said that lifting restrictions on drilling new borewells or deepening existing ones posed certain difficulties for the government. However, considering the prevailing drought situation, the government had decided to permit such activities as a special measure wherever necessary to save trees.

He clarified that the relaxation would be granted only in cases where it was essential to protect trees and would not amount to a blanket lifting of the restrictions. He also urged citizens to conserve water and undertake groundwater recharge measures.

The announcement follows an assurance given by the Chief Minister on Saturday (November 7), during his interaction with farmer Rambhau Balpande, at whose residence he stayed overnight. Mr. Fadnavis had then said the government would permit borewell drilling wherever feasible to help farmers cope with the drought.

During Sunday’s (November 8) interaction, several local representatives also raised concerns about the absence of veterinary hospitals in the region despite its substantial livestock population. The Chief Minister directed the Zilla Parishad Chief Executive Officer to assess the situation and take an immediate decision regarding veterinary facilities.

Addressing delays in projects under the Jal Jeevan Mission, Mr. Fadnavis acknowledged that several works remained incomplete due to inadequate funding. He said projects that had achieved more than 75% completion would be provided funds on priority to ensure their early completion, while the remaining projects would be completed in phases.

The Chief Minister also expressed concern over crop damage caused by wild animals and announced that the existing fencing scheme would be expanded, with particular priority given to agricultural fields adjoining forest areas.
He further said desilting works had been undertaken in water bodies in view of the drought, with the excavated silt being used to improve agricultural land.

articles.title: Modernist artist Arpita Singh, aged 89, passes away
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Arpita Singh received the Padma Bhushan in 2011 and the Lalit Kala Akademi Fellowship in 2014 for her contribution to the world of art

Modernist artist Arpita Singh, widely known for her detailed figurative works, died here at Fortis Hospital from age-related ailments on Monday (November 9, 2026), her husband and artist Paramjit Singh told PTI.
"She had heart and lung related issues for some years now. However, she was actively working. Her health dipped in the last three days and was admitted to the hospital," Paramjit added.
Her cremation will be held at 2 p.m. at Lodhi Crematorium on Sunday (November 15, 2026) .
She is survived by her husband. Their only daughter, also an artist, Anjum Singh died in 2020 from cancer.
Ms. Singh is known for her extensive body of figurative work, generally centred around a female figure, that was reflective of social upheaval and humanitarian crises of her times.
She received the Padma Bhushan in 2011 and the Lalit Kala Akademi Fellowship in 2014 for her contribution to the world of art.

Art curator Uma Nair called Singh the "high priestess of contemporary Indian art" and the "female M F Husain of the female arc". She noted that the beauty of her work was in the way how she "wove violence and chaos and patriarchal mores all so softly.

"The power of the narrative was her elixir, where the world becomes a quilt of characters who play their own parts... Her work in the early days at the Weavers Centre gave her an imagery that created connotations in textile in contemporary discourse," Nair wrote.

She added that her ability to balance the human figures with predominantly abstract compositions on canvas and paper, "show her precision and harmonic balance created principally with a reliance on contours so as to lay the formal foundations of her oeuvre to create an aesthetic bridge to her evolution".

"Her essence has been a serious curiosity about form, depth and space, and a playful improvisation — a willingness to suspend certainty in her search for the novel in terms of life’s leanings," Nair said.

Ms. Singh is known for her extensive body of figurative work, generally centred around a female figure, that was reflective of social upheaval and humanitarian crises of her times.

She received the Padma Bhushan in 2011 and the Lalit Kala Akademi Fellowship in 2014 for her contribution to the world of art.

Art curator Uma Nair called Singh the "high priestess of contemporary Indian art" and the "female M F Husain of the female arc". She noted that the beauty of her work was in the way how she "wove violence and chaos and patriarchal mores all so softly.

"The power of the narrative was her elixir, where the world becomes a quilt of characters who play their own parts... Her work in the early days at the Weavers Centre gave her an imagery that created connotations in textile in contemporary discourse," Nair wrote.

She added that her ability to balance the human figures with predominantly abstract compositions on canvas and paper, "show her precision and harmonic balance created principally with a reliance on contours so as to lay the formal foundations of her oeuvre to create an aesthetic bridge to her evolution".

articles.title: Delhi air pollution: AAP slams Delhi govt for alleged air quality data ‘manipulation’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Last week, the AAP had accused the BJP government of “manipulating” AQI data by spraying water on monitoring stations, and alleged that “fudging” AQI data was not just corruption but life-threatening

The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Monday (November 9, 2026) morning attacked the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in Delhi over alleged air quality data “manipulation” by shutting down of air quality monitoring stations.

“The government which shuts down air quality monitoring stations on the night of Diwali, the government that does data fraud, how will you trust such a government?” asked AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj in a video posted on X.

As Delhiites burst firecrackers well past the 10 p.m. deadline set by the Supreme Court for Deepavali night, PM2.5 levels in parts of the city soared to 66 times the World Health Organization’s (WHO) recommended 24-hour guideline, before gradually declining in the early hours of Monday (November 9, 2026), according to official data.

However, at the peak of pollution following the bursting of firecrackers on Sunday (November 8) night, data from several monitoring stations operated by the Delhi Government’s Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) were unavailable for hours. This raises the possibility that the actual spike in pollution could have been higher.

“The government is doing the fraud openly. We had written to the CAQM and CPCB (about the data manipulation). But everyone is silent. This is because everyone is part of this fraud,” Mr. Bharadwaj said.

Last week, the AAP had accused the BJP government of “manipulating” AQI data by spraying water on monitoring stations, and alleged that“fudging” AQI data was not just corruption but life-threatening. The party also wrote to CAQM and CPCB last week, alleging that the Delhi government was manipulating air quality data in the national capital.

articles.title: Kozhikode police arrest man in extortion, impersonation cases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The suspect, T. Nishad, was arrested from Kondotty in Malappuram district

The Kozhikode City police have arrested a 34-year-old man in connection with an ongoing investigation into a series of incidents involving extortion, criminal intimidation and impersonation. The suspect, T. Nishad, was arrested from Kondotty in Malappuram district on Sunday evening.

According to the First Information Report (FIR) registered at the Medical College police station here, the accused has been charged under Sections 308(2) and 204 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The police said he was a habitual offender, with multiple cases registered against him under the jurisdictions of the Kondotty and Manjeri police stations.

His criminal history includes cases registered at the Kondotty police station under Sections 21(b) and 29(1) of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, Section 151 of the CrPC, Section 27(b) of the NDPS Act, and Section 170 of the BNS. He also faces a case registered at the Manjeri police station under Section 118(a) of the Kerala Police Act.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has requested a new passport to facilitate her return from exile two years after she was ousted in a mass uprising
F ormer Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina requested a new passport on Monday (November 9, 2026) to facilitate her r eturn from exile two years after she was ousted in a mass uprising.

The government has been seeking her extradition from India and earlier dismissed suggestions she needed new identification documents to return home. Ms. Hasina told The Associated Press in an interview this month that she would return to Bangladesh in December at any cost.

In a letter seen by The Associated Press that was emailed to Bangladesh's top diplomat in London, a counsel of Ms. Hasina urged the diplomat to take necessary action to provide her a passport and national identity card.

“This is a significant step toward her homecoming. Having had her documents revoked by the previous regime, Her Excellency looks forward to reclaiming her fundamental rights as a Bangladeshi citizen and receiving the necessary documents,” Abu Obaidha Arin, an aide to Ms.. Hasina, told the AP .
“She is determined to return to Bangladesh by December, and she will undoubtedly return home,” he said.
It was not immediately possible to obtain comment from the Bangladesh government.

On Thursday (November 5, 2026), Junior Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said Bangladesh wants Ms. Hasina to be handed over under an extradition treaty with India. India has declined to hand her over.
“We want Hasina to be handed over. She will be handed over. She is a terrorist. She is a fugitive. There is an active extradition treaty between Bangladesh and India,” he told reporters in Dhaka.

Bangladesh's military sent Ms. Hasina to India after student-led protests forced her from power on Aug. 5, 2024. A special tribunal in 2025 sentenced her to death for crimes against humanity, ruling that she was responsible for ordering the crackdown, which left hundreds of people dead and thousands of others injured.
The United Nations has said nearly 1,400 people were killed. Ms. Hasina denies any wrongdoing. She also has rejected the tribunal’s verdict and challenged the legitimacy of the trial.

articles.title: Who is Stephen Miller, Trump’s new Chief of Staff?
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Stephen Miller, one of U.S. President Donald Trump’s closest aides for decades, will replace Susie Wiles, who becomes the first major White House casualty from the Democratic landslide earlier this week

U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday (November 6, 2026) named Stephen Miller, architect of his hardline immigration policy, as his new Chief of Staff, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback after Republicans were hammered in the midterms.

Ultra-loyalist Miller, 41, will replace Susie Wiles, who becomes the first major White House casualty from the Democratic landslide earlier this week . In a post on Truth Social announcing Mr. Miller’s appointment, Mr. Trump described him as “one of my most trusted advisors”.

Stephen Miller, a key member of Mr. Trump’s inner circle, is a prominent architect of the administration’s hardline immigration policies. Known for his sharp suits and sunglasses, Miller has been one of Mr. Trump’s closest aides for decades and longest-serving advisers, pushing nativist policies that gelled with the President’s “America First” agenda.

Mr. Miller currently serves as White House Deputy Chief of Staff and though he has a wide-ranging portfolio, he is most closely aligned with the President’s immigration policy and rhetoric on immigration. He is also a former aide to hardliner former Sen. Jeff Sessions, R-Ala., who would go on to serve as Mr. Trump’s first Attorney General.

Mr. Miller was raised in politically liberal Santa Monica, California, but developed a reputation as a combative conservative as a columnist at Duke University’s student newspaper. ⁠As a congressional aide in the 2010s, he was an early advocate for restricting immigration at a time when that was not a mainstream position in the Republican Party.

He joined Mr. Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign, then served ‌as an advisor and speechwriter in his first 2017-2021 term. After Mr. Trump lost the 2020 election, Mr. Miller founded the conservative advocacy group America First Legal, filing complaints that accused companies ‌such as Nike of discriminating against white people.
His wife, Katie Miller, is a conservative podcaster and former ⁠communications aide in Mr. Trump’s first administration.
As Mr. Trump’s Deputy Chief of Staff for policy and homeland security advisor, he was the brains behind the mass deportation programme that defined the first year of the President’s second term.

Mr. Miller is best known for driving the immigration crackdown, setting a target of 3,000 arrests per day — far above levels under previous administrations. He has pushed U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to target anybody in the country illegally, ‌not just those with criminal records.
But he faced widespread criticism after the deadly shootings of two protesters by immigration agents in Minneapolis in January — incidents that sparked mass demonstrations.

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

Stephen Miller, one of U.S. President Donald Trump’s closest aides for decades, will replace Susie Wiles, who becomes the first major White House casualty from the Democratic landslide earlier this week

U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday (November 6, 2026) named Stephen Miller, architect of his hardline immigration policy, as his new Chief of Staff, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback after Republicans were hammered in the midterms.

Ultra-loyalist Miller, 41, will replace Susie Wiles, who becomes the first major White House casualty from the Democratic landslide earlier this week . In a post on Truth Social announcing Mr. Miller’s appointment, Mr. Trump described him as “one of my most trusted advisors”.

Stephen Miller, a key member of Mr. Trump’s inner circle, is a prominent architect of the administration’s hardline immigration policies. Known for his sharp suits and sunglasses, Miller has been one of Mr. Trump’s closest aides for decades and longest-serving advisers, pushing nativist policies that gelled with the President’s “America First” agenda.

Mr. Miller currently serves as White House Deputy Chief of Staff and though he has a wide-ranging portfolio, he is most closely aligned with the President’s immigration policy and rhetoric on immigration. He is also a former aide to hardliner former Sen. Jeff Sessions, R-Ala., who would go on to serve as Mr. Trump’s first Attorney General.

Mr. Miller was raised in politically liberal Santa Monica, California, but developed a reputation as a combative conservative as a columnist at Duke University’s student newspaper. ⁠As a congressional aide in the 2010s, he was an early advocate for restricting immigration at a time when that was not a mainstream position in the Republican Party.

He joined Mr. Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign, then served ‌as an advisor and speechwriter in his first 2017-2021 term. After Mr. Trump lost the 2020 election, Mr. Miller founded the conservative advocacy group America First Legal, filing complaints that accused companies ‌such as Nike of discriminating against white people.

His wife, Katie Miller, is a conservative podcaster and former ⁠communications aide in Mr. Trump’s first administration.

As Mr. Trump’s Deputy Chief of Staff for policy and homeland security advisor, he was the brains behind the mass deportation programme that defined the first year of the President’s second term.

Mr. Miller is best known for driving the immigration crackdown, setting a target of 3,000 arrests per day — far above levels under previous administrations. He has pushed U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to target anybody in the country illegally, ‌not just those with criminal records.

But he faced widespread criticism after the deadly shootings of two protesters by immigration agents in Minneapolis in January — incidents that sparked mass demonstrations.

Eight people have tested positive for Shigella infection in Malappuram district, with five cases linked to a wedding feast at Korakkuthu in Elamkulam panchayat near Perinthalmanna.
The outbreak has prompted the Health department to step up surveillance and preventive measures in the area.

The five patients attended a wedding held on October 31, 2026, in ward 12 of Elamkulam panchayat. Around 80 people who attended the function have since reported symptoms of diarrhoea. A child from the area is also suspected to have Shigella infection and is under special observation.

The other confirmed cases include a four-year-old girl who ate food from a snack shop at 5th Mile at Amarambalam near Nilambur, and two people who ate mandi rice from a restaurant at Palunda near Chungathara, Nilambur.

The Food Safety department has collected samples of food and drinking water served at the wedding and sent them for testing. Stool samples of those affected will be examined at the laboratory at Government Medical College, Manjeri.

A special health team has begun surveillance and field-level interventions. The Health department has advised people to drink boiled and cooled water and eat properly cooked food. Drinking water sources should also be superchlorinated using bleaching powder, said health officials.

The health authorities, in coordination with the panchayat, will intensify inspections at local establishments and public functions. Event organisers have been asked to follow public health guidelines.

articles.title: FSSAI seizes 3,280 tonne food items, cancels 52 licences in nationwide inspection drive
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The regulator said it inspected 56,431 food establishments during its nationwide enforcement drive between September 1 and November 5, and seized non-compliant food products, including paneer, ghee, milk and sweets

Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has seized 3,280 tonnes of 'banned and non-compliant' food products worth ₹82 crore during its nationwide inspection drive, which began on September 1 to check adulteration during the festive season.
Acting against food safety violations, the FSSAI cancelled 52 licences, suspended 1,133 licences, and sealed 314 establishments.
In a social media post on Saturday (November 7, 2026), the FSSAI said that it has stepped up vigilance in view of festivals.

The regulator said it inspected 56,431 food establishments during its nationwide enforcement drive between September 1 and November 5, and seized non-compliant food products, including paneer, ghee, milk and sweets.

FSSAI led an intensive nationwide inspection drive across States and UTs. Through rigorous checks on over 56,000 food establishments, authorities took decisive action against substandard practices-issuing over 10000 improvement notices and suspending more than 1,100 licences 1(2) https://t.co/Ov7iIZcmdA
A total of 3,279.57 tonnes of 'banned and non-compliant' food products worth ₹81.80 crore were seized, it said.
Additionally, the regulator issued 10,047 improvement notices to food business operators.
This calendar year, the FSSAI has stepped up enforcement actions against food business operators and e-commerce companies to ensure safe food for consumers.

articles.title: At 1,152, Punjab records season’s biggest single-day jump in farm fires on Deepavali
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The latest figures indicate a significant rise in crop residue burning despite government advisories, enforcement measures and monetary penalties aimed at discouraging the practice
Punjab witnessed its sharpest single-day spike in paddy stubble-burning incidents this season on Deepavali, with 1,152 farm fires reported across the State, according to official data.
This pushed the State's total count from 3,307 on November 7 to 4,459 on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
The highest number of farm fires this season has been reported from Tarn Taran at 654, the data showed.
The latest figures indicate a significant rise in crop residue burning despite government advisories, enforcement measures and monetary penalties aimed at discouraging the practice.
The annual farm fire monitoring period begins on September 15, two weeks before paddy procurement starts on October 1.

With 194 fires, Sangrur recorded the highest number of stubble-burning incidents on Sunday (November 8), taking its seasonal tally to 488. Ferozepur reported 157 incidents, bringing its total to 592; and Bathinda added 132 cases, taking its count to 406.
Patiala recorded 92 fresh farm fires, raising its cumulative tally to 288. Barnala reported 91 new incidents and Ludhiana 71.

The data showed that till Sunday (November 8), enforcement agencies had registered 884 FIRs under Section 223 (disobedience of orders promulgated by a public servant) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and marked 1,017 red entries in land revenue records against farmers found burning stubble.
Fines totalling over ₹62 lakh have been imposed as environmental compensation in 1,228 cases of stubble burning, with over ₹32 lakh already recovered.

Recently, taking a serious view of the "very high" number of farm fires in Punjab, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) held a meeting with senior bureaucrats and police officers from 12 districts to review steps to prevent stubble burning.

articles.title: CM Suvendu defends encounter in Raiganj, says police entitled to retaliate in self-defence
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The CM’s comments came hours after a man accused of raping and murdering his 13-year-old niece in Raiganj was killed in an exchange of fire with police

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday (November 9, 2026) defended the killing of a rape-murder accused in an exchange of fire with police in Uttar Dinajpur district’s Raiganj, pointing out that personnel of the force were entitled to retaliate in self-defence.

Talking to reporters in Digha in Purba Medinipur district, the Chief Minister said his government has given police considerable operational freedom in dealing with certain offences, including rape and murder, drug trafficking and illegal infiltration from Bangladesh.

The accused, Dilip Roy, allegedly opened fire at a police team conducting a raid to arrest him in a village in Raiganj, police said. An officer said police fired in retaliation, injuring the accused. He was taken to Raiganj Medical College and Hospital, where he was declared dead.
"Do police shoot every accused? When someone attacks police, they retaliate in self-defence," he said.

"The government has given the police a free hand in certain cases, including rape and murder, drug trafficking and illegal infiltration from Bangladesh. They have also been told that they need not wait for permission from their superiors to act in such cases. There is absolutely zero tolerance towards these offences," Mr. Adhikari said.
The Chief Minister also said he had instructed police to take stringent action against anyone throwing stones during religious programmes.

Claiming that no one had dared to disrupt religious processions, idol immersions or other religious events since the BJP came to power in West Bengal, he alleged that the previous Left Front and TMC had undermined Bengal's culture, religious practices and traditions during their rule.

The Raiganj incident is the fourth reported police encounter death in West Bengal since the BJP came to power in May. In July, Prabhas Mondal, accused of raping and murdering an 11-year-old girl in Baruipur, South 24 Parganas district, was killed in a police encounter.

On October 27, two other accused — Prahlad Das, arrested in connection with the recovery of a Class 11 student's body in North 24 Parganas district's Gaighata, and Samaul Haque, accused of murdering a BJP worker in Murshidabad's Samserganj — were killed in separate police firing incidents.

articles.title: Delhi AQI row: AAP alleges data fraud, BJP fires back over Punjab stubble ‘conspiracy’
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: When asked about air quality data in Delhi missing in several monitoring stations, Kapil Mishra said that the government will look into the issue within an hour and inform the media about it

BJP leader and Delhi Labour Minister Kapil Mishra on Monday (November 9, 2026) alleged that there was a “conspiracy” in AAP-governed Punjab to set stubble on fire in Punjab on Sunday (November 8, 2026) evening, as per official data.

He alleged that 1,200 stubble burning incidents happened in Punjab on Sunday (November 8, 2026) evening, which was 10 times that of previous days. “We got calls from farmers in Punjab that stubble is being set on fire. Someone is coming and setting stubble on fire and running away, when farmers are celebrating Diwali with their families. This is a very serious issue and a conspiracy against Delhi, Punjab, and farmers,” he said.

Earlier in the day, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) attacked the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in Delhi over alleged air quality data “manipulation” by shutting down of air quality monitoring stations.

“The government which shuts down air quality monitoring stations on the night of Diwali, the government that does data fraud, how will you trust such a government?” asked AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj in a video posted on X.

“The government is doing the fraud openly. We had written to the CAQM and CPCB (about the data manipulation). But everyone is silent. This is because everyone is part of this fraud,” Mr. Bharadwaj said.

Last week, the AAP had accused the BJP government of “manipulating” AQI data by spraying water on monitoring stations, and alleged that“fudging” AQI data was not just corruption but life-threatening. The party also wrote to CAQM and CPCB last week, alleging that the Delhi government was manipulating air quality data in the national capital.
When asked about air quality data in Delhi missing in several monitoring stations, Mr. Mishra said that the government will look into the issue within an hour and inform the media about it.

At the peak of pollution following the bursting of firecrackers on Sunday (November 8, 2026) night, data from several monitoring stations operated by the Delhi Government’s Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) were unavailable for hours. This raises the possibility that the actual spike in pollution could have been higher.
Reading from 11:00 a.m. on November 9, 2026, from website of Department of Environment, Government of NCT of Delhi, showing several stations not reporting AQI data.

On Deepavali night, PM2.5 levels in parts of the city soared to 66 times the World Health Organization’s (WHO) recommended 24-hour guideline, before gradually declining in the early hours of Monday (November 9, 2026), according to official data.
