articles.title: Revised MRPs of 1,364 anti-cancer formulations come into effect; consumers to save ₹3,540 crore/year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the Ministry, 85 pharmaceutical companies have reported revised MRPs for 1,364 anti-cancer formulations across 121 drugs as of November 8, 2026

Revised Maximum Retail Prices (MRPs) of 1,364 anti-cancer formulations have come into effect from Monday (November 9, 2026), a move projected to save consumers an estimated ₹3,540.38 crore annually, according to an official release.

The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), functioning under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, capped trade margins on the MRP of 137 anti-cancer drugs based on recommendations submitted on October 17, 2026, by an Expert Committee constituted by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare.
According to the Ministry, 85 pharmaceutical companies have reported revised MRPs for 1,364 anti-cancer formulations across 121 drugs as of November 8, 2026.

Price reductions of over 50% have been reported for 679 brands, with the highest price cut recorded at 96.45%, the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers: Department of Pharmaceuticals said in the release.
The Ministry stated that no chemist or hospital pharmacy is permitted to charge more than the revised MRP.
Consumers can verify medicine rates via the revised MRP printed on packs, the 'Pharma Sahi Daam' mobile application, or the official NPPA website (nppa.gov.in), it said.

Consumers can lodge complaints against instances of overcharging or other pricing-related issues through the Pharma Jan Samadhan portal or contact the NPPA helpline at 1800-111-255, the release added.
Are lower MRPs on cancer drugs translating into affordable care? | In Focus Podcast

fullParagraphs: Proposed reforms seek to move beyond conventional, examination-orientated degrees towards interdisciplinary learning, industry exposure, research and emerging technologies

Andhra Pradesh is planning a comprehensive restructuring of postgraduate (PG) education across its 28 State universities, with an emphasis on employability, research, entrepreneurship and regional development. The proposed reforms seek to transform universities from institutions offering largely conventional, discipline-based postgraduate courses into specialised regional knowledge hubs aligned with the State’s economic priorities and emerging global opportunities.

The restructuring proposal, prepared by the Andhra Pradesh State Council of Higher Education (APSCHE), envisages a common academic framework for postgraduate programmes while allowing individual universities to develop distinctive areas of specialisation based on their geographical location, institutional strengths, available faculty and regional requirements.

articles.title: Prashant Kishore’s Brahminical criticism of BJP’s Hindutva
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Jan Suraaj party founder urges Brahmins in Bihar’s Mithila to rethink BJP Hindutva, linking secularism, social justice, and Muslim-OBC political coalitions

Secularism is a modern, constitutional principle. In real-world politics, the manifestation of this principle is tested against a rather narrow yardstick: the fair representation of religious minorities, particularly Muslims. Generally speaking, the English-speaking secularists are unaware of the caste dynamics that come into play in the field operation of representative politics, and they are also resistant to the idea of discussing caste as a determinant.

The intersection of caste representation and religious representation mirrors the intersection of social justice and secularism in electoral politics. The caste dynamics of politics are often manifested as critiques by non-Brahmins against Brahminism. A Brahmin perspective on these dynamics is rare, and that is the reason why Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor’s address to fellow Brahmins in Bihar ’s Mithila region is an extremely valuable opportunity to peer into the emerging thinking within the community. He said BJP’s Hindu communalism, which excludes Muslims from electoral calculations, has cost the Brahmins heavily and asked them to rethink their position.

fullParagraphs: Public details are sparse about the woman, also known as Huang Le, who had reportedly been a top figure at a Singapore-based data centre company called Megaspeed International
Tech executive Alice Huang is the woman accused of spying for China during an affair with Jensen Huang , head of U.S. artificial intelligence chip titan Nvidia, according to media reports.
Public details are sparse about the woman, also known as Huang Le, who had reportedly been a top figure at a Singapore-based data centre company called Megaspeed International.

Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on the Nvidia boss, according to the New York Times, which first reported that Jensen Huang was the alleged target of a spy plot.
Despite their shared surname, Alice Huang is no relation to the 63-year-old Taiwanese-born head of the world’s most valuable company.
The Times, citing people briefed on the surveillance, said that Alice Huang speaks good English and is well connected at the highest level of the global AI chip industry.
The sector is highly sensitive as the United States and China race to develop advanced AI systems with potential military applications.

An online search brought up a short profile for Alice Huang, with her photo, on a Chinese fund database. It listed previous jobs including at HSBC bank, and as a reporter for Chinese media outlets CCTV and Hunan TV.
AFP was unable to verify the contents of the profile, or who had written it, but has attempted to contact the companies cited.
Media reports last week said they had a close relationship, and Jensen Huang told Nvidia employees on Sunday he was “deeply sorry” for being “unfaithful to my wife”.
One photo from an industry party in 2024, posted on LinkedIn, appears to show the leather jacket-clad Nvidia boss sitting next to a long-haired woman in glitzy jewellery believed to be Alice Huang.

articles.title: Bangladesh Foreign Ministry examining Sheikh Hasina’s request for new passport
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Deposed PM Sheikh Hasina’s passport was cancelled soon after she fled to India in August 2024 following the uprising that toppled her government

The High Commission of Bangladesh has received a request from deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina seeking a fresh passport, a source in Dhaka has informed. The official has said that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Bangladesh is in the process of verifying the letter and will take a decision after internal consultation. Ms. Hasina’s passport was cancelled soon after she escaped to India in August 2024 after an uprising that toppled her government.

“We have received an email from Matrix Chambers, a law firm in London seeking a new passport for Sheikh Hasina. We are currently examining the content of the letter and will take an appropriate step after internal consultation,” said the source speaking to The Hindu over phone.

Ms. Hasina held a press conference on August 5 this year at the Foreign Correspondents Club where she had expressed her plans to return to Bangladesh in December. The announcement was followed by repeated assertion by the Awami League’s leaders who are based in India that Ms. Hasina will act on her announcement. As per sources in Awami League, Ms. Hasina may choose to return through one of the land ports with India including Benapole-Petrapole.

Ms Hasina has been living in New Delhi since being overthrown in a student-people uprising in 2024 July-August. The movement started against the abolition of quota system that ensured employment for families of the guerrillas of the 1971 Liberation War.

The movement escalated and turned into a protest against Ms. Hasina after a police crackdown in mid-July 2024 led to death of hundreds of students and common citizens ultimately leading to her escape on August 5 that year. The International Crimes Tribunal, a special tribunal that was constituted in November 2025 delivered a death sentence for Ms. Hasina. The verdict was however criticised later as it was passed without representation from Ms. Hasina or her legal team.

Ms. Hasina has so far refused to apologise for the police crackdown. In a written interview with The Hindu earlier this year, she said, “When police are working in the field, how can they contact the Prime Minister for every action? Police operate under standard operating procedures. They are trained to handle emergencies, crowd control and violent situations. When police personnel were attacked and killed, and police stations were set on fire, they responded according to the situation. How could I personally order officers in those circumstances? 🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

Deposed PM Sheikh Hasina’s passport was cancelled soon after she fled to India in August 2024 following the uprising that toppled her government

The High Commission of Bangladesh has received a request from deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina seeking a fresh passport, a source in Dhaka has informed. The official has said that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Bangladesh is in the process of verifying the letter and will take a decision after internal consultation. Ms. Hasina’s passport was cancelled soon after she escaped to India in August 2024 after an uprising that toppled her government.

“We have received an email from Matrix Chambers, a law firm in London seeking a new passport for Sheikh Hasina. We are currently examining the content of the letter and will take an appropriate step after internal consultation,” said the source speaking to The Hindu over phone.

Ms. Hasina held a press conference on August 5 this year at the Foreign Correspondents Club where she had expressed her plans to return to Bangladesh in December. The announcement was followed by repeated assertion by the Awami League’s leaders who are based in India that Ms. Hasina will act on her announcement. As per sources in Awami League, Ms. Hasina may choose to return through one of the land ports with India including Benapole-Petrapole.

Ms Hasina has been living in New Delhi since being overthrown in a student-people uprising in 2024 July-August. The movement started against the abolition of quota system that ensured employment for families of the guerrillas of the 1971 Liberation War.

The movement escalated and turned into a protest against Ms. Hasina after a police crackdown in mid-July 2024 led to death of hundreds of students and common citizens ultimately leading to her escape on August 5 that year. The International Crimes Tribunal, a special tribunal that was constituted in November 2025 delivered a death sentence for Ms. Hasina. The verdict was however criticised later as it was passed without representation from Ms. Hasina or her legal team.

Ms. Hasina has so far refused to apologise for the police crackdown. In a written interview with The Hindu earlier this year, she said, “When police are working in the field, how can they contact the Prime Minister for every action? Police operate under standard operating procedures. They are trained to handle emergencies, crowd control and violent situations. fullParagraphs: The gunman was wounded in a shootout with police and had been in critical condition in hospital
The alleged perpetrator of a deadly weekend shooting spree in Krakow has died, Polish police said on Monday (November 9, 2026), two days after he was critically wounded in a shootout with officers.

“We inform you that the perpetrator of the tragic events died this morning in the hospital,” regional police said in a post on X of the 24-year-old Polish man who allegedly opened fire on Saturday (November 7, 2026) in central Krakow, killing six people.

Authorities said the man had been “fascinated by far-right ideologies” and Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the shooting — the deadliest in the country since the end of communism in 1989 — an act of “terrorism”.

articles.title: World entering ‘age of climate extremes’: UN chief
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The UN chief statement came as the UN’s World Meteorological Organization released a report indicating that 2026 has continued a streak of exceptional global temperatures, melting ice and rising sea levels

The world is entering a new reality where climate extremes are the norm, the United Nations chief Antonio Guterres warned on Monday (November 9, 2026), urging leaders at the COP31 climate conference in Turkiye to “get serious”.
“A supersized El Nino is colliding with a planet already superheated by manmade climate change,” the UN secretary general said in a statement.

As leaders gathered in Antalya for the UN climate summit, Mr. Guterres called on them to “get serious by cutting emissions faster, accelerating a just transition from fossil fuels and delivering the finance and protection vulnerable countries need”.
His statement came as the UN’s World Meteorological Organization released a report indicating that 2026 has continued a streak of exceptional global temperatures, melting ice and rising sea levels.
Each of the past 12 years have been among the hottest 12 years on record, the agency said, with this year expected to be among the hottest ever.

“What we are seeing gives new meaning to the phrase off the charts,” WMO chief Celeste Saulo told reporters in Geneva, cautioning that the current exceptionally strong El Nino could unleash more heat and extreme weather well into next year.
“We should prepare for another record-breaking year in 2027.”
The global average surface temperature between January and September this year was around 1.47 degrees Celsius above the pre-industrial average, the WMO said.
And this year’s El Nino — expected to be the strongest since 1950 at least — could push the figure higher by the end of the year.

Preliminary data shows 2026 figuring among the four hottest years on record, WMO climate information chief John Kenned told reporters, adding though that “with the El Nina developing, we might see when the final numbers come in that we’re close to the top”.

articles.title: Google says new Australian internet safety bill could cut off under-18s from Gmail
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Online companies ⁠and free speech advocates say the law could give regulators too much discretion to decide what is harmful, placing ​pressure on platforms to ‌take down content

A proposed Australian internet law could force Google to block under-18s from ​using its Gmail service, an Australia-based company policy ‌head said on Monday, underscoring an industry warning ​that the draft regulation risks overreach.

Under ⁠the Digital Duty of Care legislation, which has already passed Australia’s House of Representatives but needs cross-party support to ‌pass the Senate, internet companies must show they are taking steps to weed ‌out harmful content or face a fine ‌of ⁠up to A$109 million ($75.1 million).

Online companies ⁠and free speech advocates say the law could give regulators too much discretion to decide what is harmful, placing ​pressure on platforms to ‌take down content. Google’s warning reflects concern that the law could filter into everyday parts of the internet.

A section of the law ‌requiring age checks if there was a risk ​of a child seeing pornography “could require us to age assure and block ⁠access to everyday communication services like messaging, email and private file storage”, said Rachel Lord, head of ‌policy in Australia and New Zealand for Google’s YouTube streaming website, at a Senate hearing.
“We are talking about potentially intrusive monitoring within private communications or file storage,” she added.

Representatives from Meta, TikTok and Snap voiced similar concerns, warning ‌the bill could chill online communications by allowing regulators ​broad discretion to determine what content or conduct is harmful while replacing some ⁠existing mandatory industry codes.
Several argued the uncertainty created a ⁠risk platforms would over-moderate content to avoid large regulatory penalties.
The government has said a ‌broad set of rules is the only way to ensure a safe internet.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh tightens fireworks safety rules after fatal blasts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Andhra Pradesh government has overhauled its fireworks safety, licensing and enforcement framework following explosions at fireworks manufacturing units in Rayavaram and Vetlapalem, introducing a system of centralised monitoring, risk-based inspections and stricter accountability for enforcement officials.

The reforms were notified through a government order dated November 7, 2026, issued by Chief Secretary G. Sai Prasad, following the findings of inquiry committees, which pointed to fragmented enforcement and inadequate risk-based monitoring.

Under the new framework, the Director-General of the A.P. State Disaster Response and Fire Services has been designated as the State Nodal Authority to coordinate enforcement, conduct monthly inter-departmental reviews and submit compliance reports to the Home Department. District Collectors will function as nodal authorities at the district level, overseeing implementation and quarterly reviews.

The government has also ordered the establishment of a State Explosives and Fireworks Safety Cell within 30 days. It will maintain a digital register of fireworks manufacturing units, prepare risk-based inspection schedules, develop a Fireworks Risk Index and coordinate with the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO).

District Fireworks Safety Committees, headed by Collectors, will include officials from the police, fire services, revenue, factories, labour and pollution control departments. They will review licensed units and emergency preparedness at least once every quarter.

The licensing process for LE-1(a) units will be tightened through a two-stage system, involving provisional approval followed by a mandatory physical inspection after construction. The inspection must be supported by geo-tagged photographs and video evidence.

The government has set a six-month deadline for the RTGS and Information Technology, Electronics and Communications Department to operationalise an integrated online fireworks safety portal. It will track licences, approved layouts, CCTV feeds and stock movements, besides generating alerts on irregularities.

The new framework provides for immediate closure of units, seizure of materials and legal action in cases involving unlicensed operations, unauthorised chemical formulations, excess stock, unapproved equipment and obstruction of inspections.

The government has also made inspecting officers personally accountable for their certifications. Negligent inspections and suppression of violations will be treated as serious professional misconduct, inviting disciplinary and legal action.
The effectiveness of the new framework will depend on whether the prescribed inspections, digital monitoring and interdepartmental coordination translate into consistent enforcement on the ground.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 09 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Andhra Pradesh tightens fireworks safety rules after fatal blasts

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

The Andhra Pradesh government has overhauled its fireworks safety, licensing and enforcement framework following explosions at fireworks manufacturing units in Rayavaram and Vetlapalem, introducing a system of centralised monitoring, risk-based inspections and stricter accountability for enforcement officials.

The reforms were notified through a government order dated November 7, 2026, issued by Chief Secretary G. Sai Prasad, following the findings of inquiry committees, which pointed to fragmented enforcement and inadequate risk-based monitoring.

Under the new framework, the Director-General of the A.P. State Disaster Response and Fire Services has been designated as the State Nodal Authority to coordinate enforcement, conduct monthly inter-departmental reviews and submit compliance reports to the Home Department. District Collectors will function as nodal authorities at the district level, overseeing implementation and quarterly reviews.

The government has also ordered the establishment of a State Explosives and Fireworks Safety Cell within 30 days. It will maintain a digital register of fireworks manufacturing units, prepare risk-based inspection schedules, develop a Fireworks Risk Index and coordinate with the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO).

District Fireworks Safety Committees, headed by Collectors, will include officials from the police, fire services, revenue, factories, labour and pollution control departments. They will review licensed units and emergency preparedness at least once every quarter.

The licensing process for LE-1(a) units will be tightened through a two-stage system, involving provisional approval followed by a mandatory physical inspection after construction. The inspection must be supported by geo-tagged photographs and video evidence.

The government has set a six-month deadline for the RTGS and Information Technology, Electronics and Communications Department to operationalise an integrated online fireworks safety portal. It will track licences, approved layouts, CCTV feeds and stock movements, besides generating alerts on irregularities.

The new framework provides for immediate closure of units, seizure of materials and legal action in cases involving unlicensed operations, unauthorised chemical formulations, excess stock, unapproved equipment and obstruction of inspections.

The government has also made inspecting officers personally accountable for their certifications. Negligent inspections and suppression of violations will be treated as serious professional misconduct, inviting disciplinary and legal action.

The effectiveness of the new framework will depend on whether the prescribed inspections, digital monitoring and interdepartmental coordination translate into consistent enforcement on the ground.

⚡ 3-Point Exam Takeaway & Deep Breakdown
1. Core Context & Background: The Andhra Pradesh government has overhauled its fireworks safety, licensing and enforcement framework following explosions at fireworks manufacturing units in Rayavaram and Vetlapalem, introducing a system of centralised monitoring, risk-based inspections and stricter accountability for enforcement officials.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The reforms were notified through a government order dated November 7, 2026, issued by Chief Secretary G. Sai Prasad, following the findings of inquiry committees, which pointed to fragmented enforcement and inadequate risk-based monitoring.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The effectiveness of the new framework will depend on whether the prescribed inspections, digital monitoring and interdepartmental coordination translate into consistent enforcement on the ground.

articles.title: Policeman beaten to death in Theni over Deepavali celebration dispute
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Special Police Sub-Inspector Senthilkumar was killed while questioning a gang who were filming reels about bursting firecrackers on the road on November 8 night.

A Special Sub-Inspector (SSI) of Police, K. Senthilkumar, was beaten to death by a gang for questioning them about disrupting traffic at Samadharmapuram in Theni Allinagaram by bursting crackers in the middle of the road and making social media reels on the night of Deepavali (November 8, 2026).

The police said Senthilkumar, who is attached to the office of the Theni Deputy Superintendent of Police, was returning home after duty on Sunday night (November 8). He found some people bursting crackers in the middle of the road at Samadharmapuram and making reels at around 10:30 p.m.
AIADMK, AMMK leaders lash out at CM Vijay over Deepavali day murders across Tamil Nadu
Quarrel over bursting Deepavali crackers ends up in youth’s murder in Tiruchi district
18-year-old youth murdered by gang in Chennai’s Vyasarpadi

The SSI, who was in civvies, scolded them to stop disrupting traffic and burst crackers on the road margin. When they ignored him, Mr. Senthilkumar started recording a video on his phone and sent it to his office.
Angered over this, the gang beat him. He collapsed unconscious and was rushed to a private hospital. Later, at Theni Government Medical College hospital, he was declared dead.
The Theni police are trying to identify the assailants through video footage of a closed-circuit television camera network.
On Monday (November 9), Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay announced a solatium of ₹40 lakh to the family of Senthilkumar.

articles.title: Andhra SCPCR to organise meeting on ‘Making Father’s Name Optional’ with stakeholders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: SCPCR, in association with NGOs, Children of India Foundation and HELP, will conduct the meeting

The Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (AP SCPCR) will organise a State-level consultation on ‘Making Father’s Name not Mandatory in Official Documents’, with NGOs and child rights bodies.

SCPCR, in association with NGOs, Children of India Foundation and HELP, will conduct the meeting at Hotel Swarna Palace, from 10 a.m. onwards on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), said Commission Chairman Vetukuri A.V.S. Suryanarayana Raju.

Chairpersons of Juvenile Justice Boards (JJBs), Child Welfare Committees (CWCs), Central Administrators of One Stop Centres (OSCs), Anti-Human Trafficking Units (AHTUs) and Juvenile Police Units of Krishna, NTR, Palnadu, Guntur, Eluru and West Godavari districts, and child rights bodies will attend the day-long meeting, the SCPCR Chairman said.

fullParagraphs: Edappadi Palaniswami and T.T.V. Dhinakaran came down heavily on the TVK-led government.

The All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Monday (November 9, 2026) lashed out at Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay over a number of murders reported on Deepavali day (November 8) across the State and asked him whether he would realise that neither politics was a “film set” nor the chair of Chief Minister a platform for “punch dialogues.”

In his post on social media, the former Chief Minister referred to the lynching of a Special Sub-Inspector (SSI) of Police, Senthilkumar, at Allinagaram in Theni and said it was regrettable that the police force in the State has been “shattered.”

Referring to the announcement of solatium of ₹40 lakh for the bereaved family of the officer, Mr. Palaniswami argued the amount was not sufficient and demanded that the SSI’s family be paid ₹1 crore, as mentioned in a Government Order issued in October. He wanted those responsible for the several murders to be brought to book.

Mr. Dhinakaran criticised Mr. Vijay for not taking steps to maintain law and order. articles.title: Cases booked on all seen attackers in Kalighat clash, West Bengal CM says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘Those who tried to slap police, raised their fists and hurled threats have been booked under various sections. Police personnel were injured and were obstructed in discharging their official duty,’ says CM Adhikari

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday (November 9, 2026) said all those seen assaulting or threatening police personnel during the late-night clash outside TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee ’s Kalighat residence have been booked under appropriate sections of law and that chargesheets would be filed to ensure their trials while they remain in custody.

"Those who tried to slap police, raised their fists and hurled threats have been booked under various sections. Police personnel were injured and were obstructed in discharging their official duty. Cases have been registered against all whose names surfaced after going through videos. We will ensure chargesheets are filed, and custodial trials are held. There is no question of letting anyone off," he said.
Four FIRs have been registered at Kalighat police station, including two suo motu cases over attacks on police personnel.
Mr. Banerjee has been named in one of the FIRs. Two people were arrested on Sunday (November 8) for allegedly slapping an on-duty police officer during the confrontation, officials said.
CM Adhikari, who also holds the home portfolio, said those arrested were not residents of Harish Chatterjee Street, the locality where former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee lives.
"Some of the goons who have been caught are from Iqbalpore. What were these particular people doing there at 2 a.m. in the night? That is why they have been arrested," he said.
The Chief Minister said police have been given strict instructions to arrest everyone seen in the video footage.
He said political persons seen in the footage, and their leaders, would also face action after investigation.
Clashes broke out outside Mr. Banerjee’s residence after TMC supporters gathered there to celebrate his birthday, with Trinamool Congress workers and BJP supporters engaging in a confrontation.
Police have imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita in the area for two months.

articles.title: U.S., China, Russia leaders to meet next week, says Trump; Beijing says ‘in communication with parties’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Trump on Sunday, November 8, indicated to reporters that a deal on the Russia-Ukraine war, the Iran issue and nuclear arms control would be on the agenda

United States President Donald Trump has said he will likely meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in a rare trilateral leaders’ meeting on the sidelines of the APEC gathering in Shenzhen next week.

Beijing said on Monday (November 9, 2026) it was “in communication with relevant parties” over the meeting, not ruling out the possibility as leaders gather for the APEC summit in southern China on November 18 and 19.

Mr. Trump on Sunday ( November 8, 2026) indicated to reporters that a deal on the Russia-Ukraine war, the Iran issue and nuclear arms control would be on the agenda. “One of the meetings will be with President Putin and President Xi, and that’ll be interesting. We’re talking ​a lot of things, including denuclearisation, but we’ll ​be talking a lot of things. We’re trying to end the ‌war ⁠in Iran,” Mr. Trump was quoted as saying.

Asked about his remarks, China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun on Monday (November 9, 2026) did not rule out the prospect of a meeting, saying that China was in communication with relevant parties regarding the meeting between the Chinese, Russian and U.S. presidents.

Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi will meet bilaterally next week for the third time this year, following the U.S. President’s visit to Beijing in May and the Chinese President travelling to Washington in September . They will meet once again at the end of the year at the G20 in Miami, marking an unusual four meetings in a year.

articles.title: China dismisses a spy plot claim involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as smear campaign
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The chips company CEO is at the center of a controversy over whether he drove sales of advanced computer chips to China, in spite of U.S. tech restrictions aimed at limiting China’s ability to access these advanced technologies
China denied on Monday (November 9, 2026) there was a spy plot attempt to ensnare Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, calling the spying allegations unsubstantiated and a smear campaign against Beijing.

Mr. Huang has acknowledged to the Nvidia board that he had been intimate with a business executive who U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing, according to The New York Times.
“The so-called Chinese spy allegation is unsubstantiated. It is nothing but smears against China,” Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Monday (November 9, 2026).

The chips company CEO is at the center of a controversy over whether he drove sales of advanced computer chips to China, in spite of U.S. tech restrictions aimed at limiting China’s ability to access these advanced technologies. Nvidia is one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies, alongside Apple and Microsoft.
Nvidia said on Sunday (November 8) that the company would launch an investigation into the case. Mr. Huang did not name the person in the extramarital affair.

China had previously denied the New York Times report that said Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with a Chinese citizen named Alice Huang, who ran a company that faced claims of smuggling advanced chips into China, and that she was a spy for Beijing.

“The key questions are whether he was aware of any espionage activities and whether any confidential or strategically sensitive information was compromised,” said George Chen, a partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, a Washington-based consultancy.

Mr. Huang had pushed to loosen chip sales restrictions to China in recent years, successfully lobbying U.S. President Donald Trump to allow his company to sell H200 chips this year. However, it is uncertain if Beijing would allow Chinese companies to buy these chips en masse.

While those chips are not Nvidia's most cutting-edge models, they are still advanced. Previously, Mr. Huang also lobbied Mr. Trump to sell the less-advanced H20 chips, which were designed for the Chinese market while complying with U.S. export restrictions.

Chinese media have largely focused on Huang admitting to the affair and state media outlets have mainly echoed the official government line. Some have said the New York Times report was aimed at destabilising U.S.-China relations.

The chips company CEO is at the center of a controversy over whether he drove sales of advanced computer chips to China, in spite of U.S. tech restrictions aimed at limiting China’s ability to access these advanced technologies

China denied on Monday (November 9, 2026) there was a spy plot attempt to ensnare Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, calling the spying allegations unsubstantiated and a smear campaign against Beijing.

Mr. Huang has acknowledged to the Nvidia board that he had been intimate with a business executive who U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing, according to The New York Times.

“The so-called Chinese spy allegation is unsubstantiated. It is nothing but smears against China,” Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Monday (November 9, 2026).

The chips company CEO is at the center of a controversy over whether he drove sales of advanced computer chips to China, in spite of U.S. tech restrictions aimed at limiting China’s ability to access these advanced technologies. Nvidia is one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies, alongside Apple and Microsoft.

Nvidia said on Sunday (November 8) that the company would launch an investigation into the case. Mr. Huang did not name the person in the extramarital affair.

China had previously denied the New York Times report that said Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with a Chinese citizen named Alice Huang, who ran a company that faced claims of smuggling advanced chips into China, and that she was a spy for Beijing.

“The key questions are whether he was aware of any espionage activities and whether any confidential or strategically sensitive information was compromised,” said George Chen, a partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, a Washington-based consultancy.

Mr. Huang had pushed to loosen chip sales restrictions to China in recent years, successfully lobbying U.S. President Donald Trump to allow his company to sell H200 chips this year. However, it is uncertain if Beijing would allow Chinese companies to buy these chips en masse.

While those chips are not Nvidia's most cutting-edge models, they are still advanced. Previously, Mr. Huang also lobbied Mr. Trump to sell the less-advanced H20 chips, which were designed for the Chinese market while complying with U.S. export restrictions.

Chinese media have largely focused on Huang admitting to the affair and state media outlets have mainly echoed the official government line. Some have said the New York Times report was aimed at destabilising U.S.-China relations.

Created by Robert Tappan Morris, then a student, it changed the landscape of networking like never before. A.S.Ganesh wriggles his way through this story to hand you the best bits…

It is the dream of every (or most) digital native, or all of us living through the Information Age, to break the internet. For the uninitiated, that’s the process of posting or publishing something on the internet that goes on to create a terrific amount of interest, shock, or excitement. When you break the internet, a large number of people usually end up sharing or reacting to your initial post.

Even as you continue to think about your next post, picture, or reel that can maybe achieve this, spare a moment to think about whether the internet has ever been broken. Turns out, the answer is a resounding yes. But no, it wasn’t a celebrity posting about their latest life update, creating ripples across the globe. It was, in fact, the result of a student unleashing a computer worm in an experiment gone wrong.

articles.title: Supreme Court terms vehicular emissions major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Bench highlighted the large number of vehicles plying on roads connecting Delhi with neighbouring areas, including Ghaziabad, Greater Noida, Gurugram and Faridabad

The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) termed vehicular emissions a major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR and said immediate, medium- and long-term measures were needed to curb the rising air quality index.

Hearing a suo motu case examining the regulatory framework governing air pollution, a Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana also expressed concern over “bumper-to-bumper” traffic in Delhi-NCR.
“We keep talking and sometimes make statements and suggestions, but the point is that AQI is already touching 400,” the CJI said.
The Bench highlighted the large number of vehicles plying on roads connecting Delhi with neighbouring areas, including Ghaziabad, Greater Noida, Gurugram and Faridabad.
“Look at the roads in Delhi and the roads connecting Delhi with the NCR. Take a look at any road and the kind of vehicles moving on it. That is the major problem,” the CJI said.
The Bench said the poor people are the real sufferers, as they are on the roads, and moreover, the festival time is the only period when they earn a livelihood.

articles.title: Kochi police seize three private buses as drivers found allegedly drunk; 35 offences detected in special drive
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police have launched a series of special drives in the wake of recent fatal accident in which a woman pedestrian was run over by an allegedly speeding bus near Kakkanad

The Kochi City police on Monday seized three private buses after their drivers were allegedly found to be drunk. The cases were detected during a special enforcement drive conducted in and around Kakkanad and Thrikkakara from 5.30 a.m. to 8 a.m., according to the police.
As many as 132 buses were inspected as part of the drive, and 35 offences were detected, including drunken driving.

“The drivers who were found to be under the influence of alcohol were arrested, and the buses were seized and produced before the court. Steps will now be taken to suspend the licences of the drivers,” Bijoy Chandran, ACP, Thrikkakara, said.

The police have launched a series of special drives in the wake of the recent fatal accident in which a woman pedestrian was run over by an allegedly speeding bus near Kakkanad. The police had come under severe criticism from the High Court for failing to rein in rash driving and unruly behaviour by a section of private bus employees.

District Police Chief (Kochi city) R. Nishanthini said on Monday that strict action was being taken against erring private bus employees. She said the drive to issue police clearance certificates (PCCs) to all private bus employees would be completed without delay.

“I have learnt that around 1,200 applications have been received from bus employees for PCCs as part of the drive. Steps will be taken to issue the certificates within a week. A meeting of stakeholders has been convened to discuss the further steps regarding the drive, including collecting details of the remaining employees,” the officer said.

articles.title: At peak of air pollution on Deepavali night, data goes missing at several govt monitoring stations in Delhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Data missing from several monitoring stations at the peak of air pollution during the intervening night of November 8 and 9

As Delhiites burst firecrackers well past the 10 p.m. deadline set by the Supreme Court for Deepavali night, air pollution shot up to over 150-200 times World Health Organisation (WHO) limits in parts of the city, but fell through the early morning hours of Monday (November 9, 2026) due to better weather conditions, show official data.

At the peak of pollution , following the bursting of firecrackers on Sunday night (November 8), crucial air quality data were missing from several monitoring stations managed by government authorities. Experts say missing data on peak values of air pollution will artificially show better air quality than the reality.
Though the Supreme Court allowed only green firecrackers during fixed windows on November 7 and 8, traditional firecrackers, which are more polluting, were also available in the markets of Delhi .

As per the Delhi government’s Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) data, the level of PM2.5 (a major pollution) in Patparganj of East Delhi was 2,597 micrograms per cubic metre at 1 a.m. on Monday — about 173.13 times the WHO permissible limit of 15 micrograms per cubic metre for a 24-hour period.

Similarly, the level of PM2.5 in NSUT West Campus was 3,008.4 micrograms per cubic metre at 5 a.m. on Monday (November 9) — about 200.5 times the WHO permissible limit. PM2.5 (Particulate matter 2.5) are fine inhalable particles, which can get into lungs and bloodstream and lead to a range of respiratory and other diseases.

Gufran Beig, chair professor, National Institute of Advanced Studies, said though the air pollution spiked around 12 midnight on Sunday (November 8) to 5 a.m. on Monday (November 9) due to bursting of firecrackers on Deepavali, both wind direction and speed were very favourable for faster dispersion of air pollution.

“The wind direction was earlier north westerly, originating from stubble burning areas in Punjab and Haryana. But around Sunday afternoon, it changed to easterly and south easterly and also picked up speed by Sunday evening. The reversal of wind direction led to almost negligible effect of stubble burning in Delhi,” said Mr. Beig, who is also the founder-director of the Central government’s SAFAR (System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting Research).
Hourly PM2.5 concentrations across Delhi. | Photo Credit: CPCB CAAQMS

The 24-hour average overall Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi stood at 344 (“very poor”) at 4 p.m. on Monday (November 9), lower than 376 (“very poor”) a day earlier, according to the CPCB’s daily bulletin, which is considered the day’s AQI. A higher AQI means worsening of air quality. The overall AQI of Delhi which stood at 370 (very poor) at 9 a.m. on Monday, improved through the day to reach 344 by 4 p.m.

Meanwhile, both the AAP and the Congress attacked the BJP government over the missing data, with the former alleging that it was “data fraud”. Hitting back, Delhi Labour Minister Kapil Mishra alleged there was a “conspiracy” by AAP-governed Punjab to set stubble on fire on Sunday evening.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 09 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 At peak of air pollution on Deepavali night, data goes missing at several govt monitoring stations in Delhi

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Data missing from several monitoring stations at the peak of air pollution during the intervening night of November 8 and 9

As Delhiites burst firecrackers well past the 10 p.m. deadline set by the Supreme Court for Deepavali night, air pollution shot up to over 150-200 times World Health Organisation (WHO) limits in parts of the city, but fell through the early morning hours of Monday (November 9, 2026) due to better weather conditions, show official data.

At the peak of pollution , following the bursting of firecrackers on Sunday night (November 8), crucial air quality data were missing from several monitoring stations managed by government authorities. Experts say missing data on peak values of air pollution will artificially show better air quality than the reality.

Though the Supreme Court allowed only green firecrackers during fixed windows on November 7 and 8, traditional firecrackers, which are more polluting, were also available in the markets of Delhi .

As per the Delhi government’s Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) data, the level of PM2.5 (a major pollution) in Patparganj of East Delhi was 2,597 micrograms per cubic metre at 1 a.m. on Monday — about 173.13 times the WHO permissible limit of 15 micrograms per cubic metre for a 24-hour period.

Similarly, the level of PM2.5 in NSUT West Campus was 3,008.4 micrograms per cubic metre at 5 a.m. on Monday (November 9) — about 200.5 times the WHO permissible limit. PM2.5 (Particulate matter 2.5) are fine inhalable particles, which can get into lungs and bloodstream and lead to a range of respiratory and other diseases.

Gufran Beig, chair professor, National Institute of Advanced Studies, said though the air pollution spiked around 12 midnight on Sunday (November 8) to 5 a.m. on Monday (November 9) due to bursting of firecrackers on Deepavali, both wind direction and speed were very favourable for faster dispersion of air pollution.

“The wind direction was earlier north westerly, originating from stubble burning areas in Punjab and Haryana. But around Sunday afternoon, it changed to easterly and south easterly and also picked up speed by Sunday evening. The reversal of wind direction led to almost negligible effect of stubble burning in Delhi,” said Mr. Beig, who is also the founder-director of the Central government’s SAFAR (System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting Research).

Hourly PM2.5 concentrations across Delhi. | Photo Credit: CPCB CAAQMS

The 24-hour average overall Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi stood at 344 (“very poor”) at 4 p.m. on Monday (November 9), lower than 376 (“very poor”) a day earlier, according to the CPCB’s daily bulletin, which is considered the day’s AQI. A higher AQI means worsening of air quality. The overall AQI of Delhi which stood at 370 (very poor) at 9 a.m. on Monday, improved through the day to reach 344 by 4 p.m.

Meanwhile, both the AAP and the Congress attacked the BJP government over the missing data, with the former alleging that it was “data fraud”. Hitting back, Delhi Labour Minister Kapil Mishra alleged there was a “conspiracy” by AAP-governed Punjab to set stubble on fire on Sunday evening.

articles.title: Muslim Youth League leaders booked over rally causing traffic obstruction in Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: MYL State president Sayyid Munavvar Ali Shihab Thangal and Fathima Thahiliya, MLA, among those booked

A case has been registered against 12 Muslim Youth League (MYL) leaders, including its State president Sayyid Munavvar Ali Shihab Thangal and Fathima Thahiliya, MLA, in connection with a rally organised as part of its State conference that allegedly caused traffic obstruction in Kochi, the police said on Monday.
The case was registered by Ernakulam Central Police following a rally organised by the Muslim Youth League State committee from Bolgatty to the Kerala High Court Junction on Sunday.
According to the FIR, around 2,000 people took part in the rally, which began at Goshree Junction in Bolgatty around 4 pm and reached Marine Drive around 5.30 pm.
The rally allegedly caused obstruction to vehicular and pedestrian movement along Shanmukham Road near High Court Junction, the FIR stated.

The other accused include State general secretary MLA PK Firoz, treasurer P Ismayil, vice-presidents Mujeeb Kaderi, Faisal Bafaqui Thangal, Ashraf Edaneer and KA Mahin, and secretaries CK Muhammadali, Naseer Karyara, Gafoor Kolkkalathil and TPM Jishan.
The case was registered under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Kerala Public Ways (Restriction of Assemblies and Procession) Act, 2011.
The police had announced traffic diversions in Kochi city on Sunday in connection with the rally.

articles.title: Pakistani TV anchorperson shot dead at home in Rawalpindi; husband held
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A Pakistani anchorperson was shot dead at her home in Rawalpindi, with police taking her husband into custody and seizing the suspected weapon.

Rabia Ahsan, who worked as an anchor and programme host with a local private TV channel, was found dead at her home in the Gulshanabad area of the city on Sunday (November 8, 2026), the Dawn newspaper reported.
City Police Officer (CPO) Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera said Ahsan's husband had been taken into custody and the suspected weapon seized. An investigation has been launched, he added.
Mr. Sukhera, along with the senior superintendent of police (SSP) operations and the SSP investigations, visited the crime scene with a team of forensic experts.
According to the CPO, a male domestic worker at the house told police that the victim's husband had claimed that the gunshot was fired accidentally.
Mr. Sukhera said teams from the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA) were collecting evidence from the scene, while the body was being taken to a hospital for postmortem examination.
A case was being registered and an investigation would be conducted on merit, he said.
Meanwhile, First Lady Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari expressed deep sadness over the killing and strongly condemned the violence.
She called for a thorough, impartial and transparent investigation to establish the facts and ensure that those responsible were held accountable, a statement issued by the Presidency said.
Ms. Bhutto-Zardari also expressed concern over what she described as a “disturbing pattern of killing of another professional woman in the same metropolitan area”.

articles.title: 2026 to be one of four warmest years on record: World Meteorological Organization
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The key reason behind the rising global temperatures is that the Earth’s energy imbalance is rising, and the earth system is accumulating heat at an accelerating rate, said WMO

The year 2026 will be one of the four warmest years on record, with the global average temperature for January-September 2026 touching 1.47 degrees Celsius higher than pre-industrial times (the average of the 1850-1900 period), according to a new World Meteorological Organization report.
It added that this global average temperature figure was higher than the full-year averages in 2025 and 2023, and only slightly lower than 2024, which is the warmest year on record.

Moreover, the figure is likely to rise through the end of 2026 because of the warming effect of the prevailing El Nino, which has been intensifying since August and is expected to be the strongest on record by December.

The report, ‘State of the Climate Report’, was released by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) on Friday – the first day of this year’s UN climate meeting, known as COP31, in Antalya, Türkiye.

In a statement, WMO Secretary General Celeste Saulo said, “The past four years have been the warmest in the 177-year observational record, and the heat in the oceans is breaking records for the tenth year in a row.”
“The ongoing El Nino is forecast to be one of the strongest on record, and the heat it releases from the ocean will continue to fuel high temperatures and extreme weather into 2027,” she added.
The key reason behind the rising global temperatures is that the Earth’s energy imbalance is rising, and the earth system is accumulating heat at an accelerating rate.

The imbalance reached its highest level since monitoring began, as greenhouse gases trap unprecedented amounts of heat and upset the equilibrium between incoming energy from the sun and outgoing energy, according to the WMO report.

It revealed that the atmospheric concentration of carbon dioxide has increased by 53% from around 278 parts per million (ppm) in 1750 to about 426.8 ppm in 2025. Global averaged methane concentrations increased from 729 parts per billion (ppb) in 1750 by 167% to 1,948 ppb in 2025.
Moreover, the ocean absorbs 90% of the excess heat, and 2026 is on track to be the tenth successive year of record ocean warmth, the report said.

The key reason behind the rising global temperatures is that the Earth’s energy imbalance is rising, and the earth system is accumulating heat at an accelerating rate, said WMO

The year 2026 will be one of the four warmest years on record, with the global average temperature for January-September 2026 touching 1.47 degrees Celsius higher than pre-industrial times (the average of the 1850-1900 period), according to a new World Meteorological Organization report.

It added that this global average temperature figure was higher than the full-year averages in 2025 and 2023, and only slightly lower than 2024, which is the warmest year on record.

Moreover, the figure is likely to rise through the end of 2026 because of the warming effect of the prevailing El Nino, which has been intensifying since August and is expected to be the strongest on record by December.

The report, ‘State of the Climate Report’, was released by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) on Friday – the first day of this year’s UN climate meeting, known as COP31, in Antalya, Türkiye.

In a statement, WMO Secretary General Celeste Saulo said, “The past four years have been the warmest in the 177-year observational record, and the heat in the oceans is breaking records for the tenth year in a row.”

“The ongoing El Nino is forecast to be one of the strongest on record, and the heat it releases from the ocean will continue to fuel high temperatures and extreme weather into 2027,” she added.

The key reason behind the rising global temperatures is that the Earth’s energy imbalance is rising, and the earth system is accumulating heat at an accelerating rate.

The imbalance reached its highest level since monitoring began, as greenhouse gases trap unprecedented amounts of heat and upset the equilibrium between incoming energy from the sun and outgoing energy, according to the WMO report.

It revealed that the atmospheric concentration of carbon dioxide has increased by 53% from around 278 parts per million (ppm) in 1750 to about 426.8 ppm in 2025. Global averaged methane concentrations increased from 729 parts per billion (ppb) in 1750 by 167% to 1,948 ppb in 2025.

Moreover, the ocean absorbs 90% of the excess heat, and 2026 is on track to be the tenth successive year of record ocean warmth, the report said.

articles.title: Kremlin hopes U.S. election shake-up won't shift Trump's negotiations on Ukraine
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Republicans' defeat in the U.S. midterm elections was watched closely in Russia, where some observers are predicting it could herald more support for Ukraine when the Democrats take over Congress in January.
But if the Kremlin is hearing the ticking of a clock on its nearly 5-year-old full-scale invasion of its neighbour, it seemingly remains unperturbed.

Asked if the election's outcome could stymie U.S. attempts to help negotiate a settlement between Moscow and Kyiv, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov voiced hope that U.S. President Donald Trump will continue to pursue his peace efforts.

“There is groundwork already in place, and another round of trilateral negotiations is set to take place very soon,” Mr. Peskov said of talks planned for Tuesday (November 10, 2026) and Wednesday (November 11) involving Russian, Ukrainian and U.S. representatives in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.

articles.title: Chennai sees dozens of cracker-related eye injuries; doctors call for caution
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The day may have been wet, but Chennaiites still went all out to bring in light and sparkles on Deepavali day, which fell on Sunday (November 8, 2026). While awareness about safety has increased, ophthalmologists in the city have once again called for caution and reiterated protective measures, as they have received dozens of cases of cracker-related injuries.
The Regional Institute of Ophthalmology and Government Ophthalmic Hospital received around 50 cases, with about 10 cases having to be admitted, a senior official said.

Over the Deepavali weekend, the emergency clinic at Sankara Nethralaya saw 45 cases of firecracker injuries at its main campus. Two underwent wound repair surgery, while two others were scheduled for surgery on Monday, November 9, according to T.S. Surendran, its chairman..
Chennai’s air quality deteriorates to ‘poor’ the morning after Deepavali
Poor response from residents to Chennai Corporation’s appeal for segregated collection of cracker waste

At Dr. Agarwals Eye Hospital, nearly 20 patients came in with cracker-related injuries, said S. Soundari, regional head, clinical services. One of these, she explained, was a very serious case that had been taken up for surgery. Another patient lit a firecracker, but it did not blast. He went near it to take a look, and it blasted in his face, injuring both eyes. The remaining injuries were mostly small, and would be treated medically, she said. Four cases involved children; the rest were adults, mostly in their 30s and 40s.

At Rajan Eye Care, about 15 patients have been seen over the past three days or so, said Mohan Rajan, chairman and medical director of the hospital. One patient had to undergo a surgery, while minor injuries were treated as outpatients.

Doctors have reiterated caution. Dr. Soundari called for wearing protective eye gear while bursting firecrackers, supervising children properly, and importantly, not trying to touch the eye or take objects out by oneself. “Come to a doctor immediately if there is an eye injury,” she stressed. Dr. Rajan noted that bystanders often got hurt and should be careful to maintain an adequate distance..

"Safer schools require sustained investment in teacher preparation, mental health and psychosocial support, reporting and response systems, digital safety measures, and coordinated action across education, child protection, health and technology sectors.

articles.title: NMC cautions students against fake medical colleges, asks them to verify approvals
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The advisory follows the Supreme Court taking cognisance of the issue in an ongoing case in which the court directed regulatory bodies, including the National Medical Commission, to caution students and parents against dealing with unauthorised educational institutions

The National Medical Commission (NMC) has cautioned students and parents against enrolling in medical colleges without verifying their statutory recognition and regulatory approvals, warning that fraudulent institutions could be misleading aspirants through advertisements, websites, social media promotions and unauthorised admission offers.

In a recent advisory issued in compliance with directions from the Supreme Court, the NMC has urged students to independently verify a medical college’s approval status, permitted student intake, and admission permissions for the relevant academic year before seeking admission or making any payment.

The advisory follows the Supreme Court taking cognisance of the issue in Ayesha Jain v. Amity University, Noida & Ors. , an ongoing case in which the Court directed regulatory bodies, including the NMC, to caution students and parents against dealing with unauthorised educational institutions. The directions came in the context of a reported instance of a purported fake medical college operating from a farmhouse and claiming to offer various courses.

The Commission has clarified that a medical college’s presence in an official list, or its previous operation, does not automatically establish that it has permission to admit students in subsequent academic years. Candidates must check the approval granted for the particular year and the number of seats sanctioned through official NMC and Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) records.

It has also cautioned students against relying exclusively on prospectuses, websites, advertisements, social media posts or documents such as purported Letters of Permission and approval certificates circulated by institutions or their representatives. Any doubts regarding the authenticity of such documents should be verified directly with the concerned regulatory authority.

For admissions governed by counselling procedures, candidates have been asked to use official channels, including the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC), wherever applicable, or the competent State and Union Territory counselling authorities. The Commission has also advised students against making admission-related payments to unauthorised agents, personal bank accounts or unverified intermediaries.

Highlighting the importance of distinguishing between regulatory approvals, the NMC said affiliation, registration or recognition granted by one authority for a particular purpose should not be construed as permission from the Commission to conduct an MBBS course. Each statutory requirement must be independently satisfied.

The advisory also asks students and parents to exercise caution when institutions make extraordinary claims about clinical training, hospital facilities and admission opportunities. The existence of a building, office or website, it said, does not establish that an institution is legally authorised to impart medical education.

Suspected fake medical colleges, unauthorised MBBS courses, forged permission letters and fraudulent admission offers can be reported to the NMC through its official communication channels. Complaints may also be made to the State or U.T. medical education departments, relevant regulatory authorities, and local police. Students have been advised to preserve advertisements, payment receipts, correspondence and website details as supporting evidence.

The Commission has separately clarified that courses in pharmacy, nursing, Ayurveda, and allied healthcare programmes fall under different statutory or competent regulatory authorities. Their recognition and approval must be checked with the respective regulators.

articles.title: Sabarimala ghee supply in a bind; TDB opens talks with Milma
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: As the Travancore Devaswom Board had invited bids for 50,000 litres of ghee but failed to find eligible suppliers, it has been holding discussions with office-bearers of the Milma Thiruvananthapuram Regional Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union to plug the gap in supply

With the Mandala-Makaravilakku season in Sabarimala barely a week away, the Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) is turning to Milma once again to plug the gap in ghee supply after two rounds of tendering failed to find eligible bidders.

The board had invited bids for 50,000 litres of ghee but failed to find eligible suppliers. Though Milma did not participate in the tender, the TDB has been holding discussions with office-bearers of the Milma Thiruvananthapuram Regional Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union.
TDB president K. Jayakumar said the board was yet to take a final call on procuring ghee from Milma for Aravana production and would seek legal advice before deciding on the matter.

According to him, the anticipated shortfall at the beginning of the season was only around 10,000 litres and there was no immediate cause for concern over availability. Ghee supplies were expected to increase once the temple opens on November 16, though the shortfall could affect production until then. Preparations for Aravana production are progressing, with the board currently holding a stock of 30 lakh tins. Arrangements are being finalised to produce 3.5 lakh tins daily.
“We are planning to produce another 30 lakh tins in the coming days. Appam production will also begin in a time-bound manner,” Mr. Jayakumar said.

Milma’s possible return as a supplier comes amid an ongoing Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) probe into the supply of spurious ghee to the Sannidhanam in its name last season. The investigation found that the contractor entrusted with transporting the ghee had diverted around 11,000 kg of Milma ghee meant for Sabarimala and replaced it with a cheaper product.

Meanwhile, the deadline for completing construction and other preparatory works, including maintenance, ahead of the season expires on Tuesday. Despite the TDB’s claims that preparations are complete, sources said several works at the Sannidhanam and Nilackal, including road reconstruction, remain unfinished and could take another week to complete.

articles.title: Bribe allegation drives CPI(M)-affiliated families into BJP in Keralam’s Pathanamthitta
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Around twenty-odd families quit CPI(M) and join BJP, alleging that leaders of the party’s Pariyaram local committee demanded bribes of ₹25,000 from them to facilitate the excavation of earth for house construction

Around twenty-odd families have quit the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] and joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Pathanamthitta district, alleging that leaders of the party’s Pariyaram local committee had demanded bribes from them.
The allegations relate to an incident at Varattuchira in Elanthoor, where party leaders allegedly demanded ₹25,000 to facilitate the excavation of earth for house construction.
The families, from Elanthoor Pariyaram and Varattuchira, were formally welcomed into the BJP by district president V.A. Sooraj, who also inaugurated a new party unit in the area.
The CPI(M)’s local leadership said an inquiry would be conducted into the allegations and action would be initiated.

Around twenty-odd families have quit the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] and joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Pathanamthitta district, alleging that leaders of the party’s Pariyaram local committee had demanded bribes from them.

The allegations relate to an incident at Varattuchira in Elanthoor, where party leaders allegedly demanded ₹25,000 to facilitate the excavation of earth for house construction.

The families, from Elanthoor Pariyaram and Varattuchira, were formally welcomed into the BJP by district president V.A. Sooraj, who also inaugurated a new party unit in the area.

The CPI(M)’s local leadership said an inquiry would be conducted into the allegations and action would be initiated.

articles.title: Equip students with industry-ready skills, entrepreneurial abilities, Joshi tells institutions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Union Minister says educational institutions should move beyond the conventional degree-oriented education

Union Minister for Education, Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Pralhad Joshi has stressed the need for educational institutions to move beyond conventional degree-oriented education and equip students with industry-relevant skills, entrepreneurial abilities and leadership qualities.

Speaking during the inauguration of the newly constructed third floor of the college and the Jnanayogi Sri Siddeshwar Swamiji Auditorium at the Chetan Group of Institutions in Hubballi on Saturday, he said that skill-based and industry-oriented education has become essential in an increasingly competitive world.
Educational institutions should focus on helping develop confidence, communication skills, leadership qualities and an entrepreneurial outlook among students, he said.
Mr. Joshi commended the Chetan Group for its commitment to quality education and for combining modern learning with Indian culture, values and traditions.
He expressed the hope that the institution will grow further and emerge as a centre of learning that will shape the future of thousands of students.
The programme was conducted in the presence of seer of the Sri Veerasimhasana Mahasamsthana Math at Suttur in Mysuru district Sri Shivaratri Desikendra Mahaswamiji.

The prestigious Chetanashri awards were presented to progressive farmer and agricultural entrepreneur Kavita Mishra and founder and chairman of Nadakattin Agri Business Pvt. Ltd. Abdul Khadar Nadakattin in recognition of their contributions to agriculture and entrepreneurship.

MP Jagadish Shettar, MLC Basavaraj Horatti, Hubballi-Dharwad Central MLA Mahesh Tenginkai, Hubballi-Dharwad East MLA Prasad Abbayya, MLC Lingaraj Patil, Mayor Durgamma Shashikant Bijawad and Deputy Mayor Ratnabai Eknath Nazare were among those present.

articles.title: OALP deepwater bidding deadline extended again to December 10
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Deadlines to the two rounds were last extended in September by about two months to November 15.

The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) on Monday extended the deadline for submitting bids for deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks under the 10th and 11th rounds of the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) by 25 days to December 10.

The latest extension marks the seventh for the 10th round, launched in April last year, and the third for the 11th round, which opened in March this year. The deadlines were last extended in September by nearly two months to November 15.
The 10th round offers 25 blocks, including one deepwater and 12 ultra-deepwater blocks, while the 11th round has five blocks on offer, comprising one deepwater and four ultra-deepwater areas.

In August, the Union Cabinet approved an outlay of ₹84,084 crore for the Petroleum Ministry’s National Offshore Exploration Scheme, titled ‘Samudra Manthan’. The corpus, to be utilised until FY31, includes ₹43,200 crore for drilling 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells.

State-owned explorers ONGC and Oil India have also announced substantial investments in offshore exploration. ONGC plans to invest ₹1 lakh crore by 2030, while Oil India has earmarked ₹15,000 crore over the next three years for deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration.

articles.title: Trump says likely to meet Putin, Xi at China APEC summit
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: U.S. President Donald Trump indicated to reporters that a deal on the Russia-Ukraine war, the Iran issue and nuclear arms control would be on the agenda

United States President Donald Trump has said he will likely meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in a rare trilateral leaders’ meeting on the sidelines of the APEC gathering in Shenzhen next week.

Beijing said on Monday (November 9, 2026) it was “in communication with relevant parties” over the meeting, not ruling out the possibility as leaders gather for the APEC summit in southern China on November 18 and 19.

Mr. Trump on Sunday (November 8, 2026) indicated to reporters that a deal on the Russia-Ukraine war, the Iran issue and nuclear arms control would be on the agenda. “One of the meetings will be with President Putin and President Xi, and that’ll be interesting. We’re talking ​a lot of things, including denuclearisation, but we’ll ​be talking a lot of things. We’re trying to end the ‌war ⁠in Iran,” Mr. Trump was quoted as saying.

Asked about his remarks, China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun on Monday (November 9, 2026) did not rule out the prospect of a meeting, saying that China was in communication with relevant parties regarding the meeting between the Chinese, Russian and U.S. Presidents.

Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi will meet bilaterally next week for the third time this year, following the U.S. President’s visit to Beijing in May and the Chinese President travelling to Washington in September . They will meet once again at the end of the year at the G20 in Miami, marking an unusual four meetings in a year.

Both countries have sought to inject more stability in relations and pursue what they call “a constructive relationship of strategic stability”, even as they have exchanged blows on issues including trade tariffs, restrictions on semiconductors, rare earths and Taiwan.

Chinese analysts have sought to play down the significance of a possible trilateral summit, just as they also played down Mr. Trump’s remarks in Beijing earlier this year of a “G2”. Russia was “most enthusiastic” among the three, Su Liuqiang, a scholar at the Centre for American Studies at the Shanghai Institutes for International Studies, said in an interview with state media, adding that an informal exchange was likelier than a more structured, formal trilateral summit.

“On the one hand, there is substantial political resistance in the U.S. Anti-Russia sentiment remains strong in both the U.S. and among its European allies, with opposition to negotiating with Moscow while bypassing Ukraine and Europe. On the other hand, the three countries have differing priorities. Russia’s core concern is negotiations on a ceasefire in Ukraine, the U.S. is interested in the Russia-Ukraine conflict and non-proliferation, China supports peace talks but must also balance its relations with the U.S., Russia, Europe and Ukraine. In this context, a low-profile trilateral meeting is the more realistic option,” he said, adding that practical outcomes could emphasise stabilising global energy supplies.

While China preferred “multilateralism” over ideas such as the G2 or a U.S.-China-Russia triumvirate, Mr. Su said a meeting would still be significant in suggesting that while structural competition between big powers would still continue to define global geopolitics, there was increasing interest in “managing that competition and preventing it from escalating or spinning out of control”.
