fullParagraphs: Mutual attacks continue, with the U.S. striking Iran's Qeshm island overnight, according to Iranian state media, and Iran attacking tankers in the Gulf and ‌Strait of Hormuz this month while its Yemeni Houthi allies have hit Saudi Arabia

U.S. President Donald Trump will meet ‌the Prime Minister of key mediator Qatar on Monday (November 9, 2026) as efforts to end the ​Iran war ramp up following last week's midterm elections, though senior U.S. and Gulf ⁠officials cast doubt on the chances of an imminent deal.

With no victory in sight more than eight months into the conflict he launched alongside Israel on February 28, Mr. Trump has played down the likelihood of major warfare restarting soon, but remains ‌unwilling to accept an existing Iranian truce plan.

Mutual attacks continue, with the U.S. striking Iran's Qeshm island overnight, according to Iranian state media, and Iran attacking tankers in the Gulf and ‌Strait of Hormuz this month while its Yemeni Houthi allies have hit Saudi Arabia.

Sheikh Mohammed ‌bin ⁠Abdulrahman Al-Thani, who is both Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Qatar, will meet Mr. ⁠Trump and Vice President J. D. Vance in Washington later on Monday (November 9, 2026) after having visited Tehran last week.

Iran's proposal to end the war involves an end to the U.S. blockade of its ports, the lifting of some sanctions, and a halt to bombing in return for ​Tehran stopping its own blockade of the Strait ‌of Hormuz, with talks on its nuclear programme and other sanctions to follow.

The U.S. has repeatedly rejected that plan, which Iran has said could be condensed to a two-day timeframe, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Sunday (November 8, 2026) describing Tehran's conditions as "outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic".
Iran's Foreign Ministry ‌spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei defended the plan on Monday (November 9, 2026) as the most reasonable offer on the table.

Senior ​U.S. Republicans including Mr. Vance have blamed their party's dire showing in last week's elections on the Iran war, but despite growing domestic political pressure to end the conflict, Mr. Rubio said ⁠he did not believe a diplomatic breakthrough was imminent.
A senior United Arab Emirates official, Anwar Gargash, echoed that view on Monday (November 9, 2026), saying a comprehensive political settlement between the U.S. and Iran appeared difficult.
"We should... prepare for a ‌long period of uncertainty in which neither a decisive resolution nor stable regional order can be taken for granted," he said.

U.S. President Donald Trump will meet ‌the Prime Minister of key mediator Qatar on Monday (November 9, 2026) as efforts to end the ​Iran war ramp up following last week's midterm elections, though senior U.S. and Gulf ⁠officials cast doubt on the chances of an imminent deal.

With no victory in sight more than eight months into the conflict he launched alongside Israel on February 28, Mr. Trump has played down the likelihood of major warfare restarting soon, but remains ‌unwilling to accept an existing Iranian truce plan.

Mutual attacks continue, with the U.S. striking Iran's Qeshm island overnight, according to Iranian state media, and Iran attacking tankers in the Gulf and ‌Strait of Hormuz this month while its Yemeni Houthi allies have hit Saudi Arabia.

Sheikh Mohammed ‌bin ⁠Abdulrahman Al-Thani, who is both Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Qatar, will meet Mr. ⁠Trump and Vice President J. D. Vance in Washington later on Monday (November 9, 2026) after having visited Tehran last week.

Iran's proposal to end the war involves an end to the U.S. blockade of its ports, the lifting of some sanctions, and a halt to bombing in return for ​Tehran stopping its own blockade of the Strait ‌of Hormuz, with talks on its nuclear programme and other sanctions to follow.

The U.S. has repeatedly rejected that plan, which Iran has said could be condensed to a two-day timeframe, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Sunday (November 8, 2026) describing Tehran's conditions as "outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic".

Iran's Foreign Ministry ‌spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei defended the plan on Monday (November 9, 2026) as the most reasonable offer on the table.

Senior ​U.S. Republicans including Mr. Vance have blamed their party's dire showing in last week's elections on the Iran war, but despite growing domestic political pressure to end the conflict, Mr. Rubio said ⁠he did not believe a diplomatic breakthrough was imminent.

A senior United Arab Emirates official, Anwar Gargash, echoed that view on Monday (November 9, 2026), saying a comprehensive political settlement between the U.S. and Iran appeared difficult.

"We should... prepare for a ‌long period of uncertainty in which neither a decisive resolution nor stable regional order can be taken for granted," he said.

articles.title: Number of villages without 4G connectivity falls by three-fourths in four years
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Data obtained by The Hindu under the Right to Information Act shows a sharp decline in the number of villages without serviceable internet speeds

The number of villages without 4G connectivity has fallen from 45,180 in 2022 to 11,372, about a fourth of the earlier figure, according to data from the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) obtained by The Hindu under the Right to Information Act, 2005. The reduction is partly the result of BSNL’s 4G saturation project. But the figure is beyond the scheme’s initial target of covering 24,680 villages, indicating complementary efforts by private operators.

The reduction is notable because of historical gaps in connectivity between urban and rural India. The country is still far from universal smartphone ownership, even as cities and towns often enjoy extensive high-speed 5G coverage and affordable wired home broadband. The development also comes at a time when additions to wired broadband subscriptions have stagnated for months, making mobile broadband — the primary means of internet access for Indians — all the more important.

articles.title: Congress leader criticises Modi, calls for accountability on key issues
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress party’s Vijayawada parliamentary constituency in-charge Bhargav Valluru criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi for repeatedly attacking the party instead of explaining his government’s achievements and addressing its failure to fulfil the promises made to the people.

Even on an occasion like Diwali, the Prime Minister chose to prioritise political attacks and divisive rhetoric, he said, adding that festivals are meant to strengthen love, unity, and brotherhood among the citizens.
“Unfortunately, instead of delivering a message that unites the nation, the Prime Minister continues to focus on attacking Congress. This reflects his political approach,” he said.

He demanded that the Prime Minister answer the questions on serious issues, including allegations of vote theft, the functioning of the Election Commission, unemployment, farmers’ distress, demonetisation, and the burden of GST.

Mr. Bhargav Valluru further demanded that the Central government respond to allegations that independent institutions such as the Election Commission, CBI, and Enforcement Directorate (ED) are being used to exert political pressure on opposition parties.

articles.title: Kripa Alva appears before police in Siddaramaiah ‘sting’ video case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Expelled Congress leader Kripa Alva on Monday appeared before the Cyber Crime Police, which is investigating the alleged fabricated sting video involving former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah.

Kripa Alva, a political leader from Dakshina Kannada, appeared before investigators at the Bengaluru Police Commissioner’s Office in Vasanth Nagar, accompanied by her legal counsel. She left the premises without responding to reporters’ questions.
She had earlier been questioned by the police in connection with the case and has also secured interim relief from a court.

The investigation has revealed that a mobile phone allegedly used to upload the sting video changed hands at Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy’s official residence in New Delhi, Bengaluru City Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh recently told the media.

The police have questioned former journalist Prajwal Prasad, who is reportedly associated with Mr. Kumaraswamy’s social media team as a media consultant. Investigators suspect that Mr. Prasad facilitated the purchase of the mobile phone and received it at Kumaraswamy’s official residence from Ritesh Pandey, another accused who has been arrested in the case.
The police are continuing their investigation to establish the roles of those involved in procuring the phone and uploading the video.

articles.title: Journalist suffers injury after attack by unidentified individuals at Kavali
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police say two persons arrived on motorcycles and beat up Subba Rao at Peddapavani road as he was returning home and left the spot after the latter lost consciousness

A reporter working for a regional newspaper was reportedly attacked and injured by some unidentified individuals at Kavali town in SPSR Nellore district on Sunday. Various journalist associations condemned the incident and demanded that the police take strict action against the culprits.

According to the police, two persons arrived on motorcycles and beat up Subba Rao at Peddapavani road on Sunday afternoon as he was returning home. The culprits attacked the reporter with their hands and did not use any weapons, and they left the spot immediately after he lost consciouness.
Subba Rao is currently undergoing treatment at a hospital.

Meanwhile, the members of Andhra Pradesh Union of Working Journalists (APUWJ) submitted a representation to Joint Collector Mogili Venkateswarlu on Monday, requesting promp identification of the assailants and strict action against them. The members of Andhra Pradesh Media Professionals Association (APMPA) District Committee and Journalist Protection Force (JPF) also demanded the police authorities to identify those responsible for the attack and their immediately arrest.

Speaking to The Hindu , Nellore Superintendent of Police (SP) Ajitha Vejendla said, “The assault seems to have been carried out by individuals who held a grudge against Mr. Subba Rao. However, it is yet to be established whether there is any link with political interference. The investigation is under way.”

articles.title: Srisailam gears up for ‘Karthika Masam’ festivities from November 10
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Temple management officials say ‘Sparsha Darshan’ will be suspended on Saturdays, Sundays, Mondays, and other auspicious festival days, while it will be permitted during specific time slots on other days
The month-long ‘Karthika Masam’ festivities at Sri Bhramarmba Mallikarjuna Swmay temple in Srisailam will be held from November 10 (Tuesday) to December 9.

The main events during the auspicious month include ‘Koti Deepotsavam’ (lighting of one crore lamps) opposite the temple’s vedic school on ‘Karthika Shuddha Ekadasi’ (November 20), ‘Jwala Thoranam’ (ceremonial arch of fire), ‘Laksha Deepotsavam’ (lighting of one lakh lamps) and ‘Pushkarini Harathi’ on the day of ‘Karthika Pournami’ (November 24), as well as ‘Krishnamma Harathi’ at Patala Ganga on November 13.
Meanwhile, ‘Laksha Deepotsavam’ (lighting of one hundred thousand lamps) and ‘Pushkarini Harati’ (ritual offering of lamps at the temple tank) will be conducted every Monday during the month.

Temple Trust Board chairman Pothugunta Ramesh Naidu and executive officer (EO) M. Srinivasa Rao said in a press release on Monday that ‘Sparsha Darshan’ will be suspended on Saturdays, Sundays, Mondays, and other auspicious festival days. On regular days, Sparsha Darshan will be permitted during specific time slots to ensure there is no inconvenience to devotees in the ‘Sarva Darshanam’ (general queue) line.

The temple management officials said arrangements, including accommodation for devotees, supply of drinking water, smooth darshan, ‘Arjita Sevas’ for the presiding deities, management of queue lines, crowd control, traffic regulation, sanitation, and vehicle parking, were being set up in view of the large influx of devotees during the month.
The temple doors will open daily at 3 a.m. After the early morning rituals, darshan will be available from 4.30 a.m. until 4 p.m., after which it will resume at 5.30 p.m.

As in the previous year, anointing the deity inside the sanctum sanctorum and collective anointing rituals have been suspended completely throughout the month for the convenience of general devotees. To facilitate a comfortable darshan for the devotees, the ‘Kumkumarchana’ ritual performed in the inner sanctum of the Goddess Bhramaramba will be conducted in the ‘Ashirvachana Mandapam’ during the month on Saturdays, Sundays, Mondays, and other festival days (a total of 16 days).
Other Arjita Sevas such as ‘Rudra Homam’, ‘Chandi Homam’, ‘Sakshi Ganapati Homam’, and ‘Nitya Kalyanam’ will continue as usual.

Highly placed officials had told The Hindu that New Delhi was in close contact with both sides over the specific proposal, and the government had hoped to hear back from both the Russian and Ukrainian sides at the earliest. articles.title: Syrian FM says country has no troops in Yemen, won't send any
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: He said the accord with Riyadh, a key backer of Damascus as it seeks to rebuild after more than a decade of civil war, was vital for Syria to rebuild its institutions, including the military

Syria's Foreign Minister on Monday (November 9, 2026) insisted that his country has no troops deployed in Yemen and was not planning on sending any, after Yemeni sources told AFP that Syrian soldiers were in Yemen and Saudi Arabia.
"There is no deployment of troops to Yemen nor is there a plan for such deployment in the near future," Asaad al-Shaibani said during a press conference with his Jordanian counterpart Ayman Safadi.
Multiple Yemeni officials told AFP last week that Syrian troops were already in the country, with potentially thousands to be deployed eventually.
Mr. Shaibani said that, despite Damascus and Riyadh signing a defence cooperation agreement this month, there was "no agreement with the legitimate government in Yemen for a deployment to Yemen".
"Any military plan abroad would be announced... and not done in secret," he added.
He said the accord with Riyadh, a key backer of Damascus as it seeks to rebuild after more than a decade of civil war, was vital for Syria to rebuild its institutions, including the military.
"We need Saudi expertise to help build the capacity of Syrians, and we would like there to be cooperation between us in the field of the defence industry, and on the academic level," he said.

Saudi Arabia has been trying to mobilise its allies as it comes under repeated attack by the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, where Riyadh has supported the internationally recognised government in the country's civil war since 2015.
Syria itself was devastated by a civil war that began in 2011 and only ended with the overthrow of Bashar al-Assad in December 2024 by Islamist-led rebels.

articles.title: Commercial cultivation within forest land not protected under FRA, 2006: Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Says FRA protects forest-dwelling communities dependent on forests for generations, not commercial cultivators and plantation owners
The Supreme Court has made it clear that commercial crop cultivation within reserve forest areas is not protected under the Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006.

The court has distinguished commercial cultivators and plantation owners from forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers, who have lived in forests for generations and depend on them for livelihood. Their rights are protected under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, commonly known as the FRA.
A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta recorded the court’s view in an order concerning extensive silk cotton cultivation within the reserve forests of the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve.

The court, in its November 6 order, directed the Central Empowered Committee to examine the Tamil Nadu government’s opinion that silk cotton was a ‘minor forest produce’. Presently, 3,637.83 hectares of the 5,072.64 hectares of forest land are under silk cotton cultivation.
However, the Bench made clear its prima facie view against the State’s claim of historical cultivation of silk cotton.

“What emerges from the government affidavits is the promotion and sponsored cultivation of silk cotton as a commercial crop… The concept of planned cultivation of commercial crops is totally contrary to the very concept of a naturally occurring minor forest produce,” the apex court noted.

“We are of the prima facie view that planned or promoted cultivation of a commercial crop inside the forest areas is completely impermissible, as no such right is recognised under the FRA, 2006. The Act recognises the right of forest dwellers to collect, use and dispose of minor forest produce in accordance with Section 3(1)(c). The cultivation of a commercial crop cannot, therefore, be recognised as a forest right so as to justify occupation or continued presence within the forest area,” the Bench said.

The court did not accept the Tamil Nadu government’s claim that the cultivation of silk cotton justified the presence of the cultivators in the forest area.
“If commercial crops are permitted to be cultivated in the forest areas, the very nature of the forest is bound to change,” Justice Mehta, who authored the order, observed.

fullParagraphs: Industries Minister M.B. Patil says 131 of the 147 cleared projects will come up outside Bengaluru

In a bid to provide momentum to industrial growth beyond Bengaluru, the State-Level Single Window Clearance Committee (SLSWCC) on Monday approved 147 investment proposals with a total investment of ₹6,825.93 crore, a majority of which are related to areas outside Bengaluru.

“Of the approved proposals, 131 will come up in districts other than Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural, giving a further boost to regional industrial growth,” said Large and Medium Industries and Infrastructure Development Minister M.B. Patil, who chaired the committee’s 161st meeting. “These projects are expected to create a total of 18,600 jobs across the State,” he said.

According to Mr. Patil, the proposals include 36 major projects with investments of more than ₹50 crore each, accounting for a total investment of ₹4,507.71 crore. They are expected to generate 12,074 jobs.
Another 108 new projects, with investments ranging from ₹15 crore to ₹50 crore, will bring in ₹2,238.37 crore and create around 6,526 jobs, he noted.
The committee also cleared additional investment proposals from three existing projects, amounting to ₹79.85 crore.

The Minister said the approved projects cover a diverse range of sectors, including food processing, textiles, data centres, semiconductors, IT parks, printed circuit board assembly, aerospace, sugar and general engineering.

Among the notable proposals are Advaith Tech LLP (Bengaluru), which will set up an IT & ITES park with allied infrastructure at Devanahalli with an investment of ₹380 crore, creating 500 jobs; and Vista Spaces Tec Hoodi Private Limited, which will develop an IT/ITES park at Doddanekundi in Bengaluru East taluk with an investment of ₹260 crore and create 750 jobs, he said.
Gowribidanur in Chickballapur district will host three major projects.

They are OFB Tech Limited’s 250 TPD container glass plant (₹245 crore, 400 jobs); UHP Technologies Private Limited’s semiconductor and solar cell equipment manufacturing unit (₹200 crore, 300 jobs); and Interrni International Private Limited’s integrated manufacturing facility for interiors, modular fit-outs and architectural facade systems (₹130 crore, around 600 jobs).
In Mysuru district, FIEM Industries Limited will manufacture advanced lighting and electronic components at Kochanahalli.

fullParagraphs: The Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science, Khaja Bandanawaz University (KBNU), organised a two-day hands-on workshop on GenAI and Salesforce Revolution recently, aiming to equip students with skills relevant to the rapidly evolving industry requirements in artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud-based customer relationship management (CRM) platforms.
The workshop, held at the Faculty of Science auditorium, sought to bridge the gap between classroom learning and practical industry experience.

Pro-Vice-Chancellor of KBNU Syed Ashfaq Ahmed inaugurated the workshop. Dean and Professor of the School of Computer Science, Central University of Karnataka, Kalaburagi, R.S. Hegde was the guest of honour.

Salesforce developers from Earlyg Technologies, Bengaluru, Mohammed Qutubuddin Bilal and Mohammed Noman and founder of Invidit Technologies, Kalaburagi, Nazeerullah Hussaini conducted the technical sessions.
The participants were introduced to the fundamentals of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), a branch of AI that creates new content based on patterns learnt from large datasets.
The resource persons also demonstrated how AI can be integrated with salesforce to improve customer relationship management, sales, marketing and service operations.
Around 150 registered students from various colleges in Kalaburagi participated in the workshop. Certificates were distributed to the participants at the conclusion of the programme.
Workshop coordinator Ashalatha R. provided an overview of the programme. Ahelam Tikotikar and Shirin Sultana compered the sessions.

articles.title: Chennai’s air quality deteriorates to ‘poor’ the morning after Deepavali
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Manali Village recorded the highest AQI at 296, followed by Arumbakkam at 265, Kodungaiyur at 215, Royapuram at 184 and Velachery Residential Area at 142
After a rain-interrupted start to Deepavali, firecracker bursting picked up sharply across Chennai on Sunday evening, leaving the entire city shrouded in smoke by night.

As the sun rose over a smoke-filled Chennai on Monday, the city’s average Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 213, placing it in the ‘Poor’ category at 9 a.m., according to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data.

A 24-hour ambient air quality survey conducted by the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board (TNPCB) from 6 a.m. on November 8 to 6 a.m. on November 9 found that Valasaravakkam recorded the highest AQI in the State at 343, falling in the ‘Very Poor’ category for the fourth consecutive year. The lowest reading was recorded at Thiruvottiyur at 183, in the ‘Moderate’ category.

In Chennai, five of the seven locations covered by the TNPCB survey recorded AQI levels above 250. Apart from Valasaravakkam, Nungambakkam recorded 332, Sowcarpet 311, T. Nagar 306, and Triplicane 267. Besant Nagar recorded 230, while Thiruvottiyur recorded 183.

The TNPCB conducted manual air quality monitoring at 39 locations and noise monitoring at 34 locations across Tamil Nadu from November 1 to 9, following directions issued by the Supreme Court to monitor air quality and noise levels for 15 days, beginning seven days before Deepavali and ending seven days after the festival.

The TNPCB’s comparative analysis of 39 monitoring locations across 17 districts in the State showed a continued rise in average AQI levels over the past three Deepavali periods. The average AQI increased from 143.46 in 2024 to 161.69 in 2025 and 168.97 in 2026, an increase of approximately 4.5% over the previous year.
Of the 39 locations, 25 recorded an increase in AQI levels in 2026 compared to 2025, while 14 recorded a decline.

In Chennai, Valasaravakkam’s AQI rose from 287 in 2024 to 332 in 2025, and 343 in 2026. Nungambakkam also recorded a consistent increase, from 230 in 2024 to 326 in 2025, and 332 in 2026. At Sowcarpet, the AQI increased from 193 in 2024 to 260 in 2025, and 311 in 2026. T. Nagar recorded a rise from 203 in 2024 to 273 in 2025, and 306 in 2026.

Noise levels also registered an increase both on the day before and on Deepavali. On Deepavali day, the average noise level increased from 75.70 dB(A) in 2025 to 76.73 dB(A) in 2026, an increase of 1.03 dB(A).

In Chennai, Valasaravakkam recorded the highest noise level at 88.6 dB(A), followed by Sowcarpet at 86.2 dB(A). Thiruvottiyur recorded the lowest at 77.4 dB(A). The TNPCB attributed the increase in air and noise pollution to firecracker bursting and variations in meteorological conditions, including wind speed, wind direction, and atmospheric stability.

articles.title: Two teenagers arrested for robbing pedestrians at knife-point near Durgam Cheruvu Metro station
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Two 19-year-old men were arrested for allegedly robbing pedestrians at knife-point near Durgam Cheruvu Metro station in Madhapur.

The accused attacked a man with a knife after he resisted an attempt to snatch his mobile phone, leaving him with a bleeding injury on his shoulder. Madhapur police recovered two stolen mobile phones and the knife used in the robberies.
The accused were identified as Vanagandla Naresh, a labourer from Ambedkar Colony in Jubilee Hills, and Kurma Naveen, a resident of Masthan Nagar in Madhapur.

According to the police, the duo intercepted a man who was walking alone near Durgam Cheruvu Metro station and attempted to snatch his Vivo mobile phone. When he resisted, one of them attacked him with a knife, injuring his shoulder. They then forcibly took his phone and fled.
The two later committed another robbery using the same modus operandi, stealing a smartphone phone from another victim.
The Madhapur crime team apprehended them while they were moving around the Ayyappa Society.

When the police attempted to question them, the duo tried to escape but were caught. Two stolen mobile phones and a knife were recovered from their possession, police said. The accused were linked to two robbery cases registered at Madhapur police station. Further investigation is underway.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has extended the supersession of the board of Mumbai-based Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd. by another year, effective November 24, 2026, citing public interest.

“Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026,” the RBI said in a circular.

With the latest extension, Mr. Satya Prakash Pathak will continue as the bank’s Administrator. He will be assisted by the existing Committee of Advisors comprising Mr. Venkatesh Hegde, Mr. Devendra Kumar and Mr. Suhas Gokhale.

articles.title: Twenty-one migrants die trying to reach Greece’s Crete: authorities
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Eight bodies were found on one boat and 12 on another, while some 40 people were rescued off both, says Greek Coast Guard

Twenty-one people have died over the weekend trying to reach Greece’s island of Crete, a top destination for migrants headed for the European Union from Africa, authorities said on Monday (November 9, 2026).
Eight bodies were found on one boat and 12 on another, while some 40 people were rescued off both, the Greek coast guard said on Monday. Another body was later found on Monday afternoon.
Maritime police launched an emergency rescue late Saturday after a boat issued an alarm signal, with strong winds making sea conditions difficult, the coast guard said.
Around 28 survivors and one body, all Sudanese nationals, were picked up by another boat sailing nearby, then transferred to a police vessel and taken to Crete, authorities had said on Sunday.
Two Sudanese citizens, one of them 16, were arrested after being identified by the survivors as suspected people-smugglers, the authorities said.
During the night from Sunday to Monday, the coast guard found their boat, with seven additional bodies on board, it said.
In a separate incident, 12 bodies were found on a boat south of the island on Monday, while 18 people were rescued, the coast guard said.
In all, the Greek coast guard and the EU’s Frontex border agency rescued a total of 105 on Monday, according to the port authorities.
Crete has become one of the main entry points into the European Union for migrants departing from Libya and attempting the dangerous crossing to Greece.
Many of the attempted crossings turn deadly when the vessels sink or run into trouble.

articles.title: Children make up for half of Deepavali eye-injury cases at Hyderabad hospital
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Doctors say most patients were treated without surgery, but 10 individuals require surgical intervention, while bystanders also accounted for numerous injuries from a range of fireworks, underscoring the festival’s risk to ocular health

Nine-year-old Mokshit was among 15 patients admitted to the Burns Ward of the government-run Sarojini Devi Eye Hospital in Hyderabad following eye injuries during Deepavali celebrations. Brought all the way from Bhadrachalam, the boy was anxiously waiting for doctors to decide whether he needed surgery after a firecracker fragment struck his eye.

“My son was bursting a firecracker when suddenly a part of it flew off and hit his eye. My husband and I took him to a local hospital in Bhadrachalam, where the doctors said he might require surgery and advised us to bring him here. We are now waiting for the doctors to examine him and decide on the further course of treatment,” said Lakshmi, the boy’s mother.

Mokshit’s case is among several involving children, who accounted for half of the patients treated for firecracker-related eye injuries during Deepavali at the hospital. In sheer numbers, of the 87 patients who reported to Sarojini Devi Eye Hospital over November 7 and 8, a total of 37 were children.

Hospital superintendent Modini Pandharpurkar said 54 patients were treated during the corresponding period last year. She expects the numbers to rise over the next two to three days as more patients from districts are likely to reach Hyderabad for treatment.

Of the 15 patients admitted, 10 were scheduled to undergo surgery on Monday. Two adult patients had a poor prognosis while one child was expected to recover, according to the latest hospital update. articles.title: Police seize third video allegedly showing ‘Gem Granites’ Veeramani abusing minor
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The deleted content was retrieved by cyber forensic experts from a storage device, say police sources

The Greater Chennai Police have seized one more video purportedly showing Gem Granites owner R. Veeramani sexually abusing a minor girl, taking the total number of such videos recovered in the case to three, police sources said on Monday.

The deleted video, believed to have been recorded a few years ago, was retrieved by cyber forensic experts from a storage device seized from the premises of Shanthi, a close associate of Veeramani. “The video shows the octogenarian businessman in a compromising position with a minor. We suspect that Shanthi recorded the visuals and subsequently deleted them,” a police officer said.

Investigators are in the process of identifying the victim in the video. “This is the third video seized in the case and there could be more. With this fresh evidence and a witness in another case of child abuse coming forward as a complainant, the total number of victims has risen to 13,” the officer said. Besides Veeramani, Shanthi and her husband Mahendra Simhan, six other accused persons have so far been arrested in eight different cases and lodged in the Puzhal Central Prison.

Police sources said the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) and the Income Tax Department had been alerted about suspicious financial transactions detected during the investigation in the cases of alleged sexual abuse of minors involving Veeramani. The businessman and his close associates are facing seven cases under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and a case relating to the abetment of the suicide of a minor in 2004.

During the course of investigation, police uncovered substantial financial transactions between the Gem Group of Companies, owned by Veeramani, and a private individual, Prakash Kanniah. Investigators subsequently froze the latter’s bank accounts, which reportedly held several crores of rupees, the sources said.

Further inquiries revealed that gold bars weighing more than 20 kg had been purchased and delivered at a couple of locations in the city. However, the police could not trace the gold during searches conducted on the premises of the accused persons.
The transactions reportedly took place around the time Veeramani sold two parcels of land along the East Coast Road for a total consideration of about ₹80 crore, the sources said.

The transfer of substantial money to an individual projected as an adviser to the companies and the purchase of gold bars have come under scrutiny amid allegations that certain persons had used their influence to help Veeramani and his associates evade legal action despite a specific complaint of sexual abuse of a minor against them.
Questioning Prakash Kanniah who is said to be absconding and believed to be staying in the United Kingdom could throw more light on the transactions, the sources said.

“We suspect that money or gold could have changed hands as part of the larger conspiracy to help the accused persons. Hence, we intimated the ED and the Income Tax Department about the suspicious transactions,” the officer, who did not want to be quoted, said.

articles.title: Why Manaveeyam Veedhi is at the centre of a political battle between BJP, CPI(M) in Keralam capital
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The BJP-led Corporation has made clear its intent to make the street 'protest-free' and to keep it limited to cultural activities. Former Mayor and CPI(M) leader V. Sivankutty says the road is under the Public Works department and its management rights have never been transferred to the Corporation

Manaveeyam Veedhi, the cultural corridor of Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam, is now caught in a political battle between the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Communist Party of India (Marxist). The BJP, which took power in the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation in the local body elections last December, is attempting to bring about certain changes on the street, which has been hosting various cultural events as well as protest programmes for the past three decades.

The simmering issues came out into the open on October 16 when the Museum Police attempted to seize a microphone ahead of a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. According to CPI(M) leader and former Thiruvananthapuram Mayor V.Sivankutty, the denial of police permission for the event featuring actor-activist Prakash Raj was prompted by instructions from the Corporation authorities.

Last week, the BJP-led Corporation made clear its intent to make the street “protest-free” and to keep it limited to cultural activities, leading to protests by cultural activists who have been part of the street’s activities for a long time.

K.G. Suraj, secretary of the Manaveeyam Theruvidam Cultural Collective and Street Library, calls the move a blatant overreach of authority. He said that the Corporation’s move to render the space ‘protest-free’ by eliminating expressions of dissent is an encroachment upon the artists’ freedom of thought and expression.

“Manaveeyam Veedhi was constructed and subsequently renovated by the State government with the coordination of various government departments. Any claim by the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation to have regulatory control over Manaveeyam Veedhi is purely illusory. The community of artists and enthusiasts at Manaveeyam Veedhi holds the view that art and culture should serve as instruments for social progress and change. Manaveeyam Veedhi has a history of responding to emerging social issues through art, a tradition that has included protests, and will continue to do so,” he said.
According to Mr. Sivankutty, Manaveeyam Veedhi is a road under the Public Works department (PWD) and that its management rights have never been transferred to the Municipal Corporation.

“Everyone has the right to conduct art and cultural programmes on Manaveeyam Veedhi. However, such programmes must be organised in a manner that does not compromise the fundamental vision of the space. No licence is required to host appropriate art and cultural programmes on Manaveeyam Veedhi, nor has any single entity been authorised to oversee such activities. Typically, political parties do not hold events on Manaveeyam Veedhi. This is an established understanding. Yet, the BJP violated this consensus by organising an event there last week, emboldened by their hold on the city administration,” he said.

Congress councillor K.S. Sabarinadhan said that the Corporation must adopt a position that preserves Manaveeyam as a space that upholds all democratic rights. “It is unfortunate that the Corporation is now attempting to undermine the broad, culturally oriented vision behind Manaveeyam. If there are any allegations of illegal activities on the stretch, the authorities should conduct an investigation with the assistance of the police or implement enhanced security measures. Taking the stance that protests are impermissible within this cultural space is an anti-democratic measure,” he said.
According to the Mayor’s office, the Corporation will frame a bylaw for Manaveeyam Veedhi after discussions with various stakeholders.

The BJP-led Corporation has made clear its intent to make the street 'protest-free' and to keep it limited to cultural activities. Former Mayor and CPI(M) leader V. Sivankutty says the road is under the Public Works department and its management rights have never been transferred to the Corporation

Manaveeyam Veedhi, the cultural corridor of Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam, is now caught in a political battle between the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Communist Party of India (Marxist). The BJP, which took power in the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation in the local body elections last December, is attempting to bring about certain changes on the street, which has been hosting various cultural events as well as protest programmes for the past three decades.

The simmering issues came out into the open on October 16 when the Museum Police attempted to seize a microphone ahead of a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. According to CPI(M) leader and former Thiruvananthapuram Mayor V.Sivankutty, the denial of police permission for the event featuring actor-activist Prakash Raj was prompted by instructions from the Corporation authorities.

Last week, the BJP-led Corporation made clear its intent to make the street “protest-free” and to keep it limited to cultural activities, leading to protests by cultural activists who have been part of the street’s activities for a long time.

K.G. Suraj, secretary of the Manaveeyam Theruvidam Cultural Collective and Street Library, calls the move a blatant overreach of authority. He said that the Corporation’s move to render the space ‘protest-free’ by eliminating expressions of dissent is an encroachment upon the artists’ freedom of thought and expression.

“Manaveeyam Veedhi was constructed and subsequently renovated by the State government with the coordination of various government departments. Any claim by the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation to have regulatory control over Manaveeyam Veedhi is purely illusory. The community of artists and enthusiasts at Manaveeyam Veedhi holds the view that art and culture should serve as instruments for social progress and change. Manaveeyam Veedhi has a history of responding to emerging social issues through art, a tradition that has included protests, and will continue to do so,” he said.

According to Mr. Sivankutty, Manaveeyam Veedhi is a road under the Public Works department (PWD) and that its management rights have never been transferred to the Municipal Corporation.

“Everyone has the right to conduct art and cultural programmes on Manaveeyam Veedhi. However, such programmes must be organised in a manner that does not compromise the fundamental vision of the space. No licence is required to host appropriate art and cultural programmes on Manaveeyam Veedhi, nor has any single entity been authorised to oversee such activities. Typically, political parties do not hold events on Manaveeyam Veedhi. This is an established understanding. Yet, the BJP violated this consensus by organising an event there last week, emboldened by their hold on the city administration,” he said.

Congress councillor K.S. Sabarinadhan said that the Corporation must adopt a position that preserves Manaveeyam as a space that upholds all democratic rights. “It is unfortunate that the Corporation is now attempting to undermine the broad, culturally oriented vision behind Manaveeyam. If there are any allegations of illegal activities on the stretch, the authorities should conduct an investigation with the assistance of the police or implement enhanced security measures. Taking the stance that protests are impermissible within this cultural space is an anti-democratic measure,” he said.

According to the Mayor’s office, the Corporation will frame a bylaw for Manaveeyam Veedhi after discussions with various stakeholders.

articles.title: Four acres of encroached land reclaimed in Ballari; task force clears 150 acres
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The district administration carries out a drive in the city, demolishes a compound wall built on govt. land
The district administration on Monday carried out an anti-encroachment drive in Ballari city, demolishing a compound wall allegedly built on government land and encroaching upon a public road.
The demolition was carried out following allegations of encroachment on government land.

According to the district administration, 1 acre and 9 guntas of land in survey number 607/ 1A had been encroached upon and enclosed by a compound wall. The administration removed the structure as part of its drive to reclaim government land and public roads.

In a related development, the government has also reclaimed 2 acres and 30 guntas of land allotted to the Arogya Niketan Trust in the same survey number 14 years ago. The land had been allotted for the welfare of underprivileged children and children with disabilities.

As per the conditions of the allotment, the land was required to be utilised for the intended purpose within two years. However, as the trust failed to put the land to the stipulated use within the prescribed period, the administration completed the necessary legal procedures and cancelled the allotment, bringing the land back into government possession.
With these measures, the district administration has reclaimed approximately four acres of government land in the survey number.

Additional Deputy Commissioner Mohammed Zubair said that the district-level task force constituted to identify and clear encroachments on government land has reclaimed approximately 150 acres across the district so far.
He said that the administration will continue its efforts to protect government properties and remove encroachments.

articles.title: Keralam Excise dept. bans issuance of new liquor licences until promulgation of Keralam govt.’s liquor policy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The circular comes on the heels of the government shifting Sreeram Samabasiva Rao from the Excise Commissioner’s post in the wake of the political row over the department’s “hasty” reclassification of a few bars and beer parlours as bars and the almost “instantaneous” approval for private players to open lounge bars at CIAL

The Excise department has banned the issuance of new liquor licences, including for bars and wine and beer parlours, till the United Democratic Front (UDF) government promulgates its alcohol policy for the 2026-27 fiscal year on November 30.

Additional Excise Commissioner (Enforcement) R Jayasankar, who holds the charge of Excise Commissioner, barred Deputy Commissioners from issuing new bar licences, including permits for beer and wine parlours that have acquired four-star hotel classification, to sell hard spirits.

The circular comes on the heels of the government shifting Seeram Samabasiva Rao from the Excise Commissioner’s post in the wake of a political row over the department’s “hasty” reclassification of a few bars and beer parlours as bars and the almost “instantaneous” approval to private players to open lounge bars at Cochin International Airport Limited (CIAL). The government had cancelled the renewed licences, including for the lounge bars.

Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan and Excise Minister M. Liju had accused the Excise department of jumping the gun and blindsiding the government by granting licences before the UDF finalised its liquor policy.

Mr. Liju also signalled that the government would reverse the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) dispensation decision to vest the authority to grant licences with Excise Deputy Commissioners and mandate ministerial sanction for granting fresh alcohol permits.

Communist Party of India (Marxist) State secretariat member and former Excise Minister M.B. Rajesh pushed back, saying the Oommen Chandy government had empowered Deputy Excise Commissioners to sanction liquor licences and the LDF had not issued a single bar licence without ministerial consent.

The ruling alliance also seemed edgy that the expeditious issuance of bar licences might incense the UDF’s prohibitionist base comprising powerful Christian and Muslim social organisations. Moreover, the UDF government was also miffed that the issuance of bar licences appeared starkly selective, given that 29 applications were pending disposal in the Excise department.
Notably, the Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama (Kanthapuram AP faction) had condemned the granting of licences and accused the Excise eepartment of acting behind the government’s back.
Excise department officials said the government had put 29 bar license applications from four-star hotels on hold for now.

Communist Party of India (Marxist) State secretariat member and former Excise Minister M.B. Rajesh pushed back, saying the Oommen Chandy government had empowered Deputy Excise Commissioners to sanction liquor licences and the LDF had not issued a single bar licence without ministerial consent.

articles.title: Comedian Russell Brand sentenced to more than a decade in prison
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The judge referred to Brand as a “sexual predator”

British comedian and Hollywood star Russell Brand was sentenced to ten and a half years in prison for rape and sexual assault by the Southwark Crown Court in London on Monday (November 9, 2026). Brand, 51, was found guilty on Thursday (November 5, 2026) by the court of rape and three counts of sexual assault and not guilty on three other counts. He was charged in relation to a total of seven crimes. His crimes were committed between 2004 and 2009. The court found him guilty of raping a woman in 2009 at his home, after meeting her at a comedy show in the Hammersmith neighbourhood of London. Brand has the possibility of being released in about seven years subject to conditions, the judge said.

“The consequences of what happened have affected almost every aspect of my life. Even now, I continue to experience anxiety, difficulties with trust, reduced confidence and the lasting effects of trauma,” the woman who was raped said on Monday (November 9, 2026) at the sentencing.
One of his victims said she was in “shock and turmoil” and did not “have any respect” for herself as a result of the attack on her. The judge referred to Brand as a “sexual predator”.

Brand had argued during the trial that while his past behaviour had been “wrong”, he had never forced himself on anybody. The actor was formerly a left-wing activist. In the early years of the current decade, he moved to the right, becoming skeptical of vaccines and the origins of COVID-19, building bonds with big names in U.S. President Donald Trump’s Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement, including the President’s son, Donald Trump Jr., tech billionaire Elon Musk , commentators Alex Jones and Tucker Carlson, as well as Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the U.S. Health Secretary. In September, Brand participated in a video call event for the MAHA, Make America Healthy Again, movement, which is headed by Mr. Kennedy Jr. Brand converted to Christianity more recently and was baptized in the Thames in 2024.

articles.title: Dhaka wants Hasina extradited under prisoner exchange
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Hasina seeks fresh passport, but Minister Humayun Kabir calls ousted leader a “terrorist” and dismisses request; no response from MEA, sources say denial of passport may complicate matter if India were to extradite Hasina

Hours after a legal team representing deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina sought a new passport for her, the Government of Bangladesh asserted on Monday (November 9, 2026) that Ms. Hasina can return to Bangladesh through an “acceptable prisoner exchange” programme governed by the India-Bangladesh extradition treaty.
Speaking to the media in Dhaka, the country’s Acting Foreign Minister Humayun Kabir described Ms. Hasina as a “terrorist” who had fled to India after committing crimes.

A source in Dhaka told The Hindu that Ms. Hasina has requested the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, through a London-based legal firm, for a new passport and a National Identity Card. The official said the Ministry is verifying the letter and will take a final decision after internal consultations. Ms. Hasina’s passport was revoked soon after she escaped to India in August 2024 after an uprising toppled her government.

“Bangladesh will not issue a passport to any terrorist; there is no provision for such an action. Bangladesh will seek the return of Sheikh Hasina through an acceptable prisoner exchange process,” said Mr. Kabir, in response to questions from journalists regarding the request.

He noted that Ms. Hasina is a convict sentenced to death and has no legal or moral right to obtain a passport. Mr. Kabir said India should hand over the ousted Prime Minister under the extradition treaty. He added that Ms. Hasina and several of her colleagues from the Awami League are responsible for violent crimes and financial fraud, and need to be brought to justice.

The Ministry of External Affairs is yet to respond to Mr. Kabir’s remarks, but a source familiar with the Indian stance on the matter told The Hindu that the Bangladeshi position of not issuing a passport to Ms. Hasina will further complicate the matter, as a passport will be needed if India were to consider her extradition.

The Bangladeshi official, who spoke to The Hindu , said over the phone, “We have received an email from Matrix Chambers, a law firm in London, seeking a new passport for Sheikh Hasina. We are currently examining the contents of the letter and will take an appropriate step after internal consultation.”

However, the Press Secretary of the Bangladesh High Commission, Md. Saidur Rahman, said the Bangladesh authorities are “not sure if the request is genuine”. “There is no way for us to verify whether the request was actually made on behalf of Sheikh Hasina, as the email sent by the law firm did not include any authorisation letter or supporting documents proving that the firm was authorised by her to make such a request,” he said.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: ISRO needs more human and material resources to fulfil its mandate

With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 08 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

ISRO needs more human and material resources to fulfil its mandate

With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

articles.title: Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The world must act on Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities

Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

fullParagraphs: Tiruvannamalai Collector Vandhana Garg has warned residents in Cheyyar, Arani, Vandavasi, and Polur towns along Kamandalam Naganathi river against crossing the waterbody as the waterflow in the river is on the rise
Due to continuous rain, water from Shenbagathoppu dam in Tiruvannamalai was released.

Officials of Water Resources Department (WRD), which maintains the dam, said around 100 cusecs of water per second from Shenbagathoppu dam was released as the dam reached around 80 percent of its total storage capacity.

At present, the water level in the dam is 56.24 ft as against its total storage capacity of 62.32 ft. “As per norms, excess rainwater should be released when the dam nears 80% of its total storage capacity, to ensure safety of the structure. Catchment areas, especially Jawadhu Hills that is the primary water source of the dam, have been receiving steady rains,” A. Raja Ganapathy, Assistant Engineer (AE), WRD, told T he Hindu.

Tiruvannamalai Collector Vandhana Garg has warned residents in Cheyyar, Arani, Vandavasi, and Polur towns along Kamandalam Naganathi river against crossing the waterbody as the waterflow in the river is on the rise.

At present, excess water from the dam is discharged into 48 tanks—Polur (18), Arani (12), Arcot (9), Cheyyar (8), and Vandavasi (1)—through four check dams in the district, including Alliyabhad and Karnakur, thereby recharging the water table in and around these villages.
On Saturday, rain lashed Vellore, Gudiyatham, Arcot, Ambur, Vaniyambadi, Chengam and surrounding villages in Vellore, Ranipet, Tiruvannamalai, and Tirupattur districts.

articles.title: Renovated bus terminus in Ranipet town opened for public use
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Work to restore the terminus was started in 2022
After more than four years of renovation work, the restored ₹13.55-crore integrated bus terminus on the Ranipet-Walajah Main Road was opened for public use, ahead of Deepavali.

Officials of Ranipet municipality, which executed the multi-crore work, said that the old terminus was built more than five decades ago with very few facilities for commuters. “The restored terminus helps people board long-distance buses. The facility has better seating arrangements and safety features for commuters,” said S. Kumar, a commuter.

Funded under Kalaignar Nagarpura Membattu Thittam 2022-23 that aims to fulfil the infrastructural gaps in the urban local bodies, work to restore the terminus was started in 2022. “The restored bus terminus will help commuters, especially women and senior citizens to board buses safely as round-the-clock surveillance is in place. A help desk is also available to guide commuters,” said D. Senthil Kumar, Commissioner, Ranipet municipality.

Collector N. Priya Ravichandran inspected the restored bus terminus in the town in the presence of transport and municipal officials. The restored bus terminus will operate buses to Bengaluru, Vellore, Vandavasi, Cheyyar, Chengam, Arcot, Ranipet, Coimbatore, Salem, Kancheepuram, Hosur, and Dharmapuri.

Among civic amenities, the terminus has a purified drinking water facility, solar-powered LED streetlights, digital timing boards, feeding room, a police booth, and CCTV cameras. A police outpost will also be set up in the coming days.

Every day, on an average, more than 200 buses operated by Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation ply from the terminus. Commuters said that additional buses to towns such as Tiruvannamalai, Sholinghur, Arcot, Gingee, and Kancheepuram should be operated at the terminus.

articles.title: Greek-themed Salaam Souk to be held at Palace Grounds in Bengaluru on November 8
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Karnataka Tourism Department is supporting, ‘Salaam Souk – The Big Fat Greek Souk’, an event showcasing the colours, cuisine, music and Mediterranean culture of Greece to people in Bengaluru.

Scheduled to be held on November 8 in Palace Grounds, the event marks the eighth edition of Salaam Souk and its first Greek-themed edition. It is an initiative of The Tribe & Co that has previously presented cultural themes inspired by Morocco, Turkey, Uzbekistan, India and Dubai.

The festival has been designed to recreate the feel of a Greek street market, combining Mediterranean-inspired food, fashion, art, music, home décor, beauty and wellness experiences. The event will feature 35 food stalls, 150 retail stalls, live bands, fire shows and aerial performances, offering visitors a distinctive Greek-inspired cultural experience in Bengaluru.

Political & National Report: Greek-themed Salaam Souk to be held at Palace Grounds in Bengaluru on November 8. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

articles.title: Gang held near Vaniyambadi for burglary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police said that members of the gang befriended each other when they were serving jail sentences

A gang of five persons were arrested by Vaniyambadi Taluk police in Tirupattur on Saturday for stealing 52 sovereigns of gold jewellery, one kilogram of silver objects and around ₹20,000 lakh cash from the house of a painter recently.

The arrested persons were identified as K. Naveen, 26, T. Parthiban, 30, S. Gopinath, 39, G. Manikandan, 40, and C. Sarathkumar, 25. They are previous offenders and have theft cases against them in Salem, Dharmapuri, Tirupattur, Thanjavur, and Pudukottai.

Initial inquiry revealed that the victim, R. Prabhakaran, 39, was living with his family including wife Geetha (34) and mother Ambika (65) in the house near Vaniyambadi town a few days ago when the gang barged into the house. The police said the gang allegedly tied R. Prabhakaran, 39, and his family and stole the valuables from the house before fleeing the spot.

Mr. Prabhakaran managed to untie himself and alerted Vaniyambadi Taluk police. Special teams were formed to nab the suspects. The police also analysed CCTV camera footage to identify suspects. The suspects were traced to a hideout in Thanjavur and were arrested. A car used by the gang was also seized.

The police said that members of the gang befriended each other when they were serving jail sentences. They travel to various parts of the State and stay in a locality before indulging in burglary. A case was registered and a probe is under way.

articles.title: T.N. may be heading towards a water crisis, unless northeast monsoon comes to the rescue
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: As of now, the aggregate storage in the major 15 irrigation reservoirs is about a third of the combined capacity of the reservoirs. In the corresponding period last year, the combined storage was around 92%
Tamil Nadu may be in for a spell of water crisis and lower rice production this time if the current Northeast monsoon does not come to its rescue.

As of now, the aggregate storage in the major 15 irrigation reservoirs is about a third of the combined capacity of the reservoirs. In the corresponding period last year, the situation was completely different with the combined storage being around 92%.

The State’s largest dam, Mettur, has about 23 thousand million cubic feet (tmcft) but this is hardly enough for the authorities to maintain sustained release of water to farmers, beyond a week, in the Cauvery delta.

The rainfall during the Northeast monsoon has been moderate as the State has received around 240 mm of rainfall against the anticipated 236 mm. It should get at least 260 mm more to be considered comfortable, the most of which should materialise in November. Ordinarily, December yields only about 20% of the total rainfall of the monsoon.

In fact, the existing pattern of rainfall registered by the State so far during the season appears to be more in tune with the forecast made by the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), which, in late September, predicted that the State would get 438 mm during the entire monsoon against the normal 434 mm, a deviation of one per cent. The Meteorological department, in its outlook at the beginning of October for the season, referred to the southern peninsular region of the country in general and stated that the expected rainfall “ is most likely to be normal (88-112%) of the Long Period Average (LPA).”

The TNAU, which was more specific in its forecast than the Meteorological department, had anticipated only a normal rainfall for the core districts of the Cauvery delta – Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam and Mayiladuthurai. Despite the water availability at Mettur not being comfortable and the expectation of a subdued rainfall, farmers have gone in for raising paddy during the samba-thaladi cultivation season to the tune of around 3.62 lakh hectares. Of this, nearly 50% falls under “direct sown“ category of cultivation, which means that seeds are directly sown instead of transplantation. This method is followed in times of water shortage.

But, the problem with water availability seems to be higher in the remaining areas of the State, a reflection of which can be seen in the way the farmers have taken to paddy this time. The paddy coverage in the non-delta areas of the State is about 1.3 lakh hectares shorter than what it was last year. As compared to the previous year’s share (39%) of direct sowing in the overall paddy coverage, this time the method’s share is about 57%. In 2025-26, rice production in the State was 77.5 lakh tonnes, about one lakh tonnes lower than the previous high of 79.07 lakh tonnes during 2021-22.

As part of its efforts for protecting the crop in the Cauvery delta, the State government, at meetings of the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) and the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) on Friday, demanded that Karnataka release around 20. 7 tmcft including the backlog of about 16.9 tmc ft. However, the Authority ratified the decision of the Committee, which had recommended that Karnataka release 3.88 tmcft to Tamil Nadu through 3,000 cubic feet per second (cusecs) per day for 15 days from Saturday (November 7, 2026).

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 08 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 5 Min Read

📰 T.N. may be heading towards a water crisis, unless northeast monsoon comes to the rescue

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

As of now, the aggregate storage in the major 15 irrigation reservoirs is about a third of the combined capacity of the reservoirs. In the corresponding period last year, the combined storage was around 92%

Tamil Nadu may be in for a spell of water crisis and lower rice production this time if the current Northeast monsoon does not come to its rescue.

As of now, the aggregate storage in the major 15 irrigation reservoirs is about a third of the combined capacity of the reservoirs. In the corresponding period last year, the situation was completely different with the combined storage being around 92%.

The State’s largest dam, Mettur, has about 23 thousand million cubic feet (tmcft) but this is hardly enough for the authorities to maintain sustained release of water to farmers, beyond a week, in the Cauvery delta.

The rainfall during the Northeast monsoon has been moderate as the State has received around 240 mm of rainfall against the anticipated 236 mm. It should get at least 260 mm more to be considered comfortable, the most of which should materialise in November. Ordinarily, December yields only about 20% of the total rainfall of the monsoon.

In fact, the existing pattern of rainfall registered by the State so far during the season appears to be more in tune with the forecast made by the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), which, in late September, predicted that the State would get 438 mm during the entire monsoon against the normal 434 mm, a deviation of one per cent. The Meteorological department, in its outlook at the beginning of October for the season, referred to the southern peninsular region of the country in general and stated that the expected rainfall “ is most likely to be normal (88-112%) of the Long Period Average (LPA).”

The TNAU, which was more specific in its forecast than the Meteorological department, had anticipated only a normal rainfall for the core districts of the Cauvery delta – Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam and Mayiladuthurai. Despite the water availability at Mettur not being comfortable and the expectation of a subdued rainfall, farmers have gone in for raising paddy during the samba-thaladi cultivation season to the tune of around 3.62 lakh hectares. Of this, nearly 50% falls under “direct sown“ category of cultivation, which means that seeds are directly sown instead of transplantation. This method is followed in times of water shortage.

But, the problem with water availability seems to be higher in the remaining areas of the State, a reflection of which can be seen in the way the farmers have taken to paddy this time. The paddy coverage in the non-delta areas of the State is about 1.3 lakh hectares shorter than what it was last year. As compared to the previous year’s share (39%) of direct sowing in the overall paddy coverage, this time the method’s share is about 57%. In 2025-26, rice production in the State was 77.5 lakh tonnes, about one lakh tonnes lower than the previous high of 79.07 lakh tonnes during 2021-22.

As part of its efforts for protecting the crop in the Cauvery delta, the State government, at meetings of the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) and the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) on Friday, demanded that Karnataka release around 20. 7 tmcft including the backlog of about 16.9 tmc ft. However, the Authority ratified the decision of the Committee, which had recommended that Karnataka release 3.88 tmcft to Tamil Nadu through 3,000 cubic feet per second (cusecs) per day for 15 days from Saturday (November 7, 2026).
