articles.title: Kremlin hopes U.S. election shake-up won't shift Trump's negotiations on Ukraine
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Republicans' defeat in the U.S. midterm elections was watched closely in Russia, where some observers are predicting it could herald more support for Ukraine when the Democrats take over Congress in January.
But if the Kremlin is hearing the ticking of a clock on its nearly 5-year-old full-scale invasion of its neighbour, it seemingly remains unperturbed.

Asked if the election's outcome could stymie U.S. attempts to help negotiate a settlement between Moscow and Kyiv, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov voiced hope that U.S. President Donald Trump will continue to pursue his peace efforts.

“There is groundwork already in place, and another round of trilateral negotiations is set to take place very soon,” Mr. Peskov said of talks planned for Tuesday (November 10, 2026) and Wednesday (November 11) involving Russian, Ukrainian and U.S. representatives in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.
He also praised the “successful humanitarian peace-building efforts” by first lady Melania Trump, adding that “we hope that all of this will continue.”
Last week's limited ceasefire around the Russia-occupied city of Oleshky, brokered with her help, allowed for the delivery of humanitarian aid and the evacuation of some residents.
Mr. Peskov shrugged off a question from reporters on whether the new Congress would challenge Mr. Trump's stance on Russia and Ukraine. He called it an “internal matter” for the U.S.
In recent months, Mr. Trump's actions appeared to favour Moscow

Last month, he struck a diesel fuel import deal with Russia in a stunning reversal of years of U.S. pressure on the Kremlin, to the dismay of Ukraine and its European allies. He also claimed that Kyiv's attacks on Russian oil refineries caused a spike in diesel prices in the U.S. He urged Kyiv to halt the strikes, even though rising global energy prices were largely driven by the Iran war.

Mr. Trump also issued an executive order to put on hold sweeping new sanctions that clamped down on the Russian economy, telling Congress the pause was in the national interest. Lawmakers from both parties blasted Mr. Trump's move as benefiting Russian President Vladimir Putin.

articles.title: New Zealanders won’t know for weeks who won election as neither side secures clear victory
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The tightest vote in years delivered a stinging rebuke to the major parties which have long dominated New Zealand politics, Christopher Luxon’s centre-right National party and centre-left Labour led by Chris Hipkins

New Zealanders will wait for weeks to discover who will lead the country after Saturday's (November 7, 2026) election failed to deliver a decisive win for the right or the left, leaving fraught negotiations for a wafer-thin governing majority the only apparent path to victory for either side.

The tightest vote in years delivered a stinging rebuke to the major parties which have long dominated New Zealand politics, Christopher Luxon's centre-right National party and centre-left Labour led by Chris Hipkins, as voters threw more support behind minor parties on the ideological flanks than before.
On Saturday's (November 7) numbers, minor parties would enter negotiations for a governing deal with leverage to extract deeper policy concessions from a weakened National or Labour.

The near-deadlock was partly produced because voters, apparently weary of New Zealand's economic woes and apathetic about both Luxon and Hipkins, chose to propel a new entrant group to Parliament for the first time in years.
Opportunity, led by 38-year-old business consultant and political newcomer Qiulae Wong, is unaligned with either bloc and Ms. Wong has said she could work with either side to form a government.

Ms. Wong's pledges of evidence-based centrism and an end to partisan bickering had on Saturday's (November 7) results secured seven seats for Opportunity — enough to frustrate both left and right in a simple path to power.
It was a staggering ascension for a party that made three failed attempts at Parliament before Ms. Wong became leader less than a year ago.

Other winners were harder to identify and on Sunday (November 8), “who won the election 2026” was the top trending Google search in New Zealand. So unclear was the result that parties won't begin negotiations to form a government until final tallies are released on November 27, confirming the exact number of seats they've won.

With 2.8 million ballots counted on election night, the conservative incumbent government led by Luxon's National party appeared close to the slimmest possible return to power — by just one seat. However, Mr. Luxon didn't claim victory, instead striking a note of cautious optimism that he could negotiate a second term in power.

Speaking to reporters Sunday (November 8), Luxon blamed public dissatisfaction on global shocks which have buffeted New Zealand's trade-based economy, noting that other incumbent governments worldwide have faced voters' rancor over living costs.

🌐 International & Geopolitics 📅 08 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 New Zealanders won’t know for weeks who won election as neither side secures clear victory

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

The tightest vote in years delivered a stinging rebuke to the major parties which have long dominated New Zealand politics, Christopher Luxon’s centre-right National party and centre-left Labour led by Chris Hipkins

New Zealanders will wait for weeks to discover who will lead the country after Saturday's (November 7, 2026) election failed to deliver a decisive win for the right or the left, leaving fraught negotiations for a wafer-thin governing majority the only apparent path to victory for either side.

The tightest vote in years delivered a stinging rebuke to the major parties which have long dominated New Zealand politics, Christopher Luxon's centre-right National party and centre-left Labour led by Chris Hipkins, as voters threw more support behind minor parties on the ideological flanks than before.

On Saturday's (November 7) numbers, minor parties would enter negotiations for a governing deal with leverage to extract deeper policy concessions from a weakened National or Labour.

The near-deadlock was partly produced because voters, apparently weary of New Zealand's economic woes and apathetic about both Luxon and Hipkins, chose to propel a new entrant group to Parliament for the first time in years.

Opportunity, led by 38-year-old business consultant and political newcomer Qiulae Wong, is unaligned with either bloc and Ms. Wong has said she could work with either side to form a government.

Ms. Wong's pledges of evidence-based centrism and an end to partisan bickering had on Saturday's (November 7) results secured seven seats for Opportunity — enough to frustrate both left and right in a simple path to power.

It was a staggering ascension for a party that made three failed attempts at Parliament before Ms. Wong became leader less than a year ago.

Other winners were harder to identify and on Sunday (November 8), “who won the election 2026” was the top trending Google search in New Zealand. So unclear was the result that parties won't begin negotiations to form a government until final tallies are released on November 27, confirming the exact number of seats they've won.

With 2.8 million ballots counted on election night, the conservative incumbent government led by Luxon's National party appeared close to the slimmest possible return to power — by just one seat. However, Mr. Luxon didn't claim victory, instead striking a note of cautious optimism that he could negotiate a second term in power.

Speaking to reporters Sunday (November 8), Luxon blamed public dissatisfaction on global shocks which have buffeted New Zealand's trade-based economy, noting that other incumbent governments worldwide have faced voters' rancor over living costs.

articles.title: Vijayan demands withdrawal of circular allowing colleges to increase seats without Keralam Govt nod
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The CPI(M) veteran said a September 11 circular issued by the Higher Education Department had made prior government approval mandatory for introducing new courses and increasing seats in government, aided and autonomous colleges

LoP in the Keralam Assembly Pinarayi Vijayan on Sunday (November 8, 2026) alleged that the State government's move to allow autonomous aided and self-financing colleges to increase seats without prior approval would lead to the commercialisation of education.
Demanding the immediate withdrawal of the government circular permitting the move, Mr. Vijayan said the decision had been taken under pressure from the managements of private colleges.

The CPI(M) veteran said a September 11 circular issued by the Higher Education Department had made prior government approval mandatory for introducing new courses and increasing seats in government, aided and autonomous colleges.

He contended that the government had now relaxed the norms, despite the existing provision ensuring strict scrutiny and regulation at the government level, by "succumbing to the misguided pressures of the managements".

"The current provision that no government no-objection certificate (NOC) is required for starting unaided courses and increasing seats in autonomous aided and self-financing colleges is shocking," the former CM said.

He said allowing colleges to increase seats at their discretion, without assessing the necessity and disregarding existing regulatory mechanisms, would pave the way for the commercialisation of education.
"This ill-conceived collusion is taking place despite the assurances given before the Supreme Court that self-financing courses would not be allowed in aided colleges on a large scale," he contended.
Mr. Vijayan questioned whose interests the government was protecting by granting such sweeping concessions immediately after representatives of college managements met the Higher Education Minister.

He alleged that doing away with annual inspections and allowing colleges to inform the government about seat increases only after the admission process was over amounted to "a clear conspiracy to sell seats by taking bribes by subverting the provisions of merit and reservation".
He claimed that such measures would effectively dismantle government regulation and undermine the educational rights of ordinary people, particularly the poor.

articles.title: Agitation against CEC will go on till he is removed: Venugopal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘We will withdraw from this agitation only after Gyanesh Kumar is removed from the post and steps are taken to make India's electoral system and processes flawless, impartial and fair,’ said K.C. Venugopal

AICC general secretary K.C. Venugopal on Sunday (November said the Congress-led agitation against CEC Gyanesh Kumar would continue until he was removed from the post and the country's electoral system was made impartial and transparent.
Speaking to reporters in Alappuzha, Mr. Venugopal said protests were continuing across states and districts, with only a brief pause expected during the Deepavali festival.

He described the November 1 rally organised by the Congress in New Delhi as one of the strongest protests witnessed in the country, saying the party was fighting against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah.

"We will withdraw from this agitation only after Gyanesh Kumar is removed from the post and steps are taken to make India's electoral system and processes flawless, impartial and fair. This is not a struggle that we will abandon midway," he said.

Venugopal alleged that the deletion of names from electoral rolls would deprive poor people of their voting rights and access to various government benefits, which, he claimed, were increasingly being linked to voter identity cards.
He said the Congress would launch a nationwide 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao' (Save the Vote, Save the Nation) campaign at the panchayat level over the next one-and-a-half months.

As part of the campaign, the party would appoint a 'Vote Rakshak' (guardian) in every polling booth to scrutinise electoral rolls, identify people whose names had been deleted and visit their homes to help them get their names restored, he said.
Congress units were organising programmes across states and districts, while plans were also being drawn up for joint programmes with other political parties, he said.
Mr. Venugopal said the issue would be strongly raised during the upcoming Parliament session, adding that the Opposition would take up recent controversies and issues affecting the public.
Referring to the previous Parliament session, he claimed that Amit Shah could not enter the House for nearly two weeks because of the Opposition's protests.

articles.title: Thane court sentences man to 20 years rigorous imprisonment for raping minor on promise of marriage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Four prosecution witnesses, including the survivor, her mother and neighbour, were examined to prove the charges against the accused
A special court in Maharashtra's Thane district has sentenced a 35-year-old man to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment for repeatedly raping a minor girl after promising to marry her.

Additional Sessions Judge Premal S. Vithalani convicted the accused, Shrinivas Ashok Yelgonda, a painter, under relevant sections of the Indian Penal Code and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, noting that while the absence of violence and premeditation was a mitigating factor, the law mandated a minimum 20-year term.

According to the prosecution, the victim resided in the same housing society in Diva East as the accused, and the two became acquainted in June 2020 and subsequently developed a romantic relationship through phone chats.

Special public prosecutor Rekha Hiwrale stated that the accused first sexually assaulted the minor in November 2020 inside a neighbour's vacant apartment by promising to marry her, and later raped her on several occasions. The abuse came to light in February 2022 when a dispute arose after the accused reneged on his promise to marry her.
Four prosecution witnesses, including the survivor, her mother and neighbour, were examined to prove the charges against the accused.

The defence argued that there was an unexplained delay in registering the FIR in 2022, and that exact dates of the recurring assaults were missing. However, relying on the survivor's birth certificate and school leaving certificate, the court verified that she was a "child" under 18 years of age during the major part of the abuse timeline, rendering her legal consent immaterial.

"The evidence on record clearly establishes that the victim was under the bona fide impression that the accused would solemnise marriage with her, which led her to keep the relationship and the repeated physical intimacies concealed from her parents," the judge observed.
The subsequent deliberation by the family before approaching the police is both natural and understandable given the social stigma, honour, and future of an unmarried girl, the court said.
It also noted that there was no evidence of brutal force, physical injury or premeditated sexual predation.

"While the victim's minority under the age of 18 renders her consent legally ineffective and makes the conviction unavoidable, the romantic backdrop remains a vital and compelling mitigating factor in sentencing," it stated.

articles.title: Dangerous harmonies: Is there a hidden villain in India’s devastating electrical fires?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Electrical causes are predominating in India’s recent fire incidents; while codes and guidelines are covering these increasingly, there are still major gaps such as taking into account harmonic currents put into the system by state-of-the-art electronics equipment
Just after 3.48 a.m. on May 3, 2026, fire ripped through a four-storey building in Vivek Vihar, East Delhi, killing nine. The suspected origin was an AC blast or short circuit.

Ten newborns died in an overcrowded Jhansi NICU in November 2024, a unit meant for 18 babies packed with 55. Three newborns in Amravati this August, dead not from flame but from smoke inhalation, even though the fire itself was out within 30 minutes. One newborn in Chhindwara two days before that. Ten patients at Cuttack’s SCB Medical College this March, when a short circuit in a trauma-ICU air-conditioner ignited an oxygen-rich ward at 3 a.m.

Fire accidents in India used to happen in industrial units, firecracker factories and mass gatherings. No more. The more devastating ones happen right in our neighbourhoods, in hospitals and high-rises. They are almost always triggered by electrical fires.

Delhi Fire Service attributes over 80% of the capital’s fires to electrical faults. Mumbai Fire Brigade, analysing 26,855 incidents over five years, attributes nearly three in four to the same cause. New Delhi alone saw a 37% rise in residential fires this year over last, with roughly 70% traced to short-circuiting, faulty wiring, overheating, and overloaded circuits. The National Crime Records Bureau recorded 7,566 fire accidents and 7,435 deaths in 2022, with short circuit consistently among the largest single causes.

Indian electricity demand hit 256.11 GW on April 25 this year, against air temperatures of 47 degrees, roughly double the early-2010s peak. A/Cs draw about 50 GW at peak. And projections place the A/C load at 180 GW in another 10 years. Indians bought more than 15 million air-conditioners in 2025 alone, and the International Energy Agency expects the installed base to climb from 93 million units in 2024 to 240 million by 2030.

Air-conditioners draw heavy current that electrical systems in older buildings are unable to withstand, resulting in the wiring burning up. What’s called an A/C blast is the overworked compressor in the refrigeration exploding due to sheer heat caused by overworking. Investigation into these fires has been hampered by shortage of certified fire forensic investigators. Too often, the causes are dismissed as blasts or short circuits. Root cause analysis and systemic remedies are rarely formulated.

An electrical circuit has three parts. The load is whatever draws current. It could be just a light or an air-conditioner. The wiring carries that current, insulated to keep two conductors from touching. The protection device, typically a miniature circuit breaker, is meant to cut the current flow the instant something goes wrong. The circuit breaker switches off the current within about a tenth of a second for a short circuit, or within a longer window, from a minute to an hour, for a sustained overload. A fire needs two failures at once: something in the load or wiring goes wrong, and the protection device fails to trip in time.

A peer-reviewed 2025 review in the journal Fire identifies six recurring failure modes behind that first failure: short circuits, overloads, loose or oxidised connections, series and parallel arc faults, ground faults, and equipment ageing. Of these, a loose connection is often the quietest killer. Research on wiring practice, cited in Indian engineering literature reviewing fire risk in electrical installations, shows that loose terminal connections, whether from bad workmanship, thermal expansion and contraction, or simple ageing, create a phenomenon called glowing contact: a slow-building hot spot that can smoulder in a wall or panel for months before anything is visible from outside.

There is a second, slower mechanism that gets far less attention and could explain a great deal about how India’s fires happen: harmonics. Every inverter-driven air-conditioner, along with every UPS, LED driver, ventilator and EV charger, draws current in short, jagged pulses rather than a smooth wave. This injects distortion into the electrical supply at multiples of the base 50 Hz frequency. In three-phase buildings, certain harmonic orders, called triplen harmonics, do not cancel out in the neutral conductor the way normal, balanced current does. Instead they add up. The neutral wire, which was never designed to be load-bearing and carries no circuit breaker of its own, quietly overheats. A loose joint nearby could make an overheated neutral become an ignition source ripping up ordinary insulation.

Fire investigators suspect that many chemicals and solvents are used in ICUs and the vapours they generate don’t get evacuated well-known enough because of poor maintenance of ventilation systems. They point out that ICUs have dedicated ventilation systems and need much care. While these vapours provide the fuel, a source of heat is required for ignition. And that is where harmonics-generated heating could come into play, says a fire forensic engineer who didn’t wish to be named. “Electrical fires are a gray area and require a lot of precautions. Sadly, in India, compliance with regulations is considered a financial burden,” he adds.

articles.title: Taiwan detains Communist Party leader over alleged Chinese sponsorship in election
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Authorities in Taiwan detained the leader of the island's Taiwan People's Communist Party, accusing him of running as a candidate for borough chief under the direction and sponsorship of China's Communist Party, local media reported on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

Taiwan is set to hold elections for mayors and local area chiefs on November 28. While the races focus more on livelihood issues, the results could be a good indicator of the popularity of the ruling Democratic Progressive Party under the leadership of Taiwan President Lai Ching-te ahead of the presidential election in 2028.

According to Taiwan's Central News Agency, prosecutors said in a statement on Sunday (November 8, 2026) that an initial investigation showed Taiwan People's Communist Party chair Lin Te-wang also had directed another party member to run as a candidate for chief in another borough.
Prosecutors also alleged that Mr. Lin sought to buy votes by repeatedly recruiting voters to travel to mainland China, where they received hospitality, the report said.

While Mr. Lin's party is not influential on the democratic island, it was not his first legal trouble over his alleged links with China. He and another party leader had faced charges of Chinese infiltration and attempting to influence elections but were found not guilty in 2025, the Taipei Times reported.
Taiwan's Central News Agency said the prosecutors had received intelligence about foreign interference in the election and summoned 14 people and nine witnesses.

After questioning, the government lawyers strongly suspected that Lin and the other party member had committed a crime and were concerned the pair could flee or destroy evidence, so they filed applications to the local courts to detain them and bar them from being visited by others, it said.

The courts ruled in the prosecutors' favour for Lin but released the other member on a 50,000-Taiwan-dollar ($1,525) bail, the news agency said. The other people summoned were released during the investigation, it added.
China's Taiwan Affairs Office has not immediately commented.
Beijing views Taiwan as a breakaway province to be retaken by force if necessary, and claims of China's meddling are common in Taiwanese elections.

Multiple witnesses told AFP on Sunday (November 8, 2026) that Riyadh's financial district was targeted and the area's Aramco tower was damaged, after the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said it had intercepted missiles launched by the group.
"Aramco tower in KAFD has been targeted, that's the sure thing," said one witness, referring to the King Abdullah Financial District. Two other witnesses confirmed seeing damage to the building.

A 2022 truce that had paused fighting in Yemen's long-running conflict fell apart in July and Saudi Arabia has since traded blows with the Houthis, who have struck Saudi airports, energy infrastructure and military sites.
The Iran-backed Houthis seized the Yemeni capital Sanaa in 2014, with the Saudi-led coalition entering the conflict a year later in support of the government.

The King Abdullah Financial District is one of the most visible manifestations of the kingdom's ongoing economic and social reforms drive, with towering glass skyscrapers, high-end retail outlets and green spaces dotting the area.
Targeting the district would mark a major escalation in the kingdom's fight with the Houthis.
The area is also home to residential housing and a large metro station with heavy commuter traffic during the morning rush hour.
Multiple floors of the Aramco tower appeared to have sustained damage, said another witness, with glass shattered and damage to part of the tower's facade visible.

The attack comes hours after the Kingdom's education ministry announced, late on Saturday (November 7, 2026), the return of in-person schooling after weeks of remote-learning in Riyadh following an earlier wave of strikes.

Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki, in a Sunday (November 8, 2026) morning social media post, said that "air defences intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi terrorist militia towards Riyadh", as loud explosions were heard in the Saudi capital.

"Aramco tower in KAFD has been targeted, that's the sure thing," said one witness, referring to the King Abdullah Financial District. Two other witnesses confirmed seeing damage to the building.

A 2022 truce that had paused fighting in Yemen's long-running conflict fell apart in July and Saudi Arabia has since traded blows with the Houthis, who have struck Saudi airports, energy infrastructure and military sites.

The Iran-backed Houthis seized the Yemeni capital Sanaa in 2014, with the Saudi-led coalition entering the conflict a year later in support of the government.

The King Abdullah Financial District is one of the most visible manifestations of the kingdom's ongoing economic and social reforms drive, with towering glass skyscrapers, high-end retail outlets and green spaces dotting the area.

Targeting the district would mark a major escalation in the kingdom's fight with the Houthis.

The area is also home to residential housing and a large metro station with heavy commuter traffic during the morning rush hour.

Multiple floors of the Aramco tower appeared to have sustained damage, said another witness, with glass shattered and damage to part of the tower's facade visible.

The attack comes hours after the Kingdom's education ministry announced, late on Saturday (November 7, 2026), the return of in-person schooling after weeks of remote-learning in Riyadh following an earlier wave of strikes.

Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki, in a Sunday (November 8, 2026) morning social media post, said that "air defences intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi terrorist militia towards Riyadh", as loud explosions were heard in the Saudi capital.

articles.title: Bangladesh Law Minister calls Hasina ‘convicted criminal’, says extradition request sent to India
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Indian govt previously acknowledged receiving Bangladesh's extradition requests for Ms. Hasina but has not announced any decision on handing her over

Bangladesh's Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman on Sunday (November 8, 2026) described ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina as a "convicted criminal" and said Dhaka has requested India to extradite her, according to local media reports.

Responding to questions from journalists after inaugurating a training workshop in Dhaka, Mr. Asaduzzaman said the government was taking all necessary legal steps to bring Ms. Hasina back from India and would follow due process.
"To me, she is a criminal. A criminal convicted by our tribunal. To us, this is her identity," he said, according to a report on bdnews24 website.
Asked about bringing Ms. Hasina back to Bangladesh, the Law Minister said the government would act in accordance with the law and would not be guided by emotion.

"Although the Law Ministry is not directly involved in this matter, the Ministry of Home Affairs is concerned, as it relates to the extradition treaty with India. The matter will be dealt with in accordance with the law, leaving no room for emotions. We have requested her repatriation under the treaty and through due process," Mr. Asaduzzaman was quoted as saying by the state-run BSS news agency.
Bdnews24 also quoted Mr. Asaduzzaman as saying: "That is a matter for the Indian government. We have made requests to them under the extradition treaty."
"If they hand her over to us, we will hand her over in the due process, as required under the law," he added.

India has previously acknowledged receiving Bangladesh's extradition requests for Ms. Hasina but has not announced any decision on handing her over. The Ministry of External Affairs has said the requests are being examined as part of its established processes.
Ms. Hasina fled Bangladesh for India on August 5, 2024, following a mass uprising that ended her 15-year rule. An interim government led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus subsequently took charge.

articles.title: Fresh sexual harassment complaint against ‘Gem Granites’ Veeramani
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Action has been initiated based on the statement of the minor, who was previously a witness in an already registered case

In a fresh development in the ongoing probe against granite baron R Veeramani , who is facing charges of sexually harassing minors, another girl has come forward with a complaint of harassment, police said on Sunday.
Action has been initiated based on the statement of the minor, who was previously a witness in an already registered case, they said.

The case traces back to October 2025 when a child rights activist handed over a pen drive to the Anti-Vice Squad containing a video of a minor being sexually assaulted. A note accompanying the drive alleged that the man in the footage was Veeramani and that the incident occurred at the residence of Mahendra Simhan and Shanthi.

Although the police initially attempted to file a closure report citing an inability to identify the victim, a Special POCSO court judge rejected the move in February 2026 and ordered further investigation.
Following the court's intervention, police recovered the original video during searches and subsequently arrested Mr. Veeramani, Ms. Shanthi, and Mahendra Simhan in August 2026.
A Special Investigation Team was later constituted to probe the allegations.
The police have now registered a total of eight cases concerning the sexual harassment of minors. Mr. Veeramani has been arrested in all eight cases.

The other accused include Ms. Shanthi, arrested in three cases, Lazar in five cases, Mahendra Simhan in two cases, and Ganesan in two cases. Srinivasan, Sakthivel, Babu, and Parthiban have been arrested in one case each.
All the accused are currently lodged at the Puzhal Central Prison in Chennai.

During the ongoing investigation, accused driver Mr. Lazar was taken into one-day police custody for interrogation. Based on this inquiry, authorities identified a white car used in the crime and initiated subsequent action.

articles.title: Punjab anti-drug activist Jhota cremated in his native place Mansa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jhota was shot dead in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town on October 13

The mortal remains of slain anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, whose murder 26 days ago triggered protests and a political row, were consigned to flames at his native place here on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
A large number of people had turned up when last rites were held after his body was brought here from Chandigarh, following a post-mortem at PGIMER on Saturday (November 7, 2026).
The cremation was held at Jhota’s fields on Chakerian Road.

Jhota was shot dead on October 13 in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town while he was hosting a Facebook Live session. The store owner, who had fired at Jhota after the activist confronted him over the sale of addictive drugs to an elderly man, was subsequently arrested.
A number of people also turned up at his home to pay their last respects before the cremation was held.
Jhota’s father, Bhim Singh, called upon the youth of Punjab to pledge against drug abuse, saying his son gave up his life fighting against the scourge.
“I thank the joint action committee which stood by us all through,” he told reporters on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
The joint action committee (JAC), also known as the Parminder Singh Jhota Insaaf Action Committee, is a coalition of various social organisations and activists formed in Punjab after Jhota’s murder.

Jhota’s body was brought to PGIMER Chandigarh from the mortuary of Civil Hospital in Mansa in the early hours of Friday (November 6, 2026), after his family ended their 22-day agitation and agreed to a post-mortem following a meeting with Punjab government representatives on Wednesday (November 4).
The anti-drug activist’s family, along with the JAC, had been sitting on a protest in Mansa seeking justice for the slain activist.

articles.title: No concrete proof yet from Indonesia for claim over rescued orangutans: Odisha Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Minister said some countries might stake a claim to the animals under international wildlife trade regulations, but they would have to furnish concrete evidence to establish that the rescued animals originated from their territory

Neither Indonesia nor any other country has so far provided documentary evidence to establish ownership of five baby orangutans rescued from a forest in Odisha two months ago, state Forest Minister Ganesh Ram Singh Khuntia said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
Speaking to reporters, Mr. Khuntia said all five orangutans were doing well , and expressed the State's desire to retain them at Nandankanan Zoological Park.
"All five baby orangutans are doing well and growing. No one should disturb them. We want them to stay in Odisha, and visitors will get an opportunity to see them at Nandankanan Zoo," he said.

The Minister said some countries might stake a claim to the animals under international wildlife trade regulations, but they would have to furnish concrete evidence to establish that the rescued animals originated from their territory.

"The Indonesian government has raised its claim as a routine matter. We will seek evidence to establish that the orangutans originated from their country. If they provide the proof, the animals may be handed over to them," Mr. Khuntia said.
He added that the State government had submitted details of the rescued animals to the Centre for necessary action.
"Odisha has a conducive environment for orangutans. So, we want them to stay here," he said.
The five baby orangutans were rescued from Bichitrapur forest in Balasore district on September 8 and subsequently shifted to Nandankanan Zoo, where they have been kept in quarantine.
Officials said the animals were housed in a temperature-controlled room and were gradually acclimatising to the local environment.

The State government has made arrangements for their comfort and to help them overcome stress. The animals have displayed a range of emotions, from playful behaviour and brief mood swings to anxiously clinging to one another, they said.

The Minister said some countries might stake a claim to the animals under international wildlife trade regulations, but they would have to furnish concrete evidence to establish that the rescued animals originated from their territory

Neither Indonesia nor any other country has so far provided documentary evidence to establish ownership of five baby orangutans rescued from a forest in Odisha two months ago, state Forest Minister Ganesh Ram Singh Khuntia said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

Speaking to reporters, Mr. Khuntia said all five orangutans were doing well , and expressed the State's desire to retain them at Nandankanan Zoological Park.

"All five baby orangutans are doing well and growing. No one should disturb them. We want them to stay in Odisha, and visitors will get an opportunity to see them at Nandankanan Zoo," he said.

The Minister said some countries might stake a claim to the animals under international wildlife trade regulations, but they would have to furnish concrete evidence to establish that the rescued animals originated from their territory.

"The Indonesian government has raised its claim as a routine matter. We will seek evidence to establish that the orangutans originated from their country. If they provide the proof, the animals may be handed over to them," Mr. Khuntia said.

He added that the State government had submitted details of the rescued animals to the Centre for necessary action.

"Odisha has a conducive environment for orangutans. So, we want them to stay here," he said.

The five baby orangutans were rescued from Bichitrapur forest in Balasore district on September 8 and subsequently shifted to Nandankanan Zoo, where they have been kept in quarantine.

Officials said the animals were housed in a temperature-controlled room and were gradually acclimatising to the local environment.

The State government has made arrangements for their comfort and to help them overcome stress. The animals have displayed a range of emotions, from playful behaviour and brief mood swings to anxiously clinging to one another, they said.

articles.title: H.D. Kumaraswamy alleges Hassan DC retained her post by paying bribe to district in-charge Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Hassan Deputy Commissioner K.S. Latha Kumari has denied the allegations made against her, saying she has never done anything illegal

Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel H.D. Kumaraswamy has alleged that the Hassan Deputy Commissioner retained her post by paying ₹75 lakh to Excise Minister K.M. Shivalinge Gowda, who is also the in-charge Minister of Hassan district.

Speaking to presspersons in Hassan after visiting the historic Hasanamba temple in Hassan on Sunday (November 8, 2026), Mr. Kumaraswamy read out excerpts from a written script of what he described as a WhatsApp conversation between an unidentified person and Shashikiran, the personal assistant to the Hassan Deputy Commissioner. He said he received the contents of the conversation from an official who met him the previous night.

According to Mr. Kumaraswamy, the conversation was about seeking permission for three stone crushers. The personal assistant allegedly demanded ₹60 lakh to get the clearance. As the person on the other end bargained, Mr. Shashikiran is said to have listed the people with whom the amount had to be shared.

Mr. Kumaraswamy said the conversation also mentioned that Mr. Shivalinge Gowda wanted to transfer the incumbent Deputy Commissioner from Hassan. However, she allegedly managed to convince the Minister by paying ₹75 lakh through Arsikere Tahsildar Santosh.
The script of the purported conversation was also distributed to journalists. Mr. Kumaraswamy said it also referred to the Hassan MP and several officials of the district.
He demanded an investigation into the allegations and urged the police to seize the mobile phone from the person concerned for further examination.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, who also visited the temple the same day, said the Deputy Commissioner had been doing a good job. “However, allegations are being made against her because she did not yield to their demands,” he said.

Hassan Deputy Commissioner K.S. Latha Kumari has denied the allegations made against her, saying she has never done anything illegal. “I have not done anything wrong, I am not doing anything wrong, and I will never do anything wrong,” she said.

Ms. Kumari said that if any wrong message had been sent by her personal assistant or anyone in his section, proper action would be taken. She condemned the circulation of “false and baseless information”. “Let there be an inquiry. Those who have erred should face action,” she said.
She said a complaint would be filed with the cyber police, as spreading false information was a crime. “We will bring out the truth,” she added.

articles.title: ‘Dimagi Naxals’ instigating people against Constitution and democracy: PM Modi as Maoists eliminated
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Celebrating Diwali with CRPF personnel in Bastar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the country must “identify and defeat” ideological supporters of Naxalism who have “infiltrated” parties and organisations

Targeting political opponents, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday (November 8, 2026) said armed Maoists had been eliminated, but “dimagi Naxals” (ideological supporters) had infiltrated several political parties and organisations and were instigating people against the Constitution and democracy.

“We must identify and defeat such elements and secure the country,” Mr. Modi said, while celebrating Deepavali with security personnel at a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) camp in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, continuing his tradition of spending the festival with the men and women in uniform. The government declared the country free of Naxalism on March 31, 2026.

“Amid the successes, we must remember one more thing. Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not over yet. Armed Naxalites have disappeared from the forests, but ‘dimagi Naxals’ have taken control of several organisations,” he said.

“Even today, they are instigating people against the country’s Constitution and democracy. They have infiltrated several political parties and different organisations. We must identify and defeat them and secure the country,” he added. The government, he said, took decisions that “dealt very big blows to the funding of Naxals and secessionists”.

On Independence Day in August 2026, Mr. Modi had also referred to “dimagi Naxals”, saying the country had succeeded in removing armed Naxalism but its ideological supporters were seeking opportunities to promote violence.

Recalling the fight against Naxalism in Bastar, Mr. Modi said it had not been easy, as at one point over 230 districts across nearly 20 States were affected by Left-Wing Extremism. After sunset, life would come to a standstill, thousands of villages and crores of people were affected, and there were around 2,000 Naxalite attacks annually, he said.

“This land had become soaked in the blood of our brave personnel, but not a single sigh of grief was heard from any of the ‘naamdaar’ (powerful people) living in palaces. Not a single tear rolled down their eyes. Such attacks continued to take place somewhere or the other almost every day,” he said, targeting previous governments. Between 2004 and 2013, more security personnel were killed every year than the number of Naxalites eliminated, he said.

“Unfortunately, the governments of that time treated Naxalism as an incurable disease and left it unaddressed. No country can function with such an approach towards its enemies... The lack of political will that the country faced was addressed in 2014, when you gave this Pradhan Sevak the opportunity to serve Mother India,” he said.

The morale of security forces began changing after 2014, Mr. Modi said, adding that for the first time in 47 years, not a single CRPF personnel lost his life while on duty over the past year. “This is a victory of the country’s right policies and strong political will. This is a victory of your valour, courage and restraint,” he said.

articles.title: U.S. launches task force to disrupt land transit routes into Iran
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The restrictions would expand on a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports during the two countries' eight-month war, in which Tehran has also restricted passage through the critical Strait of Hormuz trade route, choking global energy supplies
The U.S. military has announced it will create a 20-member task force to find ways to disrupt land routes into Iran that it says are used for shipments of weapons and illicit materials.

The restrictions would expand on a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports during the two countries' eight-month war, in which Tehran has also restricted passage through the critical Strait of Hormuz trade route, choking global energy supplies.

The task force's work "will further constrain Iran's ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military," U.S. Central Command chief Brad Cooper said in a statement posted on X on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

The team of both civilian and military personnel based in Florida would coordinate with U.S. government agencies on "preventing the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and illegal revenue streams across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea," the statement added.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said Washington's latest bid "will fail" and will not bring about economic collapse in the Islamic republic.

"The United States will never be able to impose the economic blockade it is pursuing and proposing under various names and through different plans," Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebi said, according to Fars news agency.
"The Americans will not achieve their objective of exerting extreme economic pressure to bring about the collapse and disintegration of Iran's economy."
Mr. Mohebi added that the United States would be "powerless to block" communication channels between Iran and neighbouring countries.
CENTCOM said that the naval blockade on Iranian ports had "prevented Iran from exporting more than $25 billion in crude oil."
In August, Washington announced what it called an "economic asphyxiation" campaign on Iran aimed at strangling its already battered economy.

Poland began two days of national mourning on Sunday (November 8, 2026) ‌and police bolstered security after six people were killed in a mass ​shooting in Krakow that authorities said was likely inspired by far-right ideology.

Saturday’s ⁠(November 7) attack in the city’s historic main square shocked a country that has prided itself on being safer than many of its Western European neighbours, deepening public concern following a string of school stabbings ‌in October that officials linked to extremist content online.
Seventeen people, including two police officers and the gunman, were wounded in the attack, authorities said.

articles.title: PM Modi desperate, 'jhola-picking-up time' fast approaching: Congress
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh said the Prime Minister has not spared the nation even on Deepavali day his "trademark abuse"

The Congress on Sunday (November 8, 2026) hit back at Prime Minister Narendra Modi after his "dimagi Naxals" (ideological supporters) jibe at political rivals, saying he is clearly distraught, disturbed and desperate, and his " jhola -picking-up time" is fast approaching.

The opposition party's dig came after Mr. Modi targeted political opponents, saying armed Maoists have been eliminated, but "dimagi Naxals" have infiltrated several political parties and organisations and are instigating people against the Constitution and democracy.

"We must identify and defeat such elements and secure the country," Modi said, while celebrating Deepavali with security personnel at a CRPF camp in Chhattisgarh's Bastar, continuing his tradition of spending the festival with India's brave men and women in uniform.

Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh said the Prime Minister has not spared the nation even on Deepavali day his "trademark abuse". "He has once again spoken of what he calls 'dimagi naxals'. He has used a very solemn non-political occasion, donned the uniform of the security forces, and hurled invectives at his political rivals," Mr. Ramesh said on X.
This is a brazen assault on all institutional norms but when has that ever stopped this man, he asked.

It was on April 28, 2024 that he had said that those demanding a caste census were urban naxals, and later on April 30, 2025, he announced that a caste census will be carried out as part of Census 2027, Mr. Ramesh said.

Earlier, in September 2020, he had called those agitating against the three black farm laws as supporters of a naxal ideology, and later, on November 19, 2021, he withdrew those very laws, the Congress leader pointed out.
"The PM is clearly distraught, disturbed and desperate. Jhola-picking-up time is fast approaching," Mr. Ramesh said.
In his remarks in Chhattisgarh's Bastar, Mr. Modi said the government took decisions that "dealt very big blows to the funding of Naxals and secessionists".
The Maoist terror elimination was a victory of the country's right policies and strong political will, said Modi, dressed in a military-style camouflage uniform and a hat.

articles.title: Democratic wins in State AG races give Trump a new headache
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Incoming Democratic attorneys general could halt ⁠cooperation with federal immigration operations, fortify abortion access and file multistate challenges against the Trump administration's environmental and gun policies

Democrats flipped attorney general offices in five Republican-leaning states in the midterm elections, dealing a significant blow to the ‌conservative legal movement and erecting a new line of resistance against President Donald Trump's agenda.

The victories in ​Texas, Ohio, Georgia, Iowa and Kansas threaten to disrupt conservative legal strategy. Incoming Democratic attorneys general could halt ⁠cooperation with federal immigration operations, fortify abortion access and file multistate challenges against the Trump administration's environmental and gun policies.
“The Texas AG’s office has been operating as the private law firm of the MAGA movement," Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson said in an interview. “No more.”

The shift reflects broader ‌voter pushback in the midterms, in which Democrats made gains nationwide. But the practical fallout may be felt most immediately in State capitals, where attorneys general direct law enforcement priorities, issue legal guidance and challenge federal mandates.

"The ‌Republican state AG offices are the tip of the spear of the conservative legal movement," said Mike Davis, ‌an influential ⁠conservative lawyer. "Losing these offices is a major setback for key conservative causes."

Over the past decade, Republican attorneys general have advanced conservative causes by challenging federal regulations, restricting gender-affirming care, curbing diversity initiatives and ​expanding gun access.
The Texas office, in particular, served ‌as a command centre for conservative legal challenges, leveraging its resources and elite staff to sue Democratic administrations.

Mr. Johnson said he plans a review of initiatives launched by his predecessor, Ken Paxton, including legal actions targeting out-of-state abortion providers, claims linking over-the-counter medications to autism, and lawsuits challenging vaccine efficacy.
He’s also critical of the State’s current partnership with U.S. Immigration and Customs ‌Enforcement (ICE) and plans to review whether it should continue.

“The Texas attorney general office was never conceived to ​be an extension of federal immigration enforcement,” he said. “And to the extent that they were detracting from the proper function of this office, we’re going to have a change of plans.”

articles.title: NGT issues notice to Tirunelveli Collector over threats to Tamirabharani fish species
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: National Green Tribunal takes suo motu cognisance of The Hindu report

The Principal Bench of the National Green Tribunal (NGT), New Delhi, has issued notice to the Tirunelveli Collector and five others over threats faced by fish species in Tamirabharani River due to pollution and habitat loss.

Taking suo motu cognisance of a report, titled ‘Tamirabharani’s Endemic Fish Face Threats From Pollution, Habitat Loss’, published in The Hindu on September 28, the Bench, comprising Justice Arun Kumar Tyagi and expert members A. Senthil Vel and Afroz Ahamed, directed that the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board, the Central Pollution Control Board’s Regional Office in Chennai, Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment (ATREE), and Agasthyamalai Community Conservation Centre (ACCC) be impleaded as respondents, besides the Collector.

The order said: “The above news item attracts the provisions of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, and prima facie raises substantial questions relating to the environment arising out of the implementation of the enactments specified in Schedule I to the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.”
The Bench directed the Registry to list the matter before the Southern Bench of the Tribunal, Chennai, on January 22, 2027, as the cause of action had arisen within its territorial jurisdiction.

It also directed the respondents to file their responses before the Bench at least one day ahead of the date of hearing. The Hindu had reported that 125 fish species had been identified in upstream, midstream and lower estuarine stretches of the river. Seven of them are endemic to the Tamirabharani.

Pollution, habitat destruction, loss of riparian vegetation, invasive fish and aquatic plants, use of soaps and shampoos by people bathing in the river, rituals performed on its banks, dumping of puja materials and clothes, and discharge of untreated sewage have contributed to the decline in fish populations.

articles.title: Delhi records ‘very poor’ air quality on Diwali with 376 AQI
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jahangirpuri recorded the highest AQI at 450, followed by RK Puram at 448, according to the Sameer app.
Delhi’s air quality was in the ‘very poor’ category on Sunday (November 8, 2026), but set to worsen after Diwali celebrations in the evening.
The average Air Quality Index (AQI) for the day settled at 376 in the ‘very poor’ category as a thick layer of smog enveloped the city and reduced visibility.
The air quality is forecast to turn ‘severe’ on Monday (November 9, 2026) following Diwali celebrations, combined with vehicular emissions, as well as the peak stubble-burning season.

Of the 59 monitoring stations that recorded data on Sunday (November 8, 2026), air quality was in the ‘severe’ category at 12 and in the ‘very poor’ category at 22. The worst AQI was recorded in Jahangirpuri at 463.

The city’s average AQI increased from 369 on Saturday to 376 on Sunday, remaining not far from the ‘severe’ threshold of 400. Several monitoring stations have already breached this mark, indicating deterioration in air quality across the capital.
According to the Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS) for Delhi, the air quality is likely to remain in the ‘severe’ category from November 9 for a few days.
ALSO WATCH Delhi air pollution: GRAP stage 3 kicks in, vehicle ban and school curbs announced

As per the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), an AQI between 0 and 50 is classified as ‘good’, 51 and 100 as ‘satisfactory’, 101 and 200 as ‘moderate’, 201 and 300 as ‘poor’, 301 and 400 as ‘very poor’, and 401 and 500 as ‘severe’.

Weather and air quality experts have attributed the anticipated deterioration to unfavourable meteorological conditions, the onset of Deepavali-related celebrations and vehicular emissions, along with the peak period of stubble burning in neighbouring states.

Unfavourable meteorological conditions are further aggravating the situation. According to the EWS, a ventilation index below 6,000 square metres per second, coupled with an average wind speed of less than 10 kilometres per hour, is unfavourable for the effective dispersion of pollutants.

articles.title: Revanth sets target of making one crore women millionaires by 2034
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Promises greater economic opportunities for SHG members; says women’s empowerment is central to his government’s policies

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy set a target of transforming one crore women into millionaires by 2034 by strengthening self-help groups (SHGs) and creating more opportunities for them in business and industry.

Interacting with women members of self-help groups at the Lagacharla Industrial Hub in Kodangal constituency on Sunday (November 8, 2026), he said nearly 70 lakh women were already members of SHGs and the government aimed to increase the membership to one crore by 2034 and make every member financially prosperous.

The Chief Minister, who celebrated his birthday with the women members of self-help groups, said he considered them his family and attributed his rise to the blessings and support of women. “I have received more from you than I ever asked for. I have nothing more to aspire for in life. My goal is to make one crore women millionaires,” he said.

Mr. Revanth Reddy said women were the backbone of families and that households prospered when women had control over financial decisions. His government was, therefore, making efforts to expand their role in economic activities and entrepreneurship.

He said women’s self-help groups had been entrusted with stitching school uniforms for students in government schools, while they were also being encouraged to operate petrol bunks, participate in solar power generation and run Indiramma canteens in the Secretariat and other government offices. Women were generating annual business worth ₹15 crore to ₹20 crore through some of these activities, he claimed.

The government had extended bank-linkage loans of ₹79,000 crore to women over the last 34 months, he said, complimenting Minister for Women and Child Welfare Danasari Anasuya (Seethakka) for her efforts in strengthening the SHG movement.

Referring to welfare measures, the Chief Minister said the government had sanctioned 4.5 lakh new pensions on Sunday (November 8), of which 3.5 lakh were for single women and widows. New pensions had also been sanctioned on a saturation basis for handloom and toddy-tapping workers, he added.

He said the Indiramma housing scheme and free electricity up to 200 units were providing support to women. Nearly 37 lakh women were travelling free on RTC buses every day, and the government was compensating the corporation for the scheme, helping it return to profitability.
Urging women to move beyond dependence on welfare schemes and become entrepreneurs and industrialists, he said the government would stand by them in their efforts to achieve economic independence.

He also called upon women to give priority to their children’s education, particularly higher education for girls. “The hardships you have faced should not be experienced by your children. Education alone can transform their lives,” he said, asking women to promise on his birthday that they would ensure higher education for their daughters.

articles.title: Poland calls Krakow shooting rampage 'terrorist' attack
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A British national was among the dead, according to police. Among the 15 wounded were nationals from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia, says an Interior Ministry spokeswoman

Poland on Sunday (November 88, 2026) launched a terrorism probe as mourners brought candles and flowers to Krakow's Main Market Square in tribute to six people killed by a gunman who authorities said was "fascinated by far-right ideologies".
The 24-year-old Polish man opened fire at random on Saturday (November 7) in the historic centre of the country's second city, in what Prime Minister Donald Tusk called an act of "terrorism".
A British national was among the dead, according to police. Among the 15 wounded were nationals from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia, an Interior Ministry spokeswoman said.
Three more bodies were found at the suspect's home in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, around 150 kilometres (95 miles) northeast of Krakow. Police said they were his parents and a sister.
The gunman was wounded in a shootout with police and is in critical condition in hospital. The National Prosecutor's Office said it had launched a terrorism investigation.
"I'm absolutely devastated," Weronika Filar, 27, a Krakow resident, told AFP on Sunday (November 8).
"It's one of the safest places on Earth genuinely... I did not expect anything like this to happen to us," she said. "Our city will never be the same."
"We've heard of various incidents of this sort happening elsewhere in Europe," Krzysztof Stepien, a 28-year-old part-time city guide told AFP.
"Nothing like this has ever happened here, and I hope it never will again," Stepien said.
Two police officers were wounded as they desperately chased the suspect, who was masked and dressed in military garb, including a bullet-proof vest.

articles.title: Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant relying on generators again after losing external power supply
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Zaporizhzhia, which produces no electricity but needs power supplied by two external links to keep nuclear fuel ‌cool, lost its off-site electricity supply after the Ferosplavna power line disconnected, the IAEA said

The Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in southeastern Ukraine ​has lost its external electricity supply and is again ‌using backup generators for reactor cooling, the plant's ​management and the UN's nuclear watchdog said ⁠on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

Zaporizhzhia, which produces no electricity but needs power supplied by two external links to keep nuclear fuel ‌cool, lost its off-site electricity supply after the Ferosplavna power line disconnected, the International Atomic ‌Energy Agency (IAEA) said.

"The cause and location ‌of ⁠the latest disconnection are not yet known," ⁠the IAEA said in an X post, adding that the plant currently has sufficient fuel reserves to operate a limited number ​of emergency diesel ‌generators for about two weeks.
The IAEA said on October 23 that the main Dniprovska power line remained unavailable.
In early September, a local ceasefire ‌brokered by the IAEA took effect to ​allow repairs to restore external power to Zaporizhzhia, which at that time had been ⁠without it since August 20.
Russia seized the nuclear plant, Europe's largest with six reactors, in the first ‌weeks of the war that began with Moscow's February 2022 invasion of its smaller neighbour.
Moscow and Kyiv have since regularly accused each other of military action that compromises nuclear safety.
The plant's Russian-installed management said the Ferosplavna line had been shut ‌down by "automatic protection", adding that radiation levels on the ​site and in the surveillance zone were normal.

"Staff at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant ⁠are monitoring all operational parameters of the equipment. All necessary ⁠measures to maintain the safe condition of the power units are being taken in ‌full," the plant's management said in a statement posted on the MAX messenger app.

articles.title: Rajajinagar murders: Two more bodies recovered near Chamundi hills in Mysuru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: With this development, five bodies have been traced so far in the case, while the search for the remaining two continues

In a fresh development in the brutal murder of seven members of a family, Rajajinagar Police have recovered two more bodies, suspected to be those of Shivakumar and his wife Divya — the accused Indushekhar’s brother-in-law and sister-in-law — near the foothills of Chamundi Hills in Mysuru, on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
Police conducted a spot mahazar of the spot with the accused while recovering the bodies.
With this development, five bodies have been traced so far in the case, while the search for the remaining two continues.

DCP, North Division said that two more dead bodies found near Chamundi hill forest area are said to be of Shivakumar and Divya. Another special police team has been deployed to Shiradi Ghat, where it is conducting searches for the two more missing bodies, he said.

On Saturday (November 7, 2026), police recovered the bodies of the accused’s wife, Sunita, and mother-in-law, Rupavathi, from a forest area in Salem, Tamil Nadu. The body of a young boy was earlier recovered near the foothills of Nandi Hills and has already been cremated.

According to the investigation, Indushekhar allegedly murdered seven of his relatives, including his wife, over a period of 15 days. He is suspected to have packed the bodies in gunny bags, transported them in his car and dumped them at different locations, including the foothills of Nandi Hills, a forest area in Salem, the foothills of Chamundi Hills and Shiradi Ghat.

The accused, who is currently in police custody, is being subjected to intensive interrogation as investigators try to establish the sequence of murders, the motive and the locations where the remaining bodies were disposed of.

The accused, who is currently in police custody, is being subjected to intensive interrogation as investigators try to establish the sequence of murders, the motive and the locations where the remaining bodies were disposed of.

articles.title: UK Hindu family takes legal action after school objects to boy wearing tilak
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The parents of a nine-year-old boy have approached the UK High Court, alleging religious discrimination after he was prevented from wearing the sacred Tilak-Chandlo to school

The parents of a nine-year-old British Hindu boy, who was withdrawn from his primary school in London after it objected to him wearing a tilak on his forehead, have initiated legal proceedings in the UK High Court.

The boy, who belongs to the Swaminarayan faith tradition, had attended Vicar’s Green Primary School in west London since 2021 and worn his religious marking, known as the Tilak-Chandlo, without difficulty.
However, the school objected to the practice in late 2025, triggering a dispute that eventually led his parents to withdraw him from the school and pursue legal action.
“As parents, it has been heartbreaking to see our son go through this simply because he wanted to practise his faith,” the parents said in a statement released by their legal team this weekend.
“He had worn his Tilak-Chandlo to school for years without difficulty, and we never imagined that something so sacred to our family would become a source of distress,” they said.
“Our son was just an ordinary little boy who enjoyed learning and spending time with his friends. His religious marking did not hurt anyone or prevent him from being a good pupil.

“We have always taught our children to respect every religion, and we simply ask that the same respect be shown to ours. We hope that no other child will have to choose between their education and their faith,” they added.
The family is represented by Ashray Law, which has filed proceedings alleging religious discrimination under the UK’s Equality Act 2010 and breaches of rights protected by the Human Rights Act 1998.
The case, filed in the High Court of England and Wales, seeks £25,000 in damages. The proceedings are ongoing, and the allegations remain in dispute.
“This case goes beyond one child or one school. It raises important questions about religious freedom and equality in British education,” said Ambrish Limbachia, director of Ashray Law.

articles.title: Jean Drèze urges T.N. govt. to take strict action amid report of ‘fake book’ at Kalaignar Centenary Library
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: “It is important to stem the rot before it spreads, all the more so if this book was AI-generated,” the economist said in a clarification via e-mail to The Hindu
Economist Jean Drèze on Sunday (November 8, 2026) said an English-language book attributed to him as the author and allegedly found in some public libraries of Tamil Nadu is “fake”.

The confirmation comes following a media report alleging that a title listed in Madurai’s Kalaignar Centenary Library may not have been authored by Mr. Drèze. The book which lists him as the author was identified as the title ‘ Democracy and Peoples Right in the Contemporary World’’.

“I am foxed and baffled to read on social media that a book called Democracy and Peoples Right in the Contemporary World, attributed to me, has surfaced in some public libraries of Tamil Nadu. If this book exists under my name, it must be fake, because I have never authored such a book,” he wrote in a clarification issued to The Hindu via e-mail.

Mr. Drèze urged the Tamil Nadu government to take “strict and swift action against the publishers of this fake book and other culprits”. “It is important to stem the rot before it spreads, all the more so if this book was AI-generated,” he added.

The economist also raised questions on procurement checks in place at public libraries and said: “The issue is not just that a fake book was printed but also how it was procured by a public library. Surely it would have taken little effort to ascertain the authenticity of this book.”

According to the media report, the book in question was allegedly procured from Phoenix Publishers and carries a valid International Standard Book Number. It also further alleged that the address of Phoenix Publishers is the same as that of Akal Vilakku Publishers.

The procurement date cited in the report is June 25, 2023 before the inauguration of the library. Madurai’s Kalaignar Centenary Library was inaugurated on July 15, 2023, by the then Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin.

articles.title: Minister Agnimitra Paul says rose water to be used for mist spraying in Kolkata; environmentalist slams move

fullParagraphs: West Bengal Minister Agnimitra Paul says rose water will be mixed into mist spraying on special occasions, while environmentalist Somendra Mohan Ghosh says the city’s air needs cleaning at the source

West Bengal Municipal Affairs and Urban Development Minister Agnimitra Paul has said that, on special occasions, rose water will be mixed with the water normally used for mist spraying to control air pollution in the city.
The move drew criticism from an environmentalist, who argued that the city’s air needed to be cleaned at the source rather than through such cosmetic interventions.

The initiative is helping reduce the concentration of dust particles in the air and keep AQI levels somewhat under control, she said.

articles.title: West Bengal to institute 'Seema Mitra' award for BSF, SSB, police personnel from 2027: Suvendu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A selection committee would be constituted to decide the awardees, he said, while addressing BSF personnel at a border outpost in Hingalganj in North 24 Parganas district, which shares a boundary with Bangladesh

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday (November 8, 2026) announced that his government would institute the 'Seema Mitra' award from 2027 to recognise exceptional contributions by BSF, SSB, and state police personnel in securing the country's borders.

A selection committee would be constituted to decide the awardees, he said, while addressing BSF personnel at a border outpost in Hingalganj in North 24 Parganas district, which shares a boundary with Bangladesh.
"We will give the 'Seema Mitra' award from next year for BSF, SSB and West Bengal police personnel," Mr. Adhikari said.
The Chief Minister visited the border outpost to greet security personnel on the occasion of Diwali and Kali Puja.
The BSF guards the India-Bangladesh border, while the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) is deployed along the country's frontiers with Nepal and Bhutan.
Mr. Adhikari apologised to the BSF and CRPF personnel for what he described as derogatory remarks and behaviour by the previous State government.

"I, as the Chief Minister of the State, apologise to you for the derogatory remarks and behaviour of the previous regime towards BSF and CRPF," he said, targeting the erstwhile Trinamool Congress government.
He alleged that the previous Mamata Banerjee government had failed to provide the required land to the BSF for fencing nearly 600 km of the India-Bangladesh border in West Bengal.
Mr. Adhikari said the BJP government had handed over the required land to the BSF soon after assuming office and would provide any additional land needed for border fencing.
He said that his government will provide any additional requirement of land by the BSF in the border areas.

articles.title: Turkey, Azerbaijan leaders vow unity after tensions
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Turkic-speaking allies describe their relationship as "one nation, two states" and, despite the friction, remain closely bound by military and energy ties

Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev vowed on Sunday (November 8, 2026) that their countries' alliance would remain solid, in a show of unity aimed at overcoming a public rift between the close neighbours.
Tensions flared in September, when Baku revised school uniform regulations to prohibit clothing deemed incompatible with secular education, effectively barring Islamic headscarves in classrooms.
Mr. Erdogan's government has dismantled restrictions on hijabs in Turkey.

Azerbaijan's move sparked protests at home and drew criticism from Mr. Erdogan's Islamist-rooted Justice and Development Party (AKP). Presidential adviser Oktay Saral demanded that Azerbaijan reverse the restrictions.
Baku also declared 31 Turkish nationals, including an Opposition lawmaker and party leaders, persona non grata over critical social media posts.

Mr. Erdogan subsequently dismissed Mr. Saral, but Mr. Aliyev stayed away from an October 30 summit of Turkic leaders in Ankara — despite a personal invitation from Mr. Erdogan. Instead, he sent Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov.

On Sunday (November 8, 2026), as Azerbaijan marked Victory Day commemorating a 2020 war with Armenia, Mr. Erdogan arrived in the country's Fuzuli district, which Baku recaptured from Armenian forces six years ago.
A guard of honour lined up at the airport, where Mr. Aliyev and First Lady Mehriban Aliyeva, welcomed Mr. Erdogan and his wife Ms. Emine.
"With the permission of Almighty God, our unity will endure forever," Mr. Erdogan told a joint press conference with Mr. Aliyev.
"This unity of hearts, which we describe with the motto 'One Nation, Two States,' is an everlasting torch that draws strength from our shared past and illuminates our future."

The Turkic-speaking allies describe their relationship as "one nation, two states" and, despite the friction, remain closely bound by military and energy ties

Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev vowed on Sunday (November 8, 2026) that their countries' alliance would remain solid, in a show of unity aimed at overcoming a public rift between the close neighbours.

Tensions flared in September, when Baku revised school uniform regulations to prohibit clothing deemed incompatible with secular education, effectively barring Islamic headscarves in classrooms.

Mr. Erdogan's government has dismantled restrictions on hijabs in Turkey.

Azerbaijan's move sparked protests at home and drew criticism from Mr. Erdogan's Islamist-rooted Justice and Development Party (AKP). Presidential adviser Oktay Saral demanded that Azerbaijan reverse the restrictions.

Baku also declared 31 Turkish nationals, including an Opposition lawmaker and party leaders, persona non grata over critical social media posts.

Mr. Erdogan subsequently dismissed Mr. Saral, but Mr. Aliyev stayed away from an October 30 summit of Turkic leaders in Ankara — despite a personal invitation from Mr. Erdogan. Instead, he sent Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov.

On Sunday (November 8, 2026), as Azerbaijan marked Victory Day commemorating a 2020 war with Armenia, Mr. Erdogan arrived in the country's Fuzuli district, which Baku recaptured from Armenian forces six years ago.

A guard of honour lined up at the airport, where Mr. Aliyev and First Lady Mehriban Aliyeva, welcomed Mr. Erdogan and his wife Ms. Emine.

"With the permission of Almighty God, our unity will endure forever," Mr. Erdogan told a joint press conference with Mr. Aliyev.

"This unity of hearts, which we describe with the motto 'One Nation, Two States,' is an everlasting torch that draws strength from our shared past and illuminates our future."
