articles.title: 23 dead in clashes between South Sudan government, opposition forces
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Fighting in the Ruweng administrative area has left 23 dead and thousands displaced, officials said, as South Sudan heads towards elections on December 22

Four weeks of clashes between South Sudan government and opposition forces in the north of the impoverished country have left 23 people dead while thousands have fled the conflict zone, authorities and police said Sunday.

Hundreds of people have died in clashes across South Sudan in recent weeks between forces loyal to President Salva Kiir and those of detained former vice president Riek Machar and other ethnic unrest, as the world's youngest country heads towards national elections scheduled for December 22.
Ruweng administrative area's information minister Tony Chol Ayat told AFP that fighters from Riek Machar's SPLA-IO force had entered Ruweng from neighbouring Unity state.
He said fighting between October 4 and Thursday this week had left 23 dead and 17 wounded. The toll was confirmed by two police sources.
Chol Ayat said that more than 100,000 people had fled the fighting while one of the police sources confirmed "thousands" had left the area.
A resident in Ruweng told AFP that SPLA-IO fighters had started fighting and that "the government built up forces on the front lines and the rebel armies were repelled".
Another Ruweng resident said there were fears of heightened conflict. Both spoke on condition of anonymity.
A South Sudan army spokesman would not comment on events, while Riek Machar's forces did not respond to an AFP query.

Independent since 2011, South Sudan is one of the world's poorest countries with widespread corruption. Saalva Kiir and Riek Machar's forces fought a civil war from 2013 to 2018 that left more than 400,000 dead.

The country's first presidential and legislative election has already been postponed several times and a UN human rights commission, which has accused the country's elite of siphoning off billions of dollars of oil revenues, has said an election in current tensions could unleash widespread new conflict.

articles.title: Europe will be represented at U.S.-mediated Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi: France
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Although Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has made it clear that he wants involvement from European allies in the process, Russia has suggested there would be no place for European representatives at the table
Europe will be represented at the upcoming U.S.-mediated talks with Moscow and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending the Ukraine war, France said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
"The Europeans will be represented and France will be in Abu Dhabi to participate in these talks," French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot told RTL radio .
His comment came after President Donald Trump stoked fears of a U.S. pivot toward the Kremlin by predicting a "very big" deal with Russia involving not only the Ukraine war but "all of Europe".

Up to now, the talks scheduled for Tuesday (November 10, 2026) and Wednesday (November 11, 2026) had been framed as a trilateral format at the level of officials, not leaders, from Ukraine, Russia and the United States.
The identities of who would take part have not been made public.

Although Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has made it clear that he wants involvement from European allies in the process, Russia has suggested there would be no place for European representatives at the table.
Mr. Barrot said that, in the past, "there have been discussions, sometimes without the Europeans and sometimes with," but "this time they will participate".
He said, "France will be there and will ensure that Europe's voice is heard."
On Thursday (November 5, 2026), U.S., European, Ukrainian and NATO officials met in Brussels ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks.
A NATO spokeswoman said they "sought to advance a just and sustainable end to the war in Ukraine".

articles.title: Habitual offender arrested for murdering 65-year-old woman in Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kengeri police have arrested a habitual offender for allegedly murdering a 65-year-old woman who was sleeping outside a temple and robbing her of cash and a gold ring in Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout.
The deceased, Narayanamma, was found dead in front of the Pataladamma Temple at Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout, Konasandra, within Kengeri police station limits, on November 3.
According to the police, Narayanamma had left her house due to family problems and had been sleeping outside the temple for the past few days.
A local resident who noticed her body informed her son, who arrived at the spot and identified her. The Kengeri police initially registered an unnatural death report based on his complaint.

However, following the post-mortem examination and information gathered during the investigation, police suspected that she had been murdered and robbed. A murder case was subsequently registered on Thursday.
During the investigation, police apprehended a suspicious person moving around Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout on Friday. During interrogation, he allegedly confessed to the crime.
The accused reportedly told investigators that he had noticed Narayanamma sleeping alone and decided to rob her to arrange money to fund his vices.
In the early hours of November 3, he allegedly went to the spot, covered her mouth, assaulted her and robbed her of the cash she was carrying and a gold ring before fleeing, leaving her dead.

Police said the accused has a criminal history and was previously involved in cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and robbery cases at Girinagar and Cottonpet police stations.
Further investigation and interrogation are under way, police said.

articles.title: P.T. Usha complains to IOA electoral officer over WhatsApp campaign for SOM polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Indian Olympic Association president alleged former archer Dola Banerjee violated the Model Code of Conduct by circulating a WhatsApp message seeking votes for four candidates ahead of Monday’s election

Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president P.T. Usha has lodged a complaint with the Electoral Officer alleging that former archer Dola Banerjee violated the Model Code of Conduct by circulating a WhatsApp message soliciting votes for a panel of four candidates in Monday’s (November 9, 2026) Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) elections.

In her complaint, Usha objected to a WhatsApp message circulated through an account bearing Banerjee’s name, seeking support for the ‘New Bharat Panel’ and asking voters to elect four named candidates, along with their ballot serial numbers and roll numbers.

Usha cited Clause 1.9 of the Model Code of Conduct, issued on October 30, 2026, which states that the promotion of a candidate shall exclude any form of publicity, including the use of new media or social networks. She contended that the circulation of the message amounted to targeted solicitation of votes through social media, and appeared to fall within the ambit of the clause. The complaint also referred to Clauses 1.2 and 1.3, which require candidates to conduct their campaigns fairly, with dignity and moderation, and to show due respect to other candidates.

Usha has urged the election authorities to examine the communication, establish the circumstances under which it was created and circulated, and seek an explanation from the persons concerned. She has also sought appropriate action under the applicable election rules if a violation is established, along with directions to ensure a level playing field for all candidates.

With polling scheduled from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on November 9, 2026, Usha has sought urgent intervention and a decision before voting begins. A screenshot of the WhatsApp message and a copy of the Model Code of Conduct were enclosed with the complaint.

articles.title: Revanth celebrates Deepavali with Indiramma house beneficiary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ministers, MLAs asked to spend festival with poor families who received houses; 2.21 lakh houses completed under scheme

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy along with Ministers and MLA celebrated Deepavali with a beneficiary of the Indiramma housing scheme at Parsapur village in Kodangal mandal on Sunday (November 8, 2026), in an initiative aimed at highlighting the government’s flagship housing programme for poor families.

The Chief Minister inaugurated the newly constructed house of Goripalli Sumitra and Srinivas, presented new clothes to the family, and had a traditional Deepavali meal of fine rice at their residence. Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar and Ministers Seethakka, Jupally Krishna Rao, Damodar Rajanarasimha and other public representatives joined the family for lunch.

The programme, titled ‘Maa Indiramma Intlo Deepavali’ (Deepavali in Our Indiramma Home), was conceived by Mr. Revanth Reddy to take the government’s housing initiative to the people and celebrate the festival with families who were allotted the houses.

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and his Cabinet colleagues have lunch at the residence of a Indiramma house beneficiary in Kodangal constituency on November 8, 2026. Photo credit: Special Arrangement.

He had asked Ministers, MLAs and other elected representatives to spend Deepavali with beneficiaries of the scheme in their respective constituencies. The idea was to make the festival a celebration with poor families who had received permanent homes through government assistance, rather than confining the programme to official celebrations.

Later, the Chief Minister also inaugurated a science museum at Kosgi, a primary health centre at Balampet, police stations at Dudyala and Kodangal, a high school and junior college at Hakimpet and a new government junior college building at Doulatabad, all in the Kodangal constituency represented by him.

The Indiramma Housing scheme is the flagship scheme of the Revanth Reddy government. The latest figures announced by Housing Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy recently revealed that around 2.21 lakh Indiramma houses had been completed across the State. The government has sanctioned 4.5 lakh houses in the first phase and another 2.5 lakh in the second phase. It has also taken up plans to construct one lakh houses in the Hyderabad urban region.

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and his Cabinet colleagues present new clothes to a family of Indiramma house beneficiary in Kodangal constituency on November 8, 2026 as a part of Deepavali celebrations. Photo credit: Special Arrangement
The beneficiaries are picked up in an open lot without any interference of political leader, and the programmes are held in open spaces in the presence of all those who applied for the scheme.

The State has committed around ₹40,000 crore towards the two phases and the proposed urban housing programme. Separately, official housing department data available in October showed that ₹7,634 crore had been released to beneficiaries towards construction assistance.

articles.title: Tens of thousands march in Amsterdam, pressing Dutch government on Gaza, Israel
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Organisers of the “Red Line” demonstration called for stricter trade sanctions, a halt to arms sales, and an official declaration that Israel’s actions in Gaza amount to genocide

Tens of thousands of people, many of them dressed in red, marched through Amsterdam on Sunday (November 8, 2026) in a mass demonstration aimed at pressing the Dutch government to take more decisive action against Israel over Gaza.

The organisers of the “Red Line” demonstrations in the Netherlands called for measures including stricter trade sanctions on Israel, officially declaring that Israel’s actions in Gaza amount to genocide, and halting all arms sales to Israel. The Dutch branch of Amnesty International, one of the organisers, said in an online post that more than 200,000 people joined the march.

“What is happening there is inhumane,” said Mike van Dongen, as he walked in the huge throng. He was critical of the Dutch government’s actions. “As far as I’m concerned, they are doing nothing,” he said. “They don’t dare take any serious steps.”

As the protesters marched along a normally busy Amsterdam street that was closed to traffic on Sunday, a man stood on a bus stop with a loudspeaker shouting “Free, free Palestine!” Many of the marchers echoed his cry as they passed.

Israel strongly rejects suggestions it is committing genocide in Gaza in its military campaign, which followed the attacks by Hamas-led militants in southern Israel on October 7, 2023. Militants killed about 1,200 people and took 251 hostages.

Israel’s retaliatory offensive has killed tens of thousands of Palestinians and destroyed much of Gaza. More than 1,550 Palestinians in Gaza have been killed by the Israeli military since a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas began in October 2025, according to the territory’s Health Ministry.
The ministry, part of the Hamas-run government, does not distinguish between civilians and militants, though it says women and children make up roughly half of the dead.

The campaign in Gaza has strained relations between the Netherlands and Israel. The Dutch Foreign Minister resigned last year after failing to secure new sanctions against Israel. Since then, a new minority coalition government has taken power and introduced an import ban on products from Israeli settlements, which the Dutch government and most of the international community consider illegal, a move that provoked a diplomatic spat with Israel.

Prime Minister Rob Jetten, who took part in a march last year but was not present on Sunday, defended his government’s actions at his weekly press conference on Friday (November 6, 2026). “Every single day and every single week, we do what we can to alleviate the terrible situation there,” he said.

He added that his administration was “exerting greater political and diplomatic pressure” on Israel to abide by its agreements on Gaza. At the same time, he said, the government was applying more pressure on Hamas and other organisations that continue to carry out “various operations that endanger the safety of ordinary Israelis.”

articles.title: Eisenkot warns of Israel crisis as he seeks to replace Netanyahu’s government
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: isenkot, 66, a political novice who has vowed to bridge Israel's deep polarisation under Netanyahu, formally received a mandate from President Isaac Herzog, giving him 28 days to form a government despite his bloc lacking a clear majority

Israel's former military chief Gadi Eisenkot started the tough task on Sunday (November 8, 2026) of forming a government , reaching out to Benjamin Netanyahu's allies as he warned the veteran Prime Minister had brought the country to a historic crisis.

Mr. Eisenkot, 66, a political novice who has vowed to bridge Israel's deep polarisation under Mr. Netanyahu, formally received a mandate from President Isaac Herzog, giving him 28 days to form a government despite his bloc lacking a clear majority.

"We are in a state of emergency, approaching a point of no return for the State of Israel," Mr. Eisenkot, who had traded his usual all black for a suit and tie, said at a ceremony at the Presidential office.
"We must form a national emergency government. This will require creative and unconventional political steps."

Mr. Eisenkot, born to a family of working-class Moroccan immigrants, would be the first Sephardic Prime Minister — a community mostly descended from West Asian or North African Jews — in a country long dominated by an Ashkenazi elite with ties to Europe.

Mr. Netanyahu is Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister, having led the country on and off for nearly two decades. He has taken the country in a sharply rightward direction and led wars in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran since the October 7, 2023, attacks by Hamas.
Both Mr. Eisenkot and Mr. Herzog acknowledged Israel's growing isolation under Mr. Netanyahu, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court.

In the United States, the most vital ally of Israel, Democrats on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) swept elections with calls to rein in Israel after the devastation in Gaza and the unpopular Iran war which Mr. Netanyahu launched with President Donald Trump.
"We are in the midst of a devastating diplomatic crisis. Even our closest friends and strategic allies are saying their relationship with Israel must be reassessed," Mr. Eisenkot said.
Mr. Eisenkot appealed to Mr. Netanyahu's Likud Party as well as the far-right party of Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich to join — but only with himself as Prime Minister.

articles.title: South Africa's ANC suffers worst election result as decline continues
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The once-dominant ANC — the party of Nelson Mandela — had received around 30% of the vote in Wednesday's (November 4, 2026) local government elections with 99% of ballots counted

South Africa's African National Congress party faced its worst election results ever on Sunday (November 8, 2026) and a new low point on its gradual decline in popularity as voters rebuked it for a failure to deliver basic services like water and electricity in towns and cities.

articles.title: Trump vows comeback as bitter showdown with Congress looms
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The devastating result leaves Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year 'lame duck' period of his White House tenure

U.S. President Donald Trump vowed a political comeback on Sunday (November 8, 2026) after his Republican Party lost control of both houses of Congress in midterm elections that amounted to an unequivocal repudiation of his turbulent Presidency.

The devastating result leaves Mr. Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year 'lame duck' period of his White House tenure, while opening the door to multiple investigations by the Democrat-controlled Congress into the President, his family and senior members of his administration.

"America took a giant step back in History with the results of the last Election," Mr. Trump said in a post on Truth Social, adding that the stock market that had grown during his tenure took a loss after the vote.
"But have no fear, we will be back, BIGGER AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!"
While the resounding election loss last Tuesday (November 3, 2026) has prompted soul-searching among Republican lawmakers, Mr. Trump has sounded defiant.
On Friday (November 6, 2026), he appointed hardline advisor Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, signalling a bare-knuckle fightback.
Democrats, meanwhile, have pledged to hold the Trump administration to account and fight against Mr. Miller, the architect of Mr. Trump's tough immigration policy.

Amid Democrat threats for administration officials to "lawyer up," Mr. Trump said on Saturday (November 8, 2026) he was ordering the Justice Department to examine Democratic threats to impeach members of his administration, likening it to "extortion."
That stance stoked a war of words between top Republicans and Democrats on U.S. political shows on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
Attorney General Todd Blanche, a former personal lawyer for Mr. Trump and now head of the Justice Department, vowed to actively defend Mr. Trump and senior members of his administration.

fullParagraphs: The Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS) has forecast that Delhi's air quality is likely to slip into the 'severe' category from November 9 and remain there for the subsequent few days

A smoky haze hung over Delhi on Deepavali night, blurring streetlights and blanketing neighbourhoods as celebrations intensified across the capital, pushing air quality at 20 monitoring stations into the ‘severe’ category, with the overall Air Quality Index standing at 371 at 10 p.m..

The haze grew denser as the evening progressed, with smoke from firecrackers hanging over roads and residential neighbourhoods. The smell of burnt crackers lingered in the air, while visibility dropped in several parts of the capital and residents reported difficulty breathing.

Despite restrictions on bursting firecrackers, several parts of Delhi continued to witness their use on Sunday evening (November 8, 2026), with reports of fireworks emerging from areas, including Pitampura, Burari, Mayur Vihar and parts of Lutyens’ Delhi.
Ahead of Deepavali, the Delhi government had appealed to people to comply with the Supreme Court’s directions on sale and use of green firecrackers.
The District Magistrate (East), in an order, had permitted the bursting of green firecrackers only on November 7 and 8, between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and 8 p.m. and 10 p.m..

Residents reported that firecrackers were being burst in outer Delhi’s Pitampura and Burari, with the intensity particularly high in Burari. dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Any regulation of crackers needs strict enforcement at all levels

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Editorial Context: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India must eliminate situations that lead to sewer cleaning deaths

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.
